Robert's will of '''9 October 1849''', B12<ref name="Evidence8bdc36c751">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S will of '''9 October 1849''', B12].</ref>, registered in 1856, gives one sixth each to brothers '''Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas''', one sixth to sister '''Mary''', and one sixth collectively to '''the children of brother James'''. ==== James's family: a promising identification with an unresolved title problem ====


Eliza Jane and Mary are explicitly sisters and daughters of '''James the Prescott carpenter'''. Identifying that James with Robert's brother is a strong property-based hypothesis, because both daughters convey interests in the same two parcels to Samuel. Together they exceed the '''one-sixth''' collective share given to James's children in Robert's will. Earlier ownership, additional inherited interests or a record error must be examined before treating these as a simple distribution of that sixth. The fractions cannot responsibly supply a child count.


The '''1868 Alexander deed has now been inspected'''. C114, 25 March 1868<ref name="Evidence1f5003a1e5">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQRC-Y C114, 25 March 1868].</ref>, DGS 008200420, image 120, pp.164–165, identifies '''Alexander Glasco of Rochester, Monroe County, New York, express agent, son of James Glasco formerly of Prescott, carpenter'''. The Canadian records now expand '''Daniel and Thomas's documented family''', which makes their brothers' and sister's records directly relevant to this enquiry. They still do not name Daniel or Thomas's parents, and they do not establish Alexander-951 as another brother. The Alexander-and-Rosanna tradition remains a hypothesis about Thomas's parents. ==== The Black branch and a possible witness at Robert's marriage ====

The original civil return for [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] and Jane Graham, 5 April 1866, records Robert's father as Alexander Glasgow, farmer, and names '''John Black''' as a witness. The return gives John no address or relationship. A plausible candidate is the John Black of Drumoolish who married Martha Savage on 13 March 1862, son of Robert Black, farmer; this remains a hypothesis, not a profile identification.

The 1862 marriage return<ref name="EvidenceBlackSavage1862">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/10945/5491449.pdf John Black–Martha Savage marriage return], page 178, entry 136, image 5491449.</ref> gives John as a full-age bachelor, farmer of Drumoolish, son of Robert Black; Martha was daughter of William Savage. Churchtown's baptism transcription records Elizabeth Black on 31 July 1845, daughter of '''Robert Black and Mary Glasgow''', resident Drumoolish<ref name="EvidenceBlackElizabeth1845">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/TamlaghtP/Baptisms.html Churchtown baptism transcription], page 7, entry 116.</ref>. This supplies a named parental couple for the Black branch and makes the deed-based John a specific person to investigate. It does not name Alexander's parents.

The 1831 Tamlaght O'Crilly census transcription lists Robert Black at Drumolish, house 57, with two males and one female, but the occupants are unnamed and other Black households occur in the same townland<ref name="EvidenceBlack1831">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census_2.html 1831 census transcription], row 643.</ref>. The newspaper's 20 December birth and the baptism transcription's nine-month age conflict; both remain reported rather than reconciled.

The 1866 witness fact is established, but identifying him with this John Black remains unproved. Shared congregation and local geography could explain contact without kinship. Even a confirmed identification would not prove that Alexander and Mary Glasgow belonged to the same parental couple. The Elizabeth and 1843 baptism images, Robert Black and Mary Glasgow's marriage, and further Churchtown witness occurrences are the next discriminating checks. The 1843 transcription's “Thomson Black” and illegible mother reading must not be changed to “Thomasina” or “Gear” without the original image.

==== 1892 New York probate citation: Nancy Glasgow's next of kin ====

The most informative parentage evidence located so far is not an Irish record but a legal notice published in New York. On 14 January 1892 the Clinton County Surrogate issued a citation on the petition of Hiram Walworth to prove the will of '''[[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]]''' of Plattsburgh, an unmarried Irish-born woman who had described herself in January 1889 as "about 68 years" old.<ref name="NancyWill1889">Clinton County, New York, Surrogate's Court, ''Records of wills, 1807–1902'', vol. Q, pp. 255–259, will of Nancy Glasgow of Plattsburgh dated 15 January 1889, admitted 9 May 1892; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYC4-66V?view=fullText FamilySearch image 159].</ref><ref name="NancyCitation1892">''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'' (Plattsburgh, New York), 26 February 1892, p. 6, legal notices, citation in the estate of Nancy Glasgow, deceased, dated 14 January 1892; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 New York State Historic Newspapers].</ref> The notice addresses heirs, next of kin and legatees. Its reference to both real and personal estate matters: the old restriction on collateral representation in personal property cannot by itself determine every relative's standing in this proceeding.<ref name="DeVoe1905">''Matter of De Voe'', 107 A.D. 245 (N.Y. App. Div. 1905), discussion of pre-1898 personal-property representation and the different treatment of real property; [https://law.justia.com/cases/new-york/appellate-division/1905/107-ad-245.html published judicial opinion]. This later case explains the distinction; it is not a decree concerning Nancy's family.</ref>

The citation names no brother or sister directly. It lists only children of named people: '''James G. Glasgow, Ann and Lizzie''', children of John Glasgow, late of "Baladonly" (Ballydonnelly, Rasharkin parish); '''James Glasgow, Mary and Ann''', children of Alexander Glasgow, formerly of Rasharkin; '''Mary Jane and Ann''', children of Robert Glasgow; the Dysart children of '''[[Glasglow-11|Jane (Glasgow) Dysart]]''' in Rasharkin, Ballymena, New Zealand and West Troy; '''David, James and Samuel Anderson of Gortahar''', identified through separate household records as sons of '''[[Glasgow-4071|Elizabeth (Glasgow) Anderson]]'''; and the unnamed children of '''Ann McClelland''' and '''Mary Thompson'''.<ref name="NancyCitation1892" /> Nancy's will independently calls Margaret (Dysart) Kennedy her niece and Robert Anderson her nephew,<ref name="NancyWill1889" /> and the Rasharkin Presbyterian register records both as children of Glasgow mothers — Jane Glascaw at Granagh and Betty Glascaw at Drumack.<ref name="Evidence5574dbd555" /> Together these records support a probable network of deceased sibling branches: John, Alexander, Robert, Jane, Elizabeth, Ann and Mary. Elizabeth is identified through the baptism and household records, not named as a parent in the notice. The list's completeness and each person's exact relationship remain to be checked in the underlying petition.

The Alexander of this citation is probably Alexander of Lisnagaver. His daughters' marriages of 1871 and 1876 each name Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver as father, his son James was baptised at Lisnagaver in 1843, and he died in May 1888 — "formerly of Rasharkin" in the citation's language. Nancy, born about 1820–21, was roughly ten years his junior: probable sisterhood fits these ages; daughterhood does not. He spent his last years at '''Gortahar''', where the citation places his sister Elizabeth's Anderson sons in 1892. His son [[Glasgow-938|Robert]] is not named. The proposed Scottish continuity and alleged survival to 1902 need original-record verification; this potential omission prevents treating completeness as already demonstrated.

The John of the citation is probably '''[[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow of Lisnagaver]]'''; Lizzie and the Ballydonnelly residence remain identity checks. His documented children were Ann (born 1848; married Bellingham in 1875, naming father John) and '''James Garvin Glasgow''' — the "James G." of the notice; the "Lizzie" of the notice is an otherwise unrecorded daughter (the Elizabeth Ann on the family memorial, died 1933, was James Garvin's widow).<ref name="Evidencef940c7acb4" /> A John Glasgow of Lisnagaver died on 24 June 1885 with son James as informant, which agrees with "late of".<ref name="JohnDeath1885">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death return, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw district, entry 2: John Glasgow, Lisnagaver, 24 June 1885; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1885/06280/4799372.pdf register image].</ref> John's original 1846 marriage return names his father as '''John Glasgow, farmer''', and the 1851 census makes Samuel Glasgow, born in County Londonderry about 1790, John's brother.<ref name="Evidencef940c7acb4" /> If Alexander and John shared a father, that father would be John Glasgow, farmer. Probable siblinghood alone does not distinguish a shared father from a shared mother or more complex half relationships.

The same document tells against the alternatives. '''[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]''' of Lisnagaver, whom earlier research treated as Alexander's possible brother, died in 1870 leaving children who were adults at Lisnagaver in the 1880s; had he been Nancy's brother they would have been her next of kin, yet none is cited while nieces in New Zealand are. This omission weighs against a simple reconstruction only if expected inclusion and completeness are established. It does not exclude Thomas or his proved brother [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel]] as Alexander's brothers or collateral relatives: Alexander could also share a parent with Thomas without Thomas being Nancy's sibling. The tradition naming [[Glasgow-3904|an older Alexander]] and Rosanna concerns Thomas; its extension to Alexander of Lisnagaver remains unproved. Likewise no member of the Glenleslie family of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] and Catherine, previously attached as Alexander's parents, appears among Nancy's next of kin; [[Glasgow-1049|Robert of Doonbought]]'s daughters were Catherine, Margaret, Maria, Netta and Jane, not the Mary Jane and Ann of the citation. The Robert of the citation is more likely the second Lisnagaver tithe occupier of 1834 — 35 acres entered immediately after Alexander's 29 — and perhaps the Robert Glasgow of Gortereghy in Griffith's Valuation who died in Ballymoney district in 1868 aged 71; his daughters have not yet been found.<ref name="Evidenceb707c32b1e" /><ref name="GriffithRasharkin">[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/rasharkin.htm Griffith's Valuation, Rasharkin parish], Glasgow occupiers at Lisnagaver (Alexander, John, Thomas), Gortereghy (Daniel, Robert) and Dromore (James).</ref><ref name="Evidenced078ae5073" />

The reconstructed family of John Glasgow, farmer, runs from Samuel (about 1790, County Londonderry) through Robert (about 1797), John (about 1801, County Antrim), Jane (about 1804), Alexander (about 1811), Elizabeth (by about 1816), Ann and Mary, to Nancy (about 1820–21) — a span that warrants checking estimated ages, identities and possible multiple unions; it does not establish two marriages of a particular parent. If these identities and a shared household are correct, their different birth counties suggest a possible movement from County Londonderry to Rasharkin parish; the John Glasgow recorded as a Desertoghill flax grower in 1796 ([[Glasgow-4090|Glasgow-4090]]) is a plausible but unproved identity for the father, and John of Lisnagaver later married a Desertoghill woman at Garvagh. No record yet names Alexander's father in his own right, and the citation cannot distinguish full from half siblings. The decisive record is Nancy's underlying Clinton County probate petition, which should state each cited person's relationship to her.

=== The Larne connection: a working family reconstruction ===

'''The Larne–Kilwaughter family is a priority origin hypothesis for Alexander's paternal line.''' The useful model connects an Irish branch with a branch that moved to South Carolina in the 1770s. [[Glasgow-2769|Robert of Tennessee]], born in South Carolina about 1790–94, is proposed as [[Glasgow-2738|James J's]] father. He is not proposed as the father of Alexander, Thomas or Daniel. There are two questions to solve together: which older Larne household supplied the Irish branch, and which man in that branch fathered Alexander. Identifying him with [[Glasgow-3905|Glasgow-3905]] means testing whether he was '''Adam of Inishrush's father''': 3905 represents that unidentified parental role, rather than a second man established by records. Its placeholder status neither supports nor disqualifies James.

==== Where the DNA and the wider catalogue narrow the search ====


The DNA evidence is positive family evidence. Alexander's established descendant line and James J's line share '''R-FT20271''', are three steps apart at Y-111 and share DYS714=27. Alongside James J's South Carolina origin and the documented Kilwaughter emigrant family, that makes the Larne connection worth pursuing ahead of an arbitrary same-surname pedigree. The American household evidence was not derived from the DNA, so their agreement is meaningful. But the proposed links from James J to Robert and Archibald are the very links being tested: they cannot also be counted as an independent proof that the match descends from Archibald.


There are already '''two additional historical comparison routes''' in the public project<ref name="Evidencedb3c53b8e9" />: a reported Robert-1143 line tested at Y-111, and a reported John-822 line tested at Y-67. They place the Larne and Inishrush questions within the same broader STR research network. Their public broad haplogroup labels do not yet establish either as FT20271-positive. Auditing those descent paths and obtaining resolved SNP states would test the proposed geographic connection more directly than treating all current FT20271 matches as interchangeable. John's omission of Alexander from his family Bible weakens '''John as Alexander's father''', not John as a collateral relative.


The proposed older Larne tree must also be tested. James-1509’s imported and live attachment is to [[Glasgow-1505|William-1505]], while the reviewed catalogue also carries a competing Hugh hypothesis. A William Glasgow, merchant of Larne, witnessed the 1760 lease; his identification with William-1505 needs checking against the other adult Williams. The derivative 1737 baptism names Hugh. [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh-1503's]] monument names a different adult son James, born about 1747/48. Both cannot casually be treated as the same child; identifying both as surviving sons of one Hugh would need explanation. William and Hugh's 1736 joint tenancy establishes association, while the proposed connections from them and Robert-1143 to [[Glasgow-1502|Robert-1502]] remain unproved. This is the unsettled joining generation, rather than a reason to disregard the well-supported branches below it.

'''The research can now be narrower:''' test Archibald's missing adult son in estate '''647'''; test the Larne household through William-3324's surviving '''1815 will, D300/1/5/49''', the '''1762 marriage''' and earlier Belfast records; identify Alexander's immediate family in '''CR5/32/1/1/1–2'''; and resolve the DNA placement of the specific Larne and Inishrush comparison lines. === How the evidence supports this account ===

The account separates the '''recorded event''', '''the identification of its people''', and '''the conclusion drawn from it'''. A baptism can directly name a child’s parents while leaving the child’s later identity unknown. A death can have an exact date while remaining a probable match to Alexander. These are different questions and should carry different qualifications.

==== What an unsuccessful search means ====


Missing evidence is useful only when we know what should have been recorded and what survives. The unnamed 1838 child’s absence from all relevant parts of the household return has more bearing on a survival hypothesis than an unrestricted web search finding nothing. It still cannot establish a death date by itself. A gap in the baptism transcription, a register starting after the marriage, and an archive image requiring onsite access are three different limitations.


The research history records completed searches and the wider register of inaccessible originals and unresolved identities; the focused next tests appear below. The next work is prioritised by the proposition it could resolve, not by the number of databases left to search. No numerical parent score is treated as a probability or allowed to replace these source-based arguments.

=== FamilySearch identity collision: Scottish and Rasharkin Alexanders ===

The authenticated FamilySearch Tree profile [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/G8WJ-HFW G8WJ-HFW] is internally conflated. Its source list contains Irish records for the Rasharkin Alexander, but its family panel also attaches a Scottish wife, Mary McCaughan (MQ57-B2Y), Scottish children and a Barony, Lanarkshire marriage. The archived discussion on this profile identifies the Scottish marriage as Alexander Glasgow and Mary Fleming on 12 June 1838 in Barony, Lanarkshire, with an 1841 Barony household headed by a flesher.

That Scottish couple is distinct from this profile's Rasharkin farmer: the latter's son James was baptized at Gortereagh on 9 February 1837, before the Scottish marriage, and Alexander appears with Mary and children at Lisnagaver in 1851. The Mary Fleming marriage is therefore not evidence against [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]]. The FamilySearch tree is useful for locating the conflict but is not proof of Mary's parents or of Alexander's parentage.

The dates are internally strained and no profile supplies a Rasharkin/Lisnagaver bridge, so this remains a separate comparison cluster rather than a proposed family for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

The later Moneyleck branch includes [[McCahon-44|Joseph McCahon]] (1867–1941), whose profile names Hugh McCahon and Mary Jane Wilson as parents, [[Wilson-71886|Hannah Wilson]] as wife and [[McCahon-18|Enos Archibald McCahon]] as a son. It links FamilySearch identity [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCJX-HRD MCJX-HRD]. Moneyleck is useful local network evidence but does not identify Mary's parents.

=== New pre-1790 Hearth Money evidence ===

The [https://adamsfamilydna.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/1669-Hearth-Money-Rolls-for-North-and-Mid-Antrim.pdf 1669 Hearth Money Rolls] list Ogan McCaghan at Kilcroagh, Armoy; Allex McCahan and John McCaghan at Ballyverdagh, Culfeightrin; Angus McCahir at Cross Denard, Culfeightrin; Gillindrish McCagher at Loughan/Ballyloghan, Culfeightrin; and Daniell McKaghin in Dunluce town. These direct household-head entries substantially pre-date the 1740 Rasharkin returns and establish a long-standing McCaughan-name presence in the wider Culfeightrin–Armoy region.

The rolls provide no ages, spouses or children and no bridge to Lisnagaver. They are therefore regional ancestral candidates and surname-network context only, not evidence that any named householder was a parent of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

The compiled Ballyverdagh/Culfeightrin account gives a secondary pedigree lead: John McCaughan (about 1724–1793), husband of Agnes McCahan, with children John (about 1754), Alexander (1756), Archibald (1758), Sarah (1760), Mary (1761) and Charles (1763). It says John was served heir to his father in 1771. The listed Mary McCaughan is chronologically possible but currently a poor candidate for Mary Glasgow's mother because she would have been about 50 in 1811 and no marriage, residence or child evidence links her to Rasharkin. The original heir, will and parish records remain to be checked.

Source: [https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm compiled Ballyverdagh/Culfeightrin McCaughan account], accessed 15 September 2026.

The same account reports a later James McCaughan, born about 1792, as a son of John McCaughan (born about 1754) of Ballyverdagh. This should not be silently merged with [[McCaughan-68|James McCaughan]], whose WikiTree profile gives birth before 1790, wife [[Larny-2|Mary Larny]] (about 1790), and son [[McCaughan-67|John]] (about 1798). On the current dates the two James profiles are chronologically incompatible, so the Ballyverdagh James is not a safe identification for the Canadian John line or for Mary's father.

=== FamilySearch Rasharkin/Ballydonnelly McCaughern cluster ===

FamilySearch's authenticated Tree gives a separate local cluster around [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/GWCJ-8BK James Mcaughern] (22 May 1842–13 December 1896, '''GWCJ-8BK'''), born at Ballydonnelly and christened at Rasharkin. His parents are [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LCRH-Z1G John McCaughern] (about 1813–1901) and [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LCRH-DL2 Elizabeth Hansen] (about 1813–1843), married in Rasharkin in 1834; listed children include [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/MZQT-2TK John McCaughern] (1835–1907) and James.

The same Tree connects [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/949C-MM6 James Mcaughern] (1830–1900) to [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L11Q-5KR James McCaughern] (about 1790–1858) and [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L119-DTP Nancy Marks] (about 1794–1859). The younger James married [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/KLP6-P27 Mary Jamison] at Finvoy on 9 March 1854 and had [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/949C-MMM James Mcaughern] (1868–).

This is significant local evidence but does not prove either James was [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] father. The about-1790 James is chronologically possible for a daughter born about 1811, but the displayed children begin with Daniel (1826), Thomas (1829), James (1830) and William (1842), with no Mary; the 1830 James is too young. Keep it as a distinct Rasharkin/Ballydonnelly branch pending the original 1834 marriage, 1842 baptism and records for the older James's children.

=== FamilySearch civil-marriage proof for the older James's children ===

The authenticated FamilySearch source list for [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L11Q-5KR James McCaughern] (about 1790–1858) contains two relationship-bearing indexed marriage records. The 27 November 1850 civil marriage of Daniel McAughern and Eleanor Graham records Daniel as age 24, estimated birth about 1826, and explicitly names '''James Mc Aughern as his father'''; the original place is Churchtown, Ballymoney. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGXX-H6G FamilySearch record FGXX-H6G]

The 9 March 1854 marriage of James McCaughern and Mary Jamison at Finvoy likewise explicitly names '''James McCaughern as the groom's father'''. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FG6V-QGF FamilySearch record FG6V-QGF]

These records materially strengthen the identification of the 1790–1858 James/Nancy household and document two sons, Daniel and James. They do not prove that this James was the 1834 Gortereghy tithe tenant or the father of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]: neither record names Mary, Glasgow, William McCaheran or Gortereghy.

=== Pre-1790 Rasharkin McCaharan graveyard root ===

The [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinCOI/graveyard.html Rasharkin Church of Ireland graveyard transcription] records '''Andrew McCaharan''', who died '''1 February 1738 aged 69''', and separately names his son '''John McCaharan''' on the same memorial. This is a direct local memorial and places the McCaharan spelling in Rasharkin more than a century before [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s estimated birth.

It is a new root cluster for the surname study, but not a proved ancestor line: the transcription gives no John's wife, townland, full death information or intervening generations. It strengthens the case for a long-established local surname population while leaving Mary's parentage unproved. The original stone image or burial/register material should be sought to recover the remainder of John's inscription.

=== New full 1803 Ballintoy McCaughan household audit ===

The complete [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf 1803 Ballintoy agricultural census] reveals several distinct early McCaughan households beyond the previously isolated Coulrasheskin entries:

* '''Broughgammon:''' deceased Dennis M'Caghan; widow Margaret McCurdy; John, Molly, Betty, Nancy and Matty.
* '''Drumnagessan/Cairn-Hill:''' John M'Caghan and Sarah McCaw; sons David, Archibald, John and James; daughter Isobel.
* '''Drumnagessan:''' Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy; daughters Catherine, Sally and Isobel.
* '''Templastragh:''' Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy; sons John, Alexander, Roger and Robert; daughter Mary.
* '''Templastragh:''' Hector M'Caghan and Peggy Laverty; son Zachariah and daughter Rose.
* '''Templastragh:''' John M'Caghan and Jane Sinclair; sons Hector and Daniel.
* '''Craige:''' Angus M'Caghan and Elizabeth Glass; sons Hugh and Archibald; daughter Belle.

The two Daniel-and-Rose entries occur as separate census households in different townlands and must not be merged without proof. The Templastragh Mary is directly recorded as a daughter of Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy, but no age, later marriage, migration or Rasharkin connection is supplied. This confirms a substantial early, multi-branch Ballintoy network, but none of these households can presently be assigned as the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]. Targeted WikiTree searches found no matching profiles for these exact household combinations, so no IDs are invented here.

=== 1824 Templastragh tithe continuity ===

The later [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf North Antrim tithe revision] independently preserves the Templastragh cluster: it lists '''Zackariah McCahan''', '''Daniel McCahan''', '''Alexander McCahan''' and a '''widow McCahan''' there in 1824. Zackariah is especially notable because the 1803 Ballintoy census names '''Zachariah McCaghan''' as the son of '''Hector McCaghan''' and '''Peggy Laverty'''. Daniel and Alexander also recur as names in the 1803 Daniel-and-Rose household, although the tithe does not state their relationships or ages.<ref name="Evidence1824TemplastraghContinuity">[https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf North Antrim tithe revision names], records 800–801 and 807–814.</ref>

This is genuine chronological corroboration for a continuing McCaughan/McCahan presence in the same Ballintoy townland, and it helps distinguish the early Templastragh households from isolated name occurrences. It still cannot identify the 1803 Mary as the later [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]: the tithe gives no women’s identities beyond the widow, no marriages or children, and no movement toward Lisnagaver or Gortereghy.

=== 1766–1860 Templastragh locality trail ===

The 1766 [https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf Religious Census for Ballintoy] records '''Daniel M'Kaughen''' in '''Templastragh''', with a household size of five. This is a direct pre-1790 occurrence of the same distinctive given name and townland later seen in the 1803 census. The 1803 household is much larger—Daniel M'Caghan, Rose McCurdy and five listed children, including Mary—and the 1824 tithe revision again lists Daniel McCahan in Templastragh.<ref name="Evidence1766TemplastraghDaniel">[https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf 1766 Ballintoy Religious Census], record 348.</ref>

The later [https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-ballintoy.php Griffith's Valuation index] also lists '''Daniel McCahan''' and '''Elizabeth McCaughan''' in Templastragh. Because the valuation is a later occupier index and does not state ages, spouses or parentage, this may represent a younger Daniel or a different household; it cannot be assumed to be the 1803 man. Taken together, the records establish a long-lived Daniel/McCaughan presence in Templastragh from 1766 through the mid-nineteenth century and justify targeted searches for a marriage or baptismal record connecting the households.

This materially strengthens the Ballintoy cluster but still does not prove that the 1803 Mary was [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]] or that Daniel and Rose were her parents.

=== Later Daniel-and-Elizabeth Templastragh branch ===

An [https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/jane-mccaughan-24-1mzn0 Ancestry public-name index] identifies '''Jane McCaughan''', born '''12 November 1834''' at '''Templastragh''', as daughter of '''Daniel McCaughan''' and '''Elizabeth Rogers'''; the same compiled entry estimates both parents at about 1800–1847 and says Jane later emigrated to New York. This is a useful later-household lead because Griffith's Valuation also lists Daniel McCahan and Elizabeth McCaughan in Templastragh.

The index is derivative and does not expose the original baptism or marriage images. It therefore cannot yet establish whether this Daniel was a son of the 1803 Daniel and Rose, a nephew, or an unrelated Daniel in the same townland. It does, however, give a specific child, date, mother’s maiden surname and migration trail for further testing. No evidence currently connects this branch to [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]].

=== First Kilraughts register: confirmed archival target ===

The [https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/accessions/2002/02digests/religion.htm National Archives catalogue] confirms that '''First Kilraughts Presbyterian Church''' records survive at PRONI as '''MIC/1P/462''', including registers and minute books from '''1815–1984'''. An independent [https://ulsterlees.azurewebsites.net/families/co-antrim/ballymoney-area/ North Antrim reconstruction] identifies a marriage in that register on '''8 November 1839''' and gives witnesses, confirming that the register preserves marriage-level detail. The couple's reported 1836 marriage should therefore be searched in the same register under Glasgow/Glasgo/Glassgow and every McCaughan/McAughin/McAughern/McCaughren variant.

This is the clearest remaining route to a contemporaneous record associated with Alexander and Mary. It may name witnesses rather than parents, so even a successful marriage entry may not prove Mary's parentage; however, repeated witnesses could connect her to one of the local McCaughan households. The register must be consulted directly before any conclusion is upgraded.

=== Collateral Drumadarragh McCaughey branch ===

The [https://ulsterlees.azurewebsites.net/families/co-antrim/ballymoney-area/ Ulster Lees reconstruction] documents a separate '''John McCaughey/McCaghy and Margaret Lees''' family associated with '''Drumadarragh''', including Jane (about 1812), Margaret (about 1825), James (about 1833), Sarah (about 1835) and other proposed children. Several adult marriages name John McCaghy as father, and Jane's later death record names John McAughley and Margaret Lees. This branch is geographically relevant to the Ballymoney-area McCaughan variants and explains why the 1817 Drumard household cannot be treated as the only local candidate.

The published reconstruction does not include a daughter Mary of the correct age and remains partly inferential. It is therefore a comparison/exclusion branch, not evidence that John and Margaret were Mary's parents.

=== 1740–1796 Tamlaght O'Crilly / Drumcannon McCaughan continuity lead ===

The 1740 Protestant Householders' Returns identify '''John McCahan''' and '''James McCahan''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''', in the Loughinsholin barony. This is an unusually early, exact-parish occurrence of two McCaughan-variant householders, decades before the Rasharkin baptismal material. The return gives no ages, household composition or relationship between the two men.<ref name="Evidence1740TamlaghtMcCahan">[https://adamsfamilydna.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/1740-Protestant-Returns-Londonderry-County-Ireland.pdf 1740 Protestant Householders' Returns], records 1171–1172.</ref>

A later circa-1800 rent-roll transcription records four McCaughan tenants in '''Drumcannon''' in '''1791''': '''Samuel''', '''Matthew''', '''William''' and '''John'''. The source explains that the undated entries are part of farm rental lists dating roughly 1796–1814, so the dated 1791 entries should be treated as a landlord record, not a census. The 1796 Flaxgrowers' List then records '''William M'Caughin''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''' with three wheels/looms.<ref name="Evidence1791Rent1796Flax">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/misc/rentrolls.html circa-1800 Bann Valley rent-roll transcription], Drumcannon entries 182, 185, 197–198; [https://www.billmacafee.com/1796flaxgrowerslist/1796flaxgrowersderry.pdf 1796 Flaxgrowers' List], record 4754.</ref>

This is new pre-1811 evidence in the same broader parish region and strengthens the case for investigating Tamlaght O'Crilly, Drumcannon and Gortereghy together. It does not prove the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]: the named tenants have no demonstrated relationship to her, and the 1791 William has not been shown to be the 1796 William. The next test is to trace these names through surviving estate papers, Presbyterian records and valuation revisions for a daughter Mary born about 1811 or a transfer into Lisnagaver/Gortereghy.

=== 1817 First Ballymoney McCaughan household: a new Mary-parent candidate ===

Rev. Robert Park's 1817 register of the First Ballymoney Presbyterian Church records '''John McCaughan [McCahon]''', wife '''Mary McCaughan [McCahon]''', and son '''James McCaughan [McCahon]''' at '''Drumard [Drumart]''', house 8. The same register records '''Grissel McCaughan [McCahan]''' and '''Hugh McCaughan [McCahan]''' in a Bendooragh household, showing the variant forms in the Ballymoney-area Presbyterian network at the period when Mary Glasgow would have been a child.<ref name="Evidence1817BallymoneyMcCaughan">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf 1817 First Ballymoney Presbyterian register], records 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

A separate compiled Ballyverdagh account lists a Drumant church-member household as John and Mary McCahon, with son James and daughters Mary and Elizabeth. Since that detail is not present in the searchable Park register entry and the underlying membership source has not been inspected, it remains a secondary lead. If the two records refer to the same couple, their daughter Mary would be chronologically compatible with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s estimated birth about 1811; no marriage, migration, residence or Glasgow connection has been found.

This is currently the strongest new chronological candidate for a Mary-parent household outside the immediate Rasharkin cluster, but it is not proof. The decisive test is to identify the original Drumard/Drumant membership sheet and trace John and Mary McCaughan through Ballymoney Presbyterian baptisms, marriages and valuation records.<ref name="EvidenceDrumantMcCahon">[https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm compiled Ballyverdagh account].</ref>

=== Complete 1817 Ballymoney-area McCaughan audit ===

The full searchable 1817 register contains at least five distinct McCaughan/McCahon placements: '''Charles and Elizabeth McCaughan''' at Balnamore, with children James, Samuel, John, Ann, Daniel and Elizabeth and an older Mary whose relationship is uncertain; '''Samuel and Martha McCaughan''' at Taghey, with sons John and James; '''John and Mary McCaughan''' at Drumard, with son James; '''Grissel McCaughan''' and '''Hugh McCaughan''' in a Bendooragh household headed by William McMaster; and '''Elizabeth McCaughan''' in a Currysiskan household headed by Widow Knox.<ref name="Evidence1817CompleteMcCaughanAudit">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf complete searchable 1817 register], records 1239–1248, 1383, 1436–1439, 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

This is important negative evidence: the primary searchable register does '''not''' list a daughter Mary in the Drumard John-and-Mary household. The separate compiled account's Drumant list of daughters Mary and Elizabeth may represent a different membership list, a different townland, or an expanded/parallel record, but it cannot currently prove that the Drumard couple had a daughter Mary. The Drumard family remains a possible chronological comparison branch, but its evidential weight is lower than the initial reading suggested.

The audit also identifies a Balnamore Mary McCaughan candidate, but the register marks her relationship as uncertain and suggests only that she may be Charles's mother. None of the five placements supplies a marriage, parent statement, migration record or Glasgow link. [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parents therefore remain unproved.

=== Dreen probate cluster: Agnes and Peter McCaughern, 1916 ===

The [https://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/reels/cwa/005014919/005014919_00647.pdf National Archives of Ireland will-calendar] records two adjacent Dreen, Rasharkin estates: '''Agnes McCaughern''', spinster, died 26 March 1916, administration granted to '''William McCaughern'''; and '''Peter McCaughern''', farmer, died 27 February 1916, also granted to William. Later unadministered grants for both estates were made to '''Catherine McCaughern''', spinster.

These entries show a substantial late local McCaughern cluster and a repeated William–Catherine administrative connection, but the calendar does not identify their exact kinship. The underlying probate packets should be obtained because they may name beneficiaries, relatives and property. This is a useful local-network lead, not evidence for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parents.

=== New parent-bearing Armoy/Cromaghs branch: William McCaughan ===

The National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index gives a new parent-bearing local record: '''William McCaughan''', whose present address was Fairhill Street, Ballycastle, supplied an 1851 census extract naming his father '''Archibald McCaughan''' and mother '''Mary'''. The indexed residence was '''Cromaghs, parish of Armoy, barony of Cary''', placing this branch in the wider Ballycastle–Armoy area rather than directly at Lisnagaver or Gortereghy.

This proves an additional Archibald–Mary McCaughan parental pair in the wider North Antrim research region, but it does not identify William with any existing WikiTree profile or connect him to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The record is a census-search-form abstraction rather than the underlying 1851 return, and the next step is to obtain the extract/image and trace William, Archibald and Mary through Cromaghs valuation and church records. No safe WikiTree ID has been assigned to this branch.

Source: [https://censussearchforms.nationalarchives.ie/search/cs/results.jsp?applicantAddress=&applicantFirstname=&applicantSurname=&barony=&censusExtractYear=&city=&county=&fatherFirstname=&fatherSurname=&motherFirstname=&motherSurname=&pageSize=&pager.offset=14290&parish=&search=Search&sort=residence_baronySort&townland= National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index], accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Cromaghs valuation corroboration: Archibald and Margaret McCahan ===

Two independent online transcriptions of Griffith's Valuation for Armoy, dated to the 1861/62 county survey, list '''Archibald Mc Cahan''' as an occupier in '''Cromaghs'''. The same entries also list '''Margaret Mc Cahan''' in Cromaghs. This corroborates the parent-bearing 1851 census-search-form branch: the Archibald named there was an Archibald of the same surname variant and townland in the next decade.

The entries do not state whether Margaret was Archibald's wife, sister, daughter or another household occupier. The valuation is an occupier/property record, not a family register. The spelling is '''McCahan''', while the 1851 search-form entry uses '''McCaughan'''; this is compatible with local spelling variation but cannot identify either person with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s family. No safe WikiTree ID has been found for Archibald or Margaret.

Sources: [https://irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-armoy.php Irish Genealogy Hub transcription of Armoy Griffith's Valuation]; [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/armoy.php Fáilte Romhat transcription]; [https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/research-guides/valuation-office-records/ National Archives guide to valuation records]. Accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Pre-1790 Ballintoy record: Archd. McKaughin at Lisbellanagroagh More ===

The 1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish records '''Archd. McKaughin''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', identified as Protestant. This is a new pre-1790 occurrence of the McCaughan spelling family in the barony of Cary, the same wider North Antrim barony containing later Ballintoy, Armoy and Ballycastle McCaughan/McCahan households.

The census supplies no age, household composition or relationship to Mary Glasgow. It cannot identify this Archibald as her father, and Lisbellanagroagh More is not the same place as Lisnagaver/Gortereghy. It is nevertheless a valuable locality and spelling lead for testing whether the later Armoy/Cromaghs and Rasharkin branches descend from an older Cary family.

Source: [https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf 1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish], entry 318, accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Lisbellanagroagh continuity: Catherine M'Caghan and Daniel McCaw ===

The 1803 Ballintoy census records '''Kath. M'Caghan''', standardised as Catherine McCaughan, at '''Lisbellanagroagh Beg'''. She was listed as the wife of John McIlfatrick and as Church of Ireland; the row gives her age as 29, implying an estimated birth about 1774. The 1824 Ballintoy tithe book then records '''Danl. McCaw''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', the neighbouring “More” townland where the 1766 census had recorded Archd. McKaughin.

These records create a continuous locality trail from an Archibald in 1766, to a McCaughan woman in the adjoining townland in 1803, to a McCaw occupier in More in 1824. They do not prove that Catherine was Archibald's daughter, that Daniel was related to either person, or that this Cary cluster was the family of [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan Glasgow]]. They are nevertheless stronger than isolated surname occurrences and justify targeted searches of Ballintoy Church of Ireland marriages, baptisms and vestry records.

Sources: [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf 1803 Trail census, Ballintoy], entries 2852–2853; [https://www.billmacafee.com/ballintoy/earlydatabases/titheballintoy.pdf 1824 Ballintoy tithe applotment], entry for Daniel McCaw at Lisbellanagroagh More; accessed 15 September 2026.

=== FamilySearch record-hint collision: James McCaughan and Alexander McCaughan ===

The logged-in FamilySearch record search returned an indexed Ireland marriage result describing '''James Mc Caughan''' as father of '''Alexander Mc Caughan'''. The attached Family Tree match was '''MCGP-3S2''', but that profile is James McCaughan born about '''1827''', with spouse Catharine McConachie and children Alexander McCaughan ('''1847–1921''', 96QG-NVJ) and Robert Mc Caughan ('''1853–1934''', K4GP-RD8). The tree profile has no sources and the relationship was added in 2020.

This is a new and important exclusion. The attached tree person cannot be the older James proposed as Mary's father: he is too young, and his son Alexander was born decades after Mary's marriage and the 1837–1844 Glasgow baptisms. The indexed father statement may belong to a different McCaughan family or be an aggregation error; it must not be cited as evidence for Mary's parentage. Source: [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCGP-3S2 FamilySearch tree profile MCGP-3S2], and [https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&q.givenName=James&q.surname=McCaughan&q.birthLikeDate.from=1760&q.birthLikeDate.to=1800&q.birthLikePlace=Antrim%2C%20Ireland FamilySearch James McCaughan search results], accessed 15 September 2026.

The same search also surfaced '''James McCaughan''' in the Irish Valuation Office Books for '''Shankill in 1838''' and '''Billy, Ballycastle in 1861'''. These are new locality leads, but the index does not expose enough detail to identify the tenant with [[McCaughan-68|McCaughan-68]], the Gortereghy tithe tenant, or Mary's father. The underlying valuation images should be checked for townland continuity, occupier changes and adjoining McCaughan households.

The death of Alexander Glasgow was registered on 16 May 1888 in Ballymoney, aged 84.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Alexander Glasgow, 16 May 1888, aged 84, Ballymoney registration district, D/1888/31/1005/7/348.</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Mary "Molly" McCaughan''' was born about 1810 or 1811 in County Antrim, Ireland. She married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], a farmer associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim.

Her parentage has not been established.

Mary's surname appears in surviving and transcribed records in several forms, including '''McCaughan''', '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern'''. Her given name appears as both '''Mary''' and '''Molly'''. These variants appear to refer to the same woman rather than separate wives of Alexander Glasgow.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">Richard John Torrens, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian Church Baptisms, 1834–1846], transcription by Barbara Braswell, particularly entries 75, 106 and 203 (accessed 16 July 2026). The page warns that faded or difficult entries may contain transcription errors. Original register: PRONI MIC.1P/292.</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Mary married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] about '''1836''', probably in County Antrim.

The detailed transcription of the surviving 1851 census records 1836 as the first-marriage year for both Alexander and Mary.<ref name="CensusTranscript">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], Lisnagaver households 34–37, p. 183 (accessed 16 July 2026). This is a transcription of the same census return, not independent evidence.</ref>

No original marriage entry has yet been identified.

The surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian marriage register begins only in 1845 and is therefore too late to contain their marriage.<ref name="ChurchCoverage">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/church.php?civilparish=Rasharkin&civilparishid=347&search_type=full Church records for Rasharkin], Presbyterian entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/292: baptisms from 1834 and marriages from 1845 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Second Portglenone Presbyterian Church remains a candidate for further research because its surviving marriage register begins in 1822 under PRONI reference MIC.1P/357.<ref name="SecondPortglenone">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/county_church_full.php?county=Antrim&denomination=Presbyterian&location=Public+Record+Office+of+Northern+Ireland&search_type=full Historic Presbyterian church records for County Antrim], Second Portglenone entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/357, marriages from 1822 (accessed 2026).</ref>

It should not, however, be described as their known marriage congregation unless an entry is found.

=== Children ===

Known and possible children of Alexander Glasgow and Mary McCaughan include:

The published Rasharkin baptism transcription contains no baptism entries for 1840 or 1841. Robert's missing baptism is therefore more likely to reflect incomplete record coverage or transcription than evidence that he belonged to another family.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== 1851 Census ===

In the surviving 1851 census, Mary was living at Lisnagaver with her husband Alexander and their children Robert, James and Ann.

Alexander was aged 40 and Mary was also aged '''40'''. Both were born in County Antrim, and the detailed census transcription records 1836 as their first-marriage year.<ref name="CensusHousehold">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, County Antrim, household 35, Alexander Glasgow household; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ household images] (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref><ref name="CensusTranscript" />

Mary's age therefore supports a birth about '''1810 or 1811'''. Earlier estimates placing her birth around 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with this contemporary census evidence.

=== Residences ===

The surviving records place Alexander and Mary within a small area of Rasharkin parish over a period of years:

Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck are separate adjoining townlands in Rasharkin civil parish, barony of Kilconway, County Antrim.<ref name="Townlands">[https://www.townlands.ie/antrim/kilconway/rasharkin/killoquin/lisnagaver/ Lisnagaver Townland, County Antrim], administrative divisions and adjoining-townland map (accessed 2026).</ref>

The changing descriptions may reflect residence close to a townland boundary rather than a substantial migration.

=== The Lisnagaver Glasgow–McCaughan Network ===

Mary and Alexander were part of a closely associated Glasgow and McCaughan network centred on Lisnagaver and the surrounding townlands.

Several Glasgow households appear together in the surviving 1851 census fragment.<ref name="CensusTranscript" />

The census explicitly identifies '''John and Samuel as brothers'''. It does not identify Alexander or Thomas as their brothers.

Later valuation evidence provides a separate land-based connection. John, Alexander and Thomas occupied consecutive principal holdings at Lisnagaver under the same immediate lessor, Robert Harvey.

The consecutive lot numbers strongly suggest that the holdings were physically close. The valuation map should still be consulted before stating that every plot directly adjoined or shared a boundary.

The combined census, church and land evidence supports a close Glasgow family-and-neighbour network at Lisnagaver while leaving the precise relationships unresolved.

==== Alexander and Thomas Glasgow ====

There is substantial circumstantial evidence that [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] was a close relative, and possibly a brother, of Mary's husband [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].

Alexander and Thomas were:

* born in County Antrim about five years apart;
* farmers;
* able to read and write;
* associated with the same Presbyterian congregation;
* recorded within the same Lisnagaver–Gortereagh–Moneyleck micro-area;
* heads of closely grouped Lisnagaver households in 1851;
* and later occupiers of consecutive valuation lots under the same lessor.

The contemporary Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism register provides a particularly strong FAN connection.

Alexander and Mary or Molly used the congregation while associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver. Thomas and [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]] used the same congregation while associated with Moneyleck and Lisnagaver.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

Most notably:

* Alexander and Mary's son James was born at Lisnagaver on '''9 October 1843''';
* Thomas and Mary Ann's daughter Eliza was born there on '''17 October 1843'''.

The children were born only eight days apart in the same small townland and appear in the same Presbyterian register.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

This is substantial FAN evidence for a close relationship.

No surviving record presently calls Alexander and Thomas brothers. Thomas should therefore be treated as Alexander's '''probable close relative and possible brother''', not as a proved sibling.

==== Thomas and Daniel Glasgow ====

A reported will record for [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea identifies [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] as his "late brother" and [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] as a nephew.<ref name="DanielWill">Will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871, reported in accumulated family research as identifying Thomas Glasgow as his "late brother". The original probate copy and complete archival citation are still required.</ref>

This supports Daniel and Thomas as brothers.

It does not establish Alexander's relationship to either man.

==== McCaughan Marriage Connection ====

The relationship between the Glasgow and McCaughan families was not limited to Mary's marriage to Alexander.

[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]'s daughter [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].

This provides another direct marriage connection between the Glasgow and McCaughen families within the same local network.

It does not, by itself, establish Robert McCaughen's relationship to Mary.

The original 1834 Rasharkin tithe book records William and James McCaheran at Gortereghy. The spelling is compatible with the McAughin and McAughern forms used for Mary in the baptism transcription, and Alexander and Mary's children were recorded at Gortereghy in 1837–38. This supports investigation of a local McCaughan family network, but the tithe names no relationships and does not establish Mary's parents.<ref name="GortereghyTithe1834">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Tithe Applotment Book for Rasharkin parish'', 1834, PRONI FIN/5/A/236, Gortereghy entries for William and James McCaheran.</ref>

=== The 1875 Mary Anne M‘Caughern Witness ===

On 18 February 1875, at Finvoy Parish Church, [[Glasgow-1371|Ann (Glasgow) Bellingham]] married Francis Bellingham.

Ann was the daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], farmer.

The witnesses were:

* Thomas Bellingham;
* '''Mary Anne M‘Caughern'''.

<ref name="BellinghamGlasgow1875">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Francis Bellingham and [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]], 18 February 1875, Finvoy Parish Church; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf digital image], entry 40.</ref>

The witness is relevant because of the established Glasgow–McCaughan network in and around Lisnagaver.

She should '''not''' presently be identified as [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow.

Reasons for caution include:

* the witness was recorded as '''Mary Anne''', rather than Mary or Molly;
* the surname was recorded as '''M‘Caughern''';
* no reliable evidence currently establishes that Alexander's wife was still living in 1875;
* other McCaughan or McAughern households existed within the wider local network.

The witness should therefore remain an unidentified associate pending further evidence.== Research Notes ==

=== Birth Date ===

Mary's age of 40 in the 1851 census supports birth about '''1810 or 1811'''.

Earlier estimates of about 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with the surviving census evidence and should not be used without an independent source.

=== Parentage ===

Mary's parents are presently '''unknown'''.

No surviving baptism, marriage entry, will, gravestone, death record or other contemporary source located for this profile explicitly names either parent.

The Rasharkin baptism entries establish Mary's maiden surname in variants such as '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern''', but they do not identify her father or mother.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== Possible John McCaughen Connection ===

A John McCaughen of Mount Pleasant Township, Washington County, Pennsylvania, made a will dated 22 February 1815 in which he referred to:

:''my onley daughter which I left in Ireland when I came to America.''

The daughter was named Mary McCaughen, and John reportedly left half of his estate to her.<ref name="PennsylvaniaMcCaughen">[https://dokumen.pub/irish-presbyterians-and-the-shaping-of-western-pennsylvania-17701830-hardcovernbsped-0822945436-9780822945437.html ''Irish Presbyterians and the Shaping of Western Pennsylvania, 1770–1830''], discussion of John McCaughen's 1815 will.</ref>

This is potentially relevant because:

* the daughter's name was Mary McCaughen;
* she remained in Ireland when her father emigrated;
* Mary's revised birth estimate of about 1810 or 1811 means she was alive by 1815.

However, no evidence currently connects the Pennsylvania testator to:

* County Antrim;
* Rasharkin;
* Lisnagaver or Gortereagh;
* Alexander Glasgow;
* or the known local McCaughan/McAughern network.

The identification should therefore be treated only as a '''research hypothesis''', not as Mary's established parentage.

=== Distinction from Mary McCaughan, wife of John McAulay ===

This Mary should not be confused with another Mary McCaughan who married John McAulay.

That woman was reportedly born about 1817 in Dublin, married John McAulay in 1840, emigrated to New York in 1859 and later appeared in the 1861 census of Ontario, Canada.

Records identify that Mary as a daughter of Hugh McCaughan.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:27T9-VWQ "New York Passenger Lists, 1820–1891", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1859.</ref><ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MQWD-6ZH "Canada, Ontario Census, 1861", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1861.</ref>

She was therefore a different woman from [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver.

=== Death ===

Mary died at Gortahar, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim, on 27 February 1892. The register describes her as a widow and housewife, reportedly aged 89. Her daughter [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Elder]] was present at death.<ref name="MaryDeath1892">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Mary Glasgow, 27 February 1892, Gortahar, Ballymoney registration district; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1892/06049/4723532.pdf digital image].</ref>

The reported age implies birth about 1803, while the 1851 census implies about 1810 or 1811. Her birth date remains estimated. The former 1866 death estimate is superseded by this registration.

=== Robert Glasgow's Scottish Death ===

[[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]]'s reported death on 27 November 1902 in Glasgow, Scotland, remains potentially important.

A Scottish death registration would normally have space to record both parents, including the mother's maiden surname, if known to the informant.

The original registration should be obtained before relying on parent details copied from online family trees.

=== Local McCaughan / McAughern Network ===

The Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription records McAughern households in or near the same local area.

This does not prove a relationship to Mary, but it makes reconstruction of the local McCaughan/McAughern population a priority.

Particular attention should be paid to:

* [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]];
* the unidentified Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 Bellingham–Glasgow marriage;
* McCaughan, McAughin and McAughern entries associated with Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck;
* witnesses to Glasgow and McCaughan marriages and baptisms;
* valuation and estate records involving the same surnames.

=== Identity and Record Cautions ===

* Mary's age of 40 in 1851 supports birth about 1810 or 1811, not 1817 or 1818.
* ''Molly'' is a familiar form of Mary and does not indicate a second wife.
* The spellings McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and M‘Caughern should not automatically be treated as different families.
* The baptism transcription is derivative evidence and the original PRONI MIC.1P/292 register should be inspected.
* No parent should be attached to Mary solely from surname similarity.
* The Pennsylvania John McCaughen theory remains unproved.
* Mary Anne M‘Caughern, witness in 1875, should not currently be merged with Mary.
* No unsupported 1866 death should be used for Mary.
* No Scottish or Australian death should be attached without evidence connecting it to the Lisnagaver family.

=== Priority Research ===

==== Priority 1 — Find Alexander and Mary's Marriage ====

* Search Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages under '''PRONI MIC.1P/357''' from about 1834 through 1838.
* Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glascow, Glascaw, McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and similar forms.
* Record residences, witnesses and minister even if no parents are named.
* Do not assume Second Portglenone was the congregation unless an entry is found.

==== Priority 1 — Inspect the Original Rasharkin Register ====

* Inspect the original Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries under '''PRONI MIC.1P/292'''.
* Check the entries for James in 1837, the unnamed child in 1838 and James in 1843–1844.
* Record the exact original spelling of Mary's surname.
* Examine adjacent entries, marginal notes and witnesses or sponsors.
* Collect every McCaughan/McAughern entry rather than only those already associated with Alexander.

==== Priority 1 — Reconstruct the McCaughan Network ====

* Investigate [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]].
* Identify Robert's father, mother, siblings, residence and landholding.
* Search for links between Robert and Mary through witnesses, naming patterns, church records, leases, probate or valuation records.
* Reconstruct McCaughan/McAughern households in Lisnagaver, Gortereagh, Moneyleck and adjoining townlands.
* Treat repeated surnames and proximity as FAN evidence only until a direct relationship is found.

==== Priority 1 — Obtain Robert Glasgow's Death Record ====

* Confirm the reported death of [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] in Scotland on 27 November 1902.
* Obtain the original Scottish statutory death registration.
* Record the names of both parents exactly as given.
* Record the mother's maiden surname and the identity of the informant.
* Assess the reliability of the parent information according to the informant's relationship to Robert.

==== Priority 2 — Identify Mary Anne M‘Caughern ====

* Trace the Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 marriage of [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]] and Francis Bellingham.
* Search Finvoy, Rasharkin and Ballymoney-area civil and Presbyterian records.
* Compare age, residence, marital status and family connections.
* Do not attach her to this profile without evidence establishing identity.

==== Priority 2 — Investigate the Pennsylvania Hypothesis ====

* Obtain the original or full abstract of John McCaughen's 1815 Washington County, Pennsylvania will.
* Establish when John emigrated from Ireland.
* Identify his place of origin in Ireland if possible.
* Determine Mary's age or circumstances from probate, guardianship, land or correspondence records.
* Search for associates linking John to County Antrim or the Bann Valley.
* Do not attach John as Mary's father unless a documentary bridge is found.

==== Priority 2 — Land and Estate Records ====

* Trace Glasgow and McCaughan/McAughern occupiers through the Lisnagaver valuation-revision books.
* Examine Harvey estate rentals, leases, assignments, arrears ledgers, tenant correspondence and surrender records.
* Pay particular attention to lots 24, 25 and 26 and nearby holdings.
* Look for explicit relationships such as daughter, son-in-law, brother, widow or representatives.
* Follow parcel numbers and tenancy succession rather than surnames alone.
* Candidate death entry: Mary Glasgow, 17 February 1892, aged 89, Ballymoney district, D/1892/31/1005/8/234. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Biography ==

'''Robert Elder''' was born about 1831, probably in County Antrim. His birth estimate is based on his reported age of 40 at marriage.

On 14 June 1871 Robert married [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Glasgow]] in the Ballymoney registration district. The original register describes him as a 40-year-old bachelor and farmer and names his father as '''[[Elder-7300|Nathaniel Elder]], farmer'''. Mary was a 28-year-old spinster residing at Lisnagaver, daughter of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], farmer.<ref name="ElderGlasgow1871">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Robert Elder and Mary Glasgow, 14 June 1871; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1871/11341/8162804.pdf digital image].</ref>

The Lisnagaver valuation revision books later show Robert succeeding Alexander Glasgow as occupier of lot 25, containing 8 acres 2 roods 10 perches. This supports continuity between the marriage family and the Lisnagaver Glasgow household but does not by itself establish Robert’s death date.<ref name="LisnagaverRevision25">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, valuation revision books for Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, PRONI VAL/12/B/4/16C and VAL/12/B/4/16D, lot 25; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx PRONI search and image viewer].</ref>

=== Family and later records ===

The 1901 census records Robert's widow [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Elder]] at Gortahar with their children [[Elder-7302|Mary]], [[Elder-7303|Robert J.]] and [[Elder-7304|Jane M.]].<ref name="Census1901">1901 Census of Ireland, Gortahar, Rasharkin, County Antrim, Mary Elder household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPB2-KNM2 indexed record].</ref> In 1911 Robert J. headed the continuing household with his mother, sister Jane and nephew [[Elder-7305|Samuel Glasgow Elder]].<ref name="Census1911">1911 Census of Ireland, Gortahar, Rasharkin, County Antrim, Robert J. Elder household; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QYHR-52T2 indexed record].</ref>

A published transcription of the First Garvagh Presbyterian register records the marriage of [[Elder-7301|William Elder]] and [[McMaster-2595|Ellen J. McMaster]] on 6 September 1864. William's father was [[Elder-7300|Nathaniel Elder]], farmer, and Robert Elder was a witness.<ref name="WilliamMarriage1864">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/GarvaghP1/Marriages/1845-1889marr.html First Garvagh Presbyterian Church marriages, 1845–1889], entry 110, William Elder and Ellen J. McMaster, 6 September 1864.</ref> The common father, occupation, locality and Robert's role as witness make William a likely brother, although the identification remains qualified pending the original register and further family evidence.

A Robert Elder aged 64 whose death was registered at Ballymoney in the fourth quarter of 1894 is a strong candidate for this man and would explain Mary's widowed status in 1901.<ref name="Death1894">Ireland civil registration death index, Robert Elder, Ballymoney, October–December 1894, vol. 1, p. 100; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FTZP-9M6 indexed record].</ref> The original death entry is required before the identification is treated as proved.
