== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
'''Alexander Glasgow''' is the proposed head of an early Bann Valley family.
His existence and family are reconstructed from later descendant testimony; no
contemporary record yet identifies him with certainty.

If [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], born about 1795 or 1796, was his son,
Alexander must have been born before about 1778. The former estimate of about
1790 is incompatible with that relationship.

Alexander is associated with Rosanna, surname unknown. A 2007 descendant account
names Alexander and Rosanna as parents of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] of
Lisnagaver and reports that Rosanna died about 23 October 1822.<ref name="DescendantAccount">[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited''], descendant account posted 25 January 2007.</ref> No marriage, baptism or will has been found to verify the account. Rosanna's reported surname Shaw is unsupported and should remain a research lead only.

== Tithe applotment book for the parish of Rasharkin ==

{{Image
|file=Glasgow-3904.png
|align=c
|size=l
|label=Tithe applotment book for the parish of Rasharkin.
|link=/photo/png/Glasgow-3904
|caption=Tithe applotment book for the parish of Rasharkin.
}}


The original Rasharkin Tithe Applotment Book records two separate Glasgow holdings at Lisnagaver in 1834:

* '''Alexr Glasgow''' — 29 acres, comprising 10 acres first quality, 10 acres second quality and 9 acres third quality.
* '''Robt Glasgow''' — 35 acres, comprising 11 acres first quality, 10 acres second quality and 14 acres third quality.

The red numbers 4 and 5 beside their names are consecutive entry numbers, not ages. The men appear on separate lines with separate acreages and assessments. The manuscript states no relationship between them.<ref name="RasharkinTithe1834">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Tithe
  applotment book for the parish of Rasharkin'', 1834, PRONI FIN/5/A/236, manuscript folio 17, PDF image 19 of 84, Lisnagaver entries for Alexr and
  Robt Glasgow; digital image accessed 5 August 2026 through the [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/BrowseSearchPage.aspx PRONI Browse
  eCatalogue].</ref>

The identity of Robt Glasgow has not been established. Possible candidates include [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]] and [[Glasgow-3941|Robert Glasgow of Coltrim]], but no inspected record connects either man with Lisnagaver. The entry should therefore remain unidentified.

or [[Glasgow-3449|Robert Glasgow (1797-1868)]] who died in Ballymoney registration district in 1868 aged 71, implying birth about 1796–97.

If he was the tithe Robert, he was only about fourteen years older than Alexander born circa 1811. That makes him a very unlikely father and a much more plausible older brother, cousin, or son of the older Alexander.

=== A persistent Marks connection ties Alexander and Thomas together ===

The original marriage witnesses reveal a useful network:

* John Marks witnessed the 1866 marriage of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow (1811-aft.1861)]]’s son [[Glasgow-938|Robert]].<ref name="MarksRobert1866">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3134069 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of Robert Glasgow and Jane Graham, 5 April 1866; John Marks witnessed.</ref>
* Jane Marks witnessed the 1879 marriage of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]’s daughter Anne/Nancy.<ref name="MarksAnne1879">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-2645258 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration for Thomas Glasgow’s daughter Anne/Nancy, 1879; Jane Marks witnessed.</ref>
* Lizzie J. Marks witnessed the 1888 marriage of Thomas’s son Daniel Neely.<ref name="MarksDaniel1888">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-2455742 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of Daniel Neely Glasgow and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888; Lizzie J. Marks witnessed.</ref>

Meanwhile, Gardiner Marks appears directly after Alexander and Robert in the 1834 Lisnagaver tithe order. A younger Gardiner Marks married in 1857 and named his father as Gardiner Marks, farmer.<ref name="MarksGardiner1857">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3271390 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of Gardiner Marks, 1857, naming his father as Gardiner Marks, farmer.</ref>

That is good independent evidence that Alexander’s and Thomas’s descendants belonged to one enduring Lisnagaver–Kilrea social network. It strengthens their probable brotherhood, although it still does not prove it.
=== Possible later division of Alexander's holding ===

The National Archives of Ireland states that acreage in the Tithe Applotment Books was recorded in Irish or Plantation measure, approximately 1.62 statute acres for each Plantation acre.<ref name="TitheMeasure">National Archives of Ireland,
  [https://www.nationalarchives.ie/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Family_History_Sources_NAI.pdf “The Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–37”], explanation of acreage and measurement, accessed 5 August 2026.</ref> On that general conversion, Alexander's 29-acre tithe holding would represent approximately 46.98 statute acres.

The later valuation records [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] occupying lot 25, containing 8 acres, 2 roods and 10 perches, and  [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] occupying lot 26, containing 32 acres, 3 roods and 15 perches.<ref name="LisnagaverValuation">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Valuation Revision Book for Killoquin Lower electoral division, Rasharkin parish, PRONI VAL/12/B/4/16A, folios 52–53, Lisnagaver lots 24–26; see also [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/rasharkin.htm Griffith's Valuation transcript for Rasharkin],
  accessed 5 August 2026.</ref>

Their combined holdings amounted to 41 acres, 1 rood and 25 perches, leaving a theoretical balance of approximately 5 acres, 2 roods and 12 perches:

Alexander's 1834 holding:
29 Plantation acres ≈ 46.98 statute acres

* Possible later division:
** Alexander, lot 25     8a 2r 10p
** Thomas, lot 26       32a 3r 15p
** theoretical balance   5a 2r 12p

This calculation makes it possible that the older Alexander's holding was later divided between the younger Alexander, Thomas and another occupier. It does not prove that the later lots were formed from the same land. The tithe and valuation surveys were compiled for different purposes, and no inspected lease, succession entry or map connects the 1834 holding directly with lots 25 and 26. The unit of measurement used in this particular Rasharkin volume should also be confirmed from its introductory or certification pages before the conversion is treated as exact.

Robert's separate 35-acre tithe holding—approximately 56.7 statute acres under the same general conversion—also remains to be accounted for.

=== Rosanna ===

Rosanna's maiden surname has not been identified.

Slater's 1846 directory lists two watch and clock makers at Kilrea:

* '''Daniel Glasco'''; and
* '''James Shaw'''.<ref name="Slater1846">[https://www.failteromhat.com/slater/0192.pdf Isaac Slater, ''Slater's National Commercial Directory of Ireland''] (1846), Kilrea, p. 473, under “Watch & Clock Makers”, listing Daniel Glasco and James Shaw (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

One possible interpretation of the descendant tradition is that Daniel Glasgow represented one side of the family and James Shaw the other. This led to the theory that Rosanna's maiden surname was Shaw.

No marriage, baptism, will or other contemporary record identifies Rosanna as a Shaw or as a sister of James Shaw. The occupational coincidence does not establish a sibling relationship. Her LNAB should therefore remain '''Unknown''', while Shaw may be retained only as a research lead.

If Rosanna remains attached as the uncertain mother of Daniel, she must have been born before about 1780. Her previously proposed birth about 1790 is chronologically impossible for a child born about 1795 or 1796.

The reported death date of about 23 October 1822 has not been independently confirmed.

=== Working children ===

Alexander and Rosanna are shown as the uncertain parents of:

* '''[[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]''', born about 1795 or 1796, a watchmaker and farmer of Kilrea; and
* '''[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]''', born about 1815 or 1816, a farmer of Lisnagaver.

[[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]], born about 1811, belongs to the same close local network but is no longer attached as their son. [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] is retained on his profile as the leading uncertain, place-based father candidate.

The descendant account explicitly identifies Thomas as a son of Alexander and Rosanna.<ref name="FamilyTradition">[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 "Trying to find Glasgow"], ''Genes Reunited'', post by Peter dated 25 January 2007, with later replies, naming Alexander and Rosanna as the parents of Thomas Glasgow of Lisnagaver, reporting Rosanna's death about 23 October 1822, and mentioning two possible clockmaker uncles at Kilrea (accessed 16 July 2026). This is descendant testimony rather than a contemporary parent record.</ref>

Daniel's original 1871 will identifies Thomas as '''“my late brother”''' and Daniel Neely Glasgow as his nephew.<ref name="DanielWill1871">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], original registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Daniel Neely Glasgow's 1888 marriage record names his father as Thomas Glasgow, farmer, and connects that family with Lisnagaver.<ref name="DanielNeelyMarriage1888">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/ IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of Daniel Neely Glasgow and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church; groom described as a farmer of Lisnagaver and his father recorded as Thomas Glasgow, farmer (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Together, these records prove that Daniel of Kilrea and Thomas of Lisnagaver were brothers. They do not identify their parents.

Their shared attachment to Alexander and Rosanna remains an uncertain reconstruction based principally on the descendant account. The evidence does not exclude:

* a half-brother relationship;
* an error in the descendant tradition;
* different parents for one or more of the men; or
* another Alexander and Rosanna belonging to the same local family cluster.

The younger Alexander remains a possible close collateral relative of Daniel and Thomas because of his age, location and association with the Lisnagaver family. No inspected record calls him their brother or names this older Alexander as his father.

The 1851 census records the younger Alexander and Thomas as similarly aged farmers in Lisnagavor families 35 and 37.<ref name="Census1851Macafee">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf W. Scott and William Macafee, ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], Rasharkin parish, Lisnagavor, families 34, 35 and 37, recording the households of John, Alexander and Thomas Glasgow (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

Their proximity supports a close relationship but does not by itself prove that they were brothers or identify their parents.

=== Clockmaker tradition ===

The descendant account's reference to two clockmaker uncles appears to preserve a genuine association with Kilrea.

[[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] is independently documented as a Kilrea watch and clock maker and is proved to have been Thomas's brother.<ref name="Slater1846" /><ref name="DanielWill1871" />

An 1831 County Londonderry census transcription records '''“Danl.”''' in Kilrea town, house 37, under the standardised surname Glasgow. The surname as read from the census return is shown as '''“Glosger [?]”'''. The house was shared by two families and contained eight males and two females; nine occupants were Presbyterian and one belonged to the Established Church.<ref name="Census1831Derry">[https://www.billmacafee.com/1831census/1831derrycensusplace.pdf William Macafee, ''Names of Householders listed in the 1831 Census Returns for the County of Londonderry''] (transcription from PRONI MIC/5A/5–9B), Kilrea town, house 37, recording “Danl.” under the standardised surname Glasgow, with the surname in the return read as “Glosger [?]”; and Tamlaght O'Crilly parish, Inishrush, houses 2 and 91, recording John and Adam “Glasco” (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

The census gives no age, occupation or family relationships. This is therefore a plausible candidate for the later clockmaker, not a proved identification. If confirmed from the manuscript, it would place Daniel at Kilrea by 1831 rather than only by the 1846 directory.

Daniel was Thomas's brother, not his uncle. The family tradition may have:

* shifted the relationship by one generation;
* referred to uncles of Thomas's children rather than Thomas himself;
* combined members of the Glasgow and Shaw families; or
* preserved only a general memory of clockmaking relatives at Kilrea.

The tradition supports further investigation but should not be converted into a specific relationship with James Shaw.

=== Possible parents ===

[[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-760890|Rose]] of Inishrush, County Londonderry, were previously proposed as Alexander's parents. No inspected record names either parent or connects Alexander directly with Inishrush.

No contemporary record inspected names Adam or Rose as Alexander's parents. No record connects Alexander directly with Inishrush.

Adam and Rose had a large and incompletely documented family. Their gravestone names their children James and Eliza, while a newspaper notice describes Nancy Glasgow as Adam's sixth daughter.<ref name="AdamGrave">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ "Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower Graveyard"], transcription of the Glasgow gravestone recording Rose, wife of Adam Glasgow; Adam Glasgow; their daughter Eliza; their son James; and grandson William. The same page transcribes the 1842 marriage notice of Nancy, sixth daughter of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The proposed connection was based on regional proximity, overlapping generations and gaps in Adam's documented family. The additional records set out below strengthen the existence of a local Glasgow cluster, but they still do not establish Alexander's parentage.

Rose was reportedly born about 1767. If Alexander was born by about 1778, she would have been only about eleven years old. This creates a severe chronological conflict with her proposed maternity.

Possible explanations include:

* one or both estimated birth years are materially wrong;
* Adam was Alexander's father by an earlier partner;
* Alexander was Adam's brother, cousin or another collateral relative; or
* there was no close connection between the Inishrush and Lisnagaver families.

Adam and Rose are not retained as Alexander's parents. Rose's age chronologically excludes her as the mother of a man old enough to father Daniel about 1795 or 1796, while no record establishes Adam as Alexander's father by another partner.

No evidence supports placing this family beneath an earlier Scottish, Kilwaughter, Derry Main or Moneymore line.

=== Tamlaght O'Crilly and Inishrush cluster ===

A transcription of the 1740 Protestant householder list for Tamlaght O'Crilly parish contains two entries under the name '''Hugh Glasgow'''.<ref name="Householders1740">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/books/Kilrea/Kilrea07.html John W. Kernohan, ''The Parishes of Kilrea and Tamlaght O'Crilly''], Appendix E, “Protestant householders in Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish in 1740,” containing two entries for Hugh Glasgow (online transcription by Richard John Torrens; accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

A Belfast News-Letter notice printed on 14 April 1772 lists '''Hugh Glasgow''' among inhabitants of Tamlaght O'Crilly parish who declared that they had surrendered their arms to Henry Ellis of Innisrush. The declaration was dated at Innisrush on 6 April 1772.<ref name="Hugh1772">[https://arborealis.ca/records/newspapers/kilrea-news/1770-1779/ “1770–1779: News transcripts for Kilrea & environs”], ''Arborealis'', transcript of the ''Belfast News-Letter'', 14 April 1772, declaration dated Innisrush, 6 April 1772, listing Hugh Glasgow among inhabitants of Tamlaght O'Crilly parish (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

It is not known whether the 1772 Hugh was one of the men listed in 1740, a son or other relative, or an unrelated namesake. The records provide no family relationships.

The 1831 census transcription records two separate Glasgow households at Inishrush:

* '''John “Glasco”''', house 2: one family, four males and four females, all Presbyterian; and
* '''Adam “Glasco”''', house 91: one family, three males and five females, all Presbyterian.<ref name="Census1831Derry" />

The return supplies no ages, occupations or relationships within either household. Alexander could theoretically have been an unnamed male in one of them, but there is no evidence that he was. John and Adam were probably part of the same local surname cluster, though their precise relationship is unknown.

The 1833 Tithe Applotment transcription records '''Adam Glasgow''' at Innisrush.<ref name="TitheInishrush1833">[https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/derry/tithe-applotments/tamlaght-o-crilly-parish.php “Tithe Applotment Books 1823–1838: Tamlaght O Crilly Parish, county Derry”], transcription entry for Adam Glasgow, Innisrush, 1833 (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

Taken together, the 1740, 1772, 1831 and 1833 records show that the Glasgow surname was established in Tamlaght O'Crilly parish across several generations. They make a connection between the Inishrush and Lisnagaver families more plausible, but they do not provide a pedigree.

Hugh Glasgow, documented in the parish in 1772, is now the most useful preceding-generation research lead because his known presence falls close to Alexander's estimated birth period. He should not be attached as Alexander's father without further evidence.

=== Lisnagaver ===

The 1834 Tithe Applotment transcription records '''Alexander Glasgow''' and '''Robert Glasgow''' consecutively at Lisnagaver.<ref name="Tithe1834">[https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrim.pdf William Macafee, ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering North Antrim''], records 7501–7502, Alexander and Robert Glasgow at Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, 1834 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The Alexander in this record may have been:

* this older Alexander;
* [[Glasgow-951|the younger Alexander]], then about twenty-three; or
* another man of the same name.

The entry supplies no age, spouse, parent or other identifying information. It should not be treated as proof that this older Alexander was alive in 1834.

Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism records confirm the later households of the younger Alexander and Thomas. Alexander and Molly McAughern had children recorded at Gortereagh in 1837–1838 and at Lisnagaver in 1844. Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken had children recorded at Moneyleck in 1842 and at Lisnagaver from 1843.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html "Rasharkin Presbyterian Church Baptisms"], entries for the households of Alexander Glasgow and Molly McAughern and Thomas Glasgow and Mary Ann McCracken (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

These records establish the younger households but do not identify their father.

The 1851 census contains a further possible collateral clue. Family 34 at Lisnagavor, immediately before the younger Alexander's family 35, comprised:

* '''John Glasgow''', aged 50, farmer, born County Antrim;
* Margaret Glasgow, wife, aged 30, born County Londonderry;
* Ann Glasgow, daughter, aged 3, born County Londonderry; and
* '''Samuel Glasgow''', John's brother, aged 60, linen weaver, born County Londonderry.<ref name="Census1851Macafee" />

Samuel was born about 1790 or 1791, placing him in roughly the same generation as Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea. His presence gives a concrete County Londonderry connection within the Glasgow household immediately beside the younger Alexander.

The census explicitly proves only that Samuel and John were brothers. It does not prove that either man was related to the younger Alexander, Thomas or Daniel. Household proximity is evidence for investigation, not a stated relationship.

=== Death ===

Alexander's date and place of death have not been identified.

He was alive before the births of his proposed children, but no secure burial, gravestone, probate or land record has been found that establishes a later date.

No Alexander Glasgow probate-calendar entry has been identified in the surviving PRONI calendars. This does not prove that Alexander left no will, since he may have died before the calendars begin or his estate may not have required probate.

=== Identity cautions ===

Alexander should not be confused with:

* [[Glasgow-951|the younger Alexander Glasgow]], born about 1810 or 1811 and living at Lisnagaver in 1851;
* Alexander Glasgow of Glenleslie, labourer and son of John Glasgow, who married Mary Anne Martin in 1847; or
* the Alexander Glasgow who died at Gortahar on 16 May 1888, aged 84, whose daughter Nancy was present at his death.

The Glenleslie marriage identifies a separate man through his residence, occupation, father and marriage date. The Gortahar death belongs to a later namesake and supplies no evidence about this Alexander.

This Alexander should not be attached as a son or brother of [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] solely to connect the Glenleslie and Lisnagaver families. A local collateral connection is possible, but its degree is unknown.

The 1831 Kilrea entry for “Danl.” under the standardised surname Glasgow should not be treated as Daniel Glasgow's record until the original census image and difficult surname reading have been checked.

=== Recommended relationships ===

* [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] — former father hypothesis; not attached because no positive parent record identifies him;
* [[Unknown-760890|Rose]] — excluded as Alexander's mother by the severe chronological conflict;
* [[Unknown-761034|Rosanna, surname unknown]] — uncertain spouse;
* [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] — uncertain working son;
* [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] — uncertain working son;
* [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] — uncertain working son.

Daniel and Thomas are independently proved to have been brothers. Their shared attachment to Alexander and Rosanna remains unproved.

Useful remaining records include:

William Kennedy McKay, including a list of subscribers to Portglenone Temperance Society, 1831, and about seventy-five marriage licences at First Portglenone Presbyterian Meeting House, 1845–1856 (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>
* church, land and estate records capable of distinguishing the two Hugh Glasgow entries in 1740 and tracing the Hugh recorded in 1772;
* records identifying John and Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagavor family 34 and testing whether they connect with Inishrush, Kilrea, Daniel, Thomas or the younger Alexander;
* an independent copy or earlier version of the descendant family account;
* records identifying Alexander or Rosanna before 1822;
* a marriage, burial or estate record for Alexander and Rosanna;
* records naming the parents of Daniel or Thomas;

* contemporary records identifying James Shaw's relatives; and
* DNA evidence connecting documented descendants of Daniel, Thomas, the younger Alexander and any independently documented Inishrush line.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

Older Alexander is a reconstructed person in the Thomas and Daniel Glasgow family tradition, rather than a man yet identified by a contemporary record. The tradition naming Alexander and Rosanna as parents of Thomas supports retaining the couple as a working pair, while Daniel's will naming Thomas as brother supports the sibling group. It does not prove Alexander's ancestry or establish that younger [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] was their son rather than a possible brother or cousin. [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] should not be shown as Alexander's father: Adam's estimated 1758 birth and Rose's reported age make parentage chronologically strained, though collateral kinship remains possible. The Larne reconstruction makes [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] a possible older-generation source and older Alexander a coherent possible brother of Adam; no record yet joins them. The Thomas-parent tradition supports this working family, while its connection to Larne remains unproved.<ref name="OlderAlexanderCurrent">The cited family account and Daniel's will support the working sibling group; neither identifies Alexander's parents.</ref>

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Unknown Glasgow''' is a research placeholder for the unidentified father of '''Adam Glasgow''' of Inishrush, County Londonderry.

This profile does not represent a man identified in any surviving record. No baptism, marriage, will, gravestone, lease, census return, church record or other document found to date names Adam's father or establishes that Adam was a son or brother of any particular Glasgow family.

Unknown's given name, birth date, birthplace, residence, wife, religion, occupation and death are unknown.

=== Adam Glasgow of Inishrush ===

Adam Glasgow was born about 1758, calculated from his gravestone, and lived at Inishrush in the civil parish of Tamlaght O'Crilly, County Londonderry.

The 1831 census recorded '''Adam Glasco''' as head of Inishrush household 91. The household contained three males and five females, all Presbyterian. A separate '''John Glasco''' headed the other Glasgow household recorded at Inishrush. The census gives no ages or relationships between either household.<ref name="Census1831">[https://www.billmacafee.com/1831census/1831derrycensusnames.pdf William Macafee, ''Names of Householders Listed in the 1831 Census Returns for the County of Londonderry''], Tamlaght O'Crilly parish, Inishrush, Adam and John Glasco households (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

A transcription of the 1833 Tithe Applotment Book reportedly lists Adam as the only Glasgow occupier in Tamlaght O'Crilly parish. The original page has not yet been checked, so this should be treated as moderate-confidence evidence rather than a proved absence of other Glasgow occupiers.<ref name="Tithe1833">Tamlaght O'Crilly Tithe Applotment Book, 1833, transcription reviewed during the Glasgow-3905 research; original image not yet inspected.</ref>

Adam married '''Rose''', whose maiden surname is unknown. Their gravestone records:

* Rose Glasgow, wife of Adam, died 31 July 1833 aged 66;
* Adam Glasgow, died 30 June 1844 aged 86;
* their son James Glasgow, died 11 December 1878 aged 84;
* their daughter Eliza Glasgow, died aged 26;
* their grandson William Glasgow, died 21 November 1882 aged 27.<ref name="AdamGrave">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ "Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower Graveyard"], transcription and photograph of the Glasgow gravestone for Adam and Rose Glasgow (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

A marriage notice identifies '''Nancy Glasgow''' as Adam's sixth daughter. On 14 January 1842 she married John Kyle of Tyanee. The notice proves that Adam had at least six daughters but does not identify Nancy's mother or any of her sisters.<ref name="NancyMarriage">[https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/ "Marriage Notices 1840–42"], notice dated 29 January 1842 reporting the marriage of John Kyle of Tyanee and Nancy, sixth daughter of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Documented children of Adam include:

* '''James Glasgow''', born about 1794, named as Adam's son on the family gravestone;
* '''Eliza Glasgow''', named as Adam's daughter on the family gravestone;
* '''Nancy Glasgow''', identified in her marriage notice as Adam's sixth daughter;
* at least four further unidentified daughters.

The following people have been proposed as children but are not proved:

* an older '''Alexander Glasgow''', husband of Rosanna or Rose Ann Shaw;
* '''Daniel Glasgow''' of Kilrea, watch and clock maker.

Daniel Glasgow's 1871 will names David Glasgow of London as his son, Daniel Neely Glasgow as his nephew and Thomas Glasgow as his late brother. It does not name Adam, Rose, James, any Inishrush property or any relationship to the Inishrush family. Daniel should therefore not be described as Adam's probable son without further evidence.<ref name="DanielWill">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx PRONI Will Calendars], registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, 1871.</ref>

No record concerning Adam, Rose or their documented children names Adam's parents.

=== Earlier Glasgow households in Tamlaght O'Crilly ===

The strongest evidence for an earlier local Glasgow generation is the 1740 Protestant household return.

Two separate adult householders named '''Hugh Glasgow''' were recorded in Tamlaght O'Crilly parish. One Hugh entry appears immediately before Hugh Ellis and James McCullough in the collector's sequence and within a broader group containing surnames independently associated with Inishrush.

Both Hugh entries have their townland recorded as “Not specified”. Collector order can cross localities. Neither man can therefore be described as an Inishrush resident, and neither can be identified as Adam's father.<ref name="Hugh1740">[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf William Macafee, ''1740 Protestant Householders' Return'']; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/books/Kilrea/Kilrea07.html collector-order transcription for Tamlaght O'Crilly], surviving typescript PRONI T/808/15258 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Neither entry can represent the younger Hugh Glasgow represented by [[Glasgow-540]] under that man's broadly supported chronology. They instead establish that at least two earlier-generation Hugh Glasgow households existed in Adam's parish before his birth.

A newspaper notice dated 14 April 1772 names a '''Hugh Glasgow''' among inhabitants of Tamlaght O'Crilly parish who surrendered arms to Henry Ellis of Inishrush on 6 April. The notice does not say that Hugh lived at Inishrush, distinguish him from the two earlier householders or name any relative.<ref name="Hugh1772">[https://arborealis.ca/records/newspapers/kilrea-news/1770-1779/ ''Belfast News-Letter'' extracts for the Kilrea area], notice dated 14 April 1772 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

These records create a coherent local Hugh Glasgow cluster but do not establish that Hugh was the name of Adam's father.

=== Inishrush during Adam's lifetime ===

The Inishrush bleaching works were advertised for letting in 1758. In 1764 the Vintners or Conolly estate offered Inishrush, Inishrush Lile and other lands to solvent tenants from 1 November 1764. The Inishrush mill was offered again in 1792.

None of the notices names an incoming or outgoing Glasgow tenant. The 1764 reletting is nevertheless a significant research point because it occurred during Adam's childhood and may have generated leases or rentals identifying the household through which his family entered or remained at Inishrush.<ref name="InishrushNotices">[https://arborealis.ca/records/newspapers/kilrea-news/subject-index-1800/ Kilrea-area newspaper subject index and decade transcripts, 1750–1800]; specifically [https://arborealis.ca/records/newspapers/kilrea-news/1760-1769/ ''Belfast News-Letter'', 8 May 1764] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Reports concerning the Inishrush Volunteers in 1780 and a four-parish Protestant meeting in 1783 name only officers, donors or chairmen. They are not membership or attendance lists. The absence of Adam or another Glasgow from those reports is therefore not evidence that the family was absent.

A derivative abstract of a 1799 pro-Union declaration includes an '''Adam Glasco''' among County Londonderry subscribers. The abstract does not preserve the original signature order or state his residence. An occurrence of “Innishrush” elsewhere in the multi-column page is not attached to Adam. The entry cannot yet be identified securely as Adam Glasgow of Inishrush.<ref name="Union1799">[https://www.kinsleuth.com/belnews/1790-1800.htm ''Belfast News-Letter'' name and place abstracts, 27 September 1799] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Current Conclusion ===

Adam Glasgow's father has not been identified to a reliable genealogical standard.

The available evidence shows:

* two adult Hugh Glasgow householders in Adam's parish in 1740;
* a Hugh Glasgow somewhere in the same parish in 1772;
* Adam at Inishrush by the end of the eighteenth or early nineteenth century;
* several later Glasgow households in the surrounding district;
* no record stating a parent-child or sibling relationship between Adam and any of those men.

The earlier Hugh households are the best local lineage clue, but no individual candidate is proved.

=== Candidate Assessment ===

==== Earlier local Hugh Glasgow householders ====

'''Status: strongest local lineage cluster; individual identity unproved.'''

The two 1740 Hugh households are securely recorded in Tamlaght O'Crilly. One occurs in an Ellis and McCullough collector neighbourhood compatible with Inishrush-area records. The 1772 Hugh notice adds continuity of the name within the parish.

The records do not supply townlands, ages, wives, children or relationships. It is not possible to determine whether the Hugh named in 1772 was one of the 1740 householders, a son of one of them or another man.

Neither Hugh should be attached as Adam's father.

==== Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McCullough tradition ====

A late family history states that Hugh Glasgow married Margaret McCullough and had sons John, Robert and Hugh. It places the family on a farm near Portglenone and states that the younger Hugh was born in County Londonderry in 1739.

The Portglenone locality, McCullough surname, 1740 collector sequence and 1772 Ellis notice are geographically coherent. The account was, however, written about 160 years after the period described and contains chronological errors. It gives the alleged son Robert no birth, residence, wife, children, occupation or death.<ref name="HughTradition">[https://www.wikitree.com/photo.php/0/0a/Glasgow-590.pdf William Melanchthon Glasgow family history], six-page scan (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The tradition is a research lead, not proof that either Hugh was Adam's ancestor.

==== Younger Hugh Glasgow ====

'''Status: materially weakened as Adam's possible father.'''

Hugh “Glasgo” of Deer Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, signed his will on 29 March 1827. It was proved on 25 April 1831.

The will names:

* sons John, Hugh, Alexander and Robert;
* daughter Nancy;
* granddaughter Sarah, daughter of Alexander;
* an unnamed wife.

John and Robert were executors. Robert received the land and residue and was required to support his mother. Adam, who was alive in Ireland, was not named.<ref name="HughWill">Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, Will Book 3, no. 252, pp. 492–493, [https://www.ancestry.com/imageviewer/collections/8802/images/005537856_00276?pid=1733435 will-book image]; corresponding loose probate packet, FamilySearch DGS 5538049, images 239–243, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L991-GV6H?cc=1999196&wc=9PMK-MNG%3A268499101%2C281697201 packet cover] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Adam's omission while four sons received bequests is substantial adverse evidence against this Hugh being Adam's father.

It is not absolute exclusion. The will does not state that it names every child, and it also omits Clatworthy and Mary, who appear in the later seven-child family account.

No positive evidence connects younger Hugh to Adam.

==== Robert Glasgow, [[Glasgow-550]] ====

'''Status: chronologically possible but weak and undocumented locally.'''

The profile's estimated birth about 1737 in County Londonderry and death about 1787 are unsupported. No record found places this Robert at Inishrush or names Adam as his son.

Robert should not be substituted for Unknown Glasgow.

Two documented namesakes must be kept separate:

* Robert Glasgow of Killwaughter, County Antrim, was already an adult married leaseholder in February 1738. His wife was Rachel, formerly Wilson. He also witnessed a Larne-area lease in 1741. He cannot have been a child born about 1737.<ref name="KillwaughterRobert">Registry of Deeds memorials [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=74015 74015] and [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=76724 76724] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>
* A Robert Glasgow appointed surgeon on St Vincent in 1785 had previously served as an Army hospital mate in the West Indies. He exchanged to half-pay as an apothecary in 1791 and remained alive through at least 1825. A 1787 letter was addressed to his brother James at Beith, Scotland. This man cannot support the claimed 1787 death or an Irish connection for [[Glasgow-550]].<ref name="MilitaryRobert">[https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/DGZ-1785-4695 ''Dublin Gazette'', 13–15 December 1785, no. 4695]; [https://archive.org/details/rollofcommission00ande/page/61/mode/1up Johnston, ''Roll of Commissioned Officers in the Medical Service of the British Army'', 1917], p. 61 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== John Glasgow, [[Glasgow-549]] ====

'''Status: possible in late tradition; no relationship to Adam proved.'''

John is named in the late family account as a son of Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McCullough. No contemporary record links him to Adam.

An older Adam and Maria remain a naming-pattern hypothesis for John's parents. Applying that hypothesis to Adam of Inishrush depends on the unproved brotherhood; it supplies an alternative to test, not a record-identified parental couple.

=== John Glasgow, Born 1767 ===

The family Bible of [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] records:

* John Glasgow, born 10 April 1767;
* Mary Arthur, born 25 March 1774;
* their marriage on 21 May 1798;
* children Rose, Maria, Jane, Adam, Lavina, James, Margaret, John and Arthur.<ref name="JohnBible">[https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I368&tree=tree1 John Glasgow family page and Bible images], Bible printed in 1797 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

John's letter of 20 March 1847, written in Ohio to Jane Glasgow Gray, recalls family beekeeping at Inishrush. This proves John's own residence there.

The letter mentions receiving a letter from “Adam” on 27 December 1846. That correspondent cannot have been Adam Glasgow born about 1758, who died in 1844. John had a son Adam born in 1804, who is the more likely correspondent.

A separate letter from R. Mulhollan supplied Irish news concerning a James Glasgow. Nothing in the surviving wording states that John and James were brothers or identifies James by residence.<ref name="JohnLetter">[https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/documents/John%20Glasgow%20letter%20to%20Jane%20Glasgow%20Gray%203-20-1847.pdf John Glasgow to Jane Glasgow Gray, 20 March 1847], scan and transcript (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The Bible, letter, gravestone material, surviving child profiles, newspaper extracts, Reformed Presbyterian history and accessible United States probate indexes do not name John's parents, brother or Irish inheritance. Unavailable Guernsey County loose probate material remains an unresolved research route.

John may have been related to Adam, but no relationship should presently be attached.

=== DNA Evidence ===

The public Glasgow Y-DNA project attributes kit ''N18544'' to John Glasgow, born 1767.

Its published 67-marker result has a genetic distance of eight from kit ''254947'', attributed by its participant to a Robert Glasgow born about 1710. FamilyTreeDNA's stated genealogical matching limit at 67 markers is seven. John's kit is distance four at 37 markers from a line attributed to James Glasgow, born 1731, which is at the matching limit.<ref name="YDNA">[https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=ydna-results-overview Glasgow Y-DNA project]; [https://help.familytreedna.com/hc/en-us/articles/6019925167631-Understanding-Y-DNA-Genetic-Distance FamilyTreeDNA, “Understanding Y-DNA Genetic Distance”]; [https://www.legacytree.com/wp-content/uploads/T1508095.CLIENTGlasgow1508.report.public.pdf Legacy Tree Genealogists, public Glasgow Y-DNA report, 2016] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The earliest-ancestor labels are participant supplied. Neither comparison represents [[Glasgow-550]] or a proved strict male-line descendant of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush.

The published DNA evidence therefore cannot identify Adam's father.

=== Adam's Proposed and Later Family ===

==== James Glasgow ====

James is proved as Adam's son by the family gravestone.

James Glasgow of Inishrush, farmer, died in December 1878 aged 84. Henry Glasgow of Inishrush was present at the death. The return establishes Henry as a close household or family associate but does not state their relationship.<ref name="CivilDeaths">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/ IrishGenealogy.ie], civil death returns for James Glasgow of Inishrush, December 1878, and William Glasgow of Inishrush, 21 November 1882.</ref>

William Glasgow of Inishrush, a bachelor farmer aged 27, died on 21 November 1882. Lindsey Glasgow, described as William's brother, was present. William is the grandson named on Adam and Rose's gravestone, but the records inspected so far do not identify William and Lindsey's parents.

A different James Glasgow who married Sarah Barnett in 1848 was aged 25 and named his father as John Glasgow, farmer. He was born about 1823 and cannot be Adam's son James, born about 1794.

John Glasgow's 1847 letter relayed an Irish report that a James Glasgow was believed to have fathered an illegitimate child by his servant, an unnamed daughter of Henry Barkly.

The report does not:

* expressly identify James as James of Inishrush;
* name the servant;
* name the child;
* identify adult Henry Glasgow as the child;
* establish Rose Anne's maiden surname;
* prove any additional relationship within Adam's family.

Second Portglenone baptisms survive for 1821–1867 under PRONI ''MIC1P/357'', including the relevant 1845–1849 period, but the pages are not publicly available and have not been searched. No negative baptism conclusion can be drawn.

==== Nancy Glasgow ====

Nancy married John Kyle of Tyanee on 14 January 1842 and was explicitly Adam's sixth daughter.

The officiating minister, William Kennedy McKay, served First Portglenone. That congregation's surviving marriage register begins in 1845, after Nancy's marriage.

Current WikiTree profiles use estimated births around 1822, but no record found establishes Nancy's birth year, names her mother or identifies a child. No descendant should be attached without additional evidence.

==== Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea ====

Daniel's will proves that David Glasgow of London was his son and that Thomas Glasgow was his late brother. It also names his nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow.

It supplies no relationship to Adam or the Inishrush family. Daniel should remain detached from Adam unless a separate relational source is found.

=== Later Inishrush Land Succession ===

The Valuation Revision Books establish a later succession on Inishrush plot 29:

* James Glasgow occupied about 19 acres in the 1860–1863 volume;
* he remained the occupier in the 1864–1879 volume;
* the 1880–1883 book continued to carry James after his December 1878 death, showing administrative delay;
* James was then struck out;
* Rose Anne was inserted with an 1884 revision annotation and later struck out;
* Adam Glasgow was inserted with an 1893 annotation;
* Adam was the sole named occupier in the 1899–1910 volume.

The area remained 19 acres, 2 roods and 10 perches. This strongly establishes occupation succession from James to Rose Anne to the later Adam, but the valuation books do not state their relationships.<ref name="Valuation">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx PRONI Valuation Revision Books], VAL/12/B/34/10A–E, Inishrush plot 29 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The 1901 and 1911 censuses record a later Adam Glasgow and Eliza at Inishrush with United States-born sons Adam D. and Henry. The 1911 return states that five children had been born and two remained living. These records create a Philadelphia research route for family papers and vital records, but do not by themselves connect the later Adam to Adam born about 1758.<ref name="LaterCensus">[https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/ National Archives of Ireland, 1901 and 1911 census search], Inishrush Glasgow households (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The 1929 Bellaghy Estate Land Purchase Commission schedule lists five current Inishrush holdings under Patrick McLaughlin, Francis Diamond and Joseph McLaughlin. No Glasgow was then listed. This shows only that the later plot-29 occupation had ended before the 1929 sale.<ref name="LandPurchase1929">[https://billmacafee.com/estates/bellaghy/lpcsbellaghyestate1929.pdf Land Purchase Commission sale schedule for the Bellaghy Estate, 1929] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

=== Inishrush Estate and Deed Evidence ===

The 1734 Inishrush head lease and later eighteenth-century deed indexes name Ellis, Conolly, Wilson, Bay, McCleland, Huey and others, but no Glasgow as a principal party. This is only qualified negative evidence because subtenants and some witnesses may be omitted from memorials.<ref name="Deed57951">[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=57951 Registry of Deeds memorial 57951] and associated Inishrush townland-index searches (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

A 1950 study of the rundale system reports that Inishrush retained intermixed partnership holdings. The author's Inishrush informant had seen an 1801 joint lease covering part of the townland and naming the Hill, Hastings, Neill and Brattan families.

That lease did not name a Glasgow, but it covered only part of Inishrush. Families could occupy intermixed shares or hold below the head-lease level. It is not a census and does not prove that Adam was absent.<ref name="Rundale">[https://pureadmin.qub.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/364690144/The_rundale_system_in_Ireland.pdf Desmond McCourt, ''The Rundale System in Ireland'', Queen's University Belfast PhD thesis, 1950], p. 146 and Appendix B.IV no. 7 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

PRONI ''T877/216'', dated 1 December 1800, is Thomas Conolly's renewable-for-ever lease to Joseph Courtney of the Inishrush mill and seven plantation acres at £10 5s rent. It is a distinct mill holding, not the 1801 four-family partnership lease. The catalogue description names no Glasgow, although the undigitised deed may contain unnamed lives or witnesses.

Registry memorial ''193/462/128477'' is a securely localised unread lead because the townland index records “Innishrushe + mill” and an Ellis-to-Dobbyn transaction. Memorial ''215/276/141741'' has a conflicting secondary-index citation. Memorial ''393/423/260245'' has not been localised. None currently identifies Adam or his father.

=== Other Local Glasgow Households ===

==== Margaret Glasgow of Tyanee ====

A Kilrea First Presbyterian marriage entry dated 6 October 1825 identifies Mary Patton as the daughter of John Patton and his wife '''Margaret Glasgow''' of Tyanee, associated with the Portglenone congregation.

John Patton remained a Tyanee householder in the 1831 census and a tithe occupier in 1833. The surviving Portglenone register window does not identify Margaret's parents or marriage.

No cemetery, newspaper, census-substitute or descendant record inspected so far connects Margaret to Adam. She should not be attached as Adam's daughter or sister.<ref name="Patton1825">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Marriages/1825.html Kilrea First Presbyterian marriage-register transcript], entry dated 6 October 1825; [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-search-forms-1841-and-1851/ National Archives of Ireland census-search collection guide; former legacy detail ID 41311] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== Robert Glasgow of Coltrim ====

A published report states that “Robt. Glasco, Coltrim” discovered an ancient ladle mill there in 1818. The 1827 Lissan tithe book lists Robert Glasgow at Coltrim, and the 1831 census records a Robert heading an eleven-person Presbyterian household there.

The tithe book separately lists another Robert Glasgow at Drumnabragy and John Glasgow at Drumeen. Exact townland identification is therefore essential.

The Coltrim records establish continuity for one later Robert but provide no age or relationship to Adam. He must not be merged with [[Glasgow-550]].<ref name="ColtrimRobert">Colin Rynne, ''Industrial Archaeology Review'' 33:2 (2011), citing W. E. Hogg, p. 295; Lissan Tithe Applotment Book, 1827, PRONI FIN 5A/203; 1831 census of County Londonderry.</ref>

==== Robert Glasgow of Lisnagaver ====

A '''Robert Glasgow''' was recorded immediately after an Alexander Glasgow at Lisnagaver in the 1834 Tithe Applotment transcription.<ref name="Tithe1834">William Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrim.pdf ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering North Antrim''], Rasharkin parish, records 7501–7502, Alexander and Robert Glasgow at Lisnagaver (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The tithe record gives no age, wife or relationship.

Robert may have been:

* a brother or other relative of Adam;
* a son of Adam;
* a brother or relative of the older Alexander Glasgow;
* the father of John and Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagaver;
* or an unrelated member of the wider Glasgow population.

None of these arrangements is proved.

If a profile is created, it should be separate and unconnected, described only as:

:'''Robert Glasgow, born before about 1773, living at Lisnagaver in 1834.'''

His parents, wife and children should remain unlinked.

==== John and Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagaver ====

The surviving 1851 census records [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], aged about 50, farming at Lisnagaver. His unmarried brother '''Samuel Glasgow''', aged about 60, lived in the same household.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf "1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription"], Lisnagaver households 34–37, p. 183 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Their approximate births were:

* Samuel Glasgow — about 1790 or 1791;
* John Glasgow — about 1800 or 1801.

The same census cluster included:

* Alexander Glasgow, born about 1810 or 1811;
* Thomas Glasgow, born about 1815 or 1816.

John, Alexander and Thomas were later recorded as occupiers at Lisnagaver.

Possible arrangements include:

* Robert Glasgow of Lisnagaver as father of John and Samuel;
* an older Alexander as father of the younger Alexander and Thomas;
* Robert and the older Alexander as brothers or close relatives;
* John, Samuel, Alexander and Thomas as brothers.

No arrangement has been proved. John and Samuel should not be attached as children of Robert, Adam, the older Alexander or Unknown Glasgow.

==== Separate Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie ====

The Robert recorded at Lisnagaver in 1834 must not be confused with [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] of Glenleslie.

The Glenleslie Robert was born about 1779 and lived with [[Unknown-540856|Catherine]]. Their 1851 household included:

* Margaret Glasgow, born about 1801;
* John Glasgow, born about 1811 and absent in America;
* Samuel Glasgow, born about 1821 and absent in America.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf "1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription"], Glenleslie household of Robert and Catherine Glasgow (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The Glenleslie Robert cannot have been the father of Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagaver, born about 1791, because Robert would have been only about twelve.

The Glenleslie John and Samuel were approximately ten and thirty years younger than the Lisnagaver brothers. These are separate families and should not be merged.

==== Separate Kilrea-to-Ontario Cluster ====

A merchant Samuel Glasgow who died at Prescott, Ontario, is very strongly the man described as formerly of Kilrea and as having emigrated in 1831.

A later local title-chain account calls a shipbuilder Robert Glasgow, who died in 1856, Samuel's father. No original record inspected so far states that relationship.

No evidence connects the Prescott Robert or Samuel to Adam, Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, [[Glasgow-550]] or any proposed son of Adam. This cluster should remain separate.

=== Church Record Limitations ===

The surviving Drimbolg or Drumbolg material consists of:

* baptisms beginning in 1895;
* marriages beginning in 1864;
* a session or discipline book covering 1809–1859;
* committee minutes beginning in 1887.

No surviving Drimbolg baptism register can record Adam's birth about 1758.

A published church-history extract names John Glasgow at congregational sessions in 1809 and 1827. It is not a transcript or membership list, and John's appearance does not establish a relationship to Adam.<ref name="DrimbolgRecords">[https://www.billmacafee.com/churchrecords/churchrecordsderry.pdf County Londonderry church-record inventory], Drumbolg or Drimbolg entry, PRONI MIC1C/15 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

The 1831 Reformed Presbyterian Synod roll names James Smyth as Drimbolg's minister and Samuel McEwen as its delegate elder. No Glasgow appears. A synod roll records delegates rather than every congregational elder or member, so this is not evidence that John or Adam was absent from the congregation.<ref name="Synod1831">[https://archive.org/details/rpci-minutes-of-synod-1831 Reformed Presbyterian Church of Ireland, ''Minutes of Synod'', 1831] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

=== Record-Coverage Limitations and Negative Searches ===

==== 1766 Religious Census ====

The surviving County Londonderry returns cover ten named parishes but omit Tamlaght O'Crilly, Kilrea, Lissan and Maghera.

The collection cannot determine whether either 1740 Hugh household survived, identify an adult Adam or Robert or test whether the Glasgow family remained in the target parish. A missing result is archival non-coverage, not evidence of absence.<ref name="Coverage1766">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/discover/census-land-and-surveys/census/ireland-1766-religious-census Findmypast, “Ireland, 1766 Religious Census”]; [https://www.rootsireland.ie/derry-genealogy/derry-census-substitutes/ Roots Ireland, County Derry census-substitute coverage]; [https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/research-guides/religious-census-1766/ National Archives of Ireland research guide] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== 1775 Dissenters' Petitions ====

The surviving Tenison Groves transcripts cover selected Ulster places, including Coleraine or Killowen and Londonderry city, but not Tamlaght O'Crilly, Kilrea or the Drimbolg congregation.

This collection cannot test the local Glasgow households. A missing surname result is not evidence of absence.<ref name="Coverage1775">[https://www.findmypast.ie/discover/census-land-and-surveys/census/ireland-1775-dissenters-petitions Findmypast, “Ireland, 1775 Dissenters' Petitions”]; PRONI T808/15307 and PRONI Names index (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== Virtual Record Treasury ====

Exact-name, spelling-variant and place searches of the Virtual Record Treasury found:

* the already-known 1831 Adam Glasco census return;
* the two known 1740 Hugh Glasgow households;
* unrelated namesakes and place references;
* early Inishrush probate-index residents John Clark in 1696, James Dobbin in 1718, William Bay in 1734 and Henry Ellis in 1791.

No indexed record names Adam's father or links a candidate Robert to Inishrush.

This is a bounded search of the Treasury's reconstructed and indexed corpus. It does not cover undigitised estate rentals, all PRONI church books or every destroyed record.<ref name="VRT">[https://virtualtreasury.ie/ Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland], exact-name, variant and Inishrush searches completed 17 July 2026.</ref>

==== Freeholder Records ====

PRONI's indexed pre-1840 freeholder database returned Glasgow entries at Killycurrough, Drumgreenagh, Drumcon, Goston, Loy, Lislea, Craigs and Oritor.

It returned no Adam, Glasco, Glasgo or Glascow. The only County Londonderry result was John Glasgow of Drumcon, whose original entry names no relative or lease life.

A separate address search produced no Inishrush result. The database therefore does not adequately cover the target place, and Adam's absence cannot be used to infer that he held no freehold.<ref name="Freeholders">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/freeholders/default.aspx PRONI Freeholders Records], Glasgow and Inishrush variant searches, including D/834/1 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== Registry of Deeds Indexes ====

Exact and variant surname searches for 1700–1850 returned no indexed County Londonderry or Inishrush Robert Glasgow.

The volunteer index is incomplete and may omit subtenants and other subsidiary parties. This is a qualified negative only.<ref name="DeedsSearch">[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/search/index.php Registry of Deeds Index Project], Glasgow surname and variant searches, 1700–1850 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== Probate ====

The PRONI online will calendar returned no probate abstract for Adam, James, Henry or A. D. Glasgow of Inishrush.

This leaves no online probate statement of the earlier family relationships. It does not establish that no will, administration or destroyed probate record ever existed.

==== Newspapers ====

Searchable Londonderry Sentinel marriage-notice transcriptions for 1829–1849 returned Nancy's 1842 marriage as the only target-family notice.

The newspaper began in September 1829, and the online pages are selected derivative transcriptions rather than complete registers. They cannot identify all of Adam's daughters or prove that no other notice existed.<ref name="SentinelMarriages">[https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriage-notices-1829-1831/ Londonderry Sentinel marriage-notice transcriptions, 1829–1849] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Other newspaper abstracts and public title searches produced no inspectable report naming Adam's father, brother, birthplace or earlier residence. Commercial July 1844 newspaper runs and the relevant Coleraine Chronicle material were inaccessible and were not treated as negative results.

==== PRONI T1762 ====

The collection titled “Glasgow family and Presbyterian papers”, ''T1762'', is not an Inishrush Glasgow family archive.

Its six-item hierarchy contains only one surname item: ''T1762/5'', a solicitor's copy of the will and codicil of William Glasgow, farmer of Oritor, County Tyrone, concerning Oritor lands. The remaining items concern unrelated Presbyterian or personal papers.

No item description names Adam, Inishrush, Tamlaght O'Crilly or a candidate father.<ref name="T1762">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/ PRONI eCatalogue], T1762 hierarchy and T1762/5 description (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

==== NAI Rebellion Papers ====

National Archives of Ireland packet ''620/42/15'' concerns “Glasco” bills, accounts and financial material dated 1764–1798.

The fuller catalogue context includes Mary Lynch's assignment of Trinity Lane premises to Abraham Taylor, suggesting a Dublin commercial setting. The description supplies no Glasco forename, County Londonderry location, occupation or relationship.

It must not be connected to the Inishrush family without inspection of the full calendar or microfilm.

==== Census Search Forms ====

Four public Inishrush census-search results were located under the surnames Courtney, McAtomney and Wilson.

The result metadata does not expose household members, parents or the census year searched, and the detailed records were not retrievable. Northern forms also survive separately at PRONI.

These remain collateral leads because a pension search form may identify an applicant's claimed parents or childhood household. They are not evidence that no Glasgow appeared in the surviving forms.<ref name="CensusForms">[https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-search-forms-1841-and-1851/ National Archives of Ireland Census Search Forms collection guide], Inishrush search results and associated PRONI coverage review (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

=== Relationship Settings ===

Recommended WikiTree treatment:

* Adam Glasgow — attach only as '''uncertain son''';
* Unknown spouse — leave blank;
* birth date — preferably blank; otherwise “before 1758”, marked uncertain;
* birthplace — leave blank;
* death date and place — leave blank;
* religion and occupation — leave blank;
* earlier Hugh Glasgow householders — do not attach;
* [[Glasgow-540|younger Hugh Glasgow]] — do not attach;
* [[Glasgow-550|Robert Glasgow]] — do not attach;
* [[Glasgow-549|John Glasgow]] — do not attach;
* Robert Glasgow of Lisnagaver — do not attach;
* John and Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagaver — do not attach;
* Margaret Glasgow of Tyanee — do not attach;
* Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea — do not attach as Adam's son without further evidence.

=== Evidence Limitations ===

This profile represents an unidentified generation rather than a documented person.

No record currently establishes:

* Unknown's given name;
* his birth or birthplace;
* his wife;
* his residence;
* his religion;
* his occupation;
* his death;
* that either 1740 Hugh Glasgow was Adam's father;
* that the Hugh named in 1772 was one of the 1740 householders;
* that Adam and John Glasgow, born 1767, were brothers;
* that Adam and Robert Glasgow were brothers;
* that Robert was the father of John and Samuel of Lisnagaver;
* that Adam, Robert or an older Alexander shared the same father;
* that Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea was Adam's son;
* that the proposed older Alexander was Adam's son.

The strongest available evidence concerns local Glasgow households and Adam's later descendants, not Unknown himself.

=== Interpretive Cautions ===

Do not:

* name Hugh, Robert, John or an inferred Adam and Maria couple as Adam's parents;
* describe either 1740 Hugh as an Inishrush resident;
* call younger Hugh conclusively excluded solely because Adam was omitted from his will;
* use the absence of Glasgow entries from the 1766 census or 1775 petitions as evidence, because the surviving collections do not cover the parish;
* infer that a Glasgow obtained an Inishrush lease merely because the townland was advertised in 1764;
* treat the four surnames on the reported 1801 lease as a complete list of Inishrush residents;
* treat the 1780 Volunteers notice or 1783 meeting report as a roster;
* call Adam an Inishrush signatory in 1799;
* infer Unknown's name from the names of Adam's proposed sons;
* create a child of James from the 1847 report;
* identify Henry Glasgow as that child;
* assign Rose Anne the Barkly maiden surname;
* claim that the Second Portglenone baptism register has been searched;
* attach Margaret Glasgow of Tyanee to Adam;
* interpret John's 1847 “Adam” correspondent as Adam born about 1758;
* apply the current Y-DNA comparison to Adam or [[Glasgow-550]];
* use the 1831 synod delegate roll as a complete membership list;
* identify the West Indian Army medical officer as [[Glasgow-550]];
* identify the married Killwaughter leaseholder as [[Glasgow-550]];
* use the freeholder database to claim that Adam held no freehold;
* merge the Lisnagaver, Glenleslie, Coltrim, Killwaughter, Prescott or military families without a relational record.

=== Further Research ===

The most useful remaining research targets are:

* inspect PRONI ''D1062/1/16'' and ''VAL/2/B/5/40C'', the 1858–1859 Inishrush map and field-book targets;
* inspect surviving Vintners or Conolly estate rentals ''D2094/50–51'', ''D2094/75–78'' and ''T2825/C/19/1–13'' for tenancy succession between 1775 and 1801;
* inspect Hercules Ellis's 1750 will, PRONI ''T597/3'';
* inspect the Drimbolg session or discipline book, PRONI ''MIC1C/15'', covering 1809–1859;
* inspect Second Portglenone baptisms for 1845–1849, PRONI ''MIC1P/357'', Coleraine reel 179;
* obtain the original 1833 Tamlaght O'Crilly Tithe Applotment page;
* inspect Registry memorial ''193/462/128477'';
* verify or discard memorial ''215/276/141741'';
* localise memorial ''393/423/260245'';
* inspect the unresolved Inishrush census-search forms held by the National Archives and PRONI;
* search the Philadelphia branch for birth, church, passenger, obituary and family-paper records;
* obtain the unresolved Guernsey County loose probate material for John Glasgow's family;
* search marriage records naming the fathers of John Glasgow of Lisnagaver and other members of the local cluster;
* search valuation-revision books for succession to the Lisnagaver holdings;
* investigate Thomas Glasgow and Daniel Neely Glasgow through Daniel of Kilrea's will;
* continue cemetery and estate searches in Tamlaght O'Crilly, Kilrea, Rasharkin and nearby Portglenone congregations.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

This profile remains an explicitly uncertain placeholder for an unidentified father of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] of Inishrush; it is not a second, record-identified man. The Larne model makes [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] a concrete possible older-generation candidate, but does not establish that James fathered Adam. The 1762 marriage to Janet Shutter is later than Adam's estimated 1758 birth, so it supplies no basis for attaching Janet as Adam's mother. Two Hugh Glasgow householders in Tamlaght O'Crilly in 1740 and the later parish Hugh are separate local leads; neither is Adam's documented father. John of Inishrush may be Adam's brother or another collateral relation, but the 1831 list names no relationship. The profile should retain only uncertain relationships until a baptism, estate, deed, church record, or comparable contemporary evidence identifies Adam's parent.<ref name="PlaceholderCurrent">The records cited in the preceding research notes identify relevant households and localities but contain no parental statement for Adam.</ref>
