50918453.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Daniel Glasgow''' was born about 1795 or 1796 in Ireland. He became a
watchmaker and farmer at Kilrea, County Londonderry. His original death return
records that he died there on 16 October 1871, aged seventy-five, a widower and
watchmaker. Kate Glasgow was present at his death.<ref name="Death1871">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], Daniel Glasgow, Kilrea, 16 October 1871.</ref>

Daniel was probably married to Margaret Irwin. A Rasharkin Presbyterian
baptismal record identifies Robert, born in 1827, as a child of Daniel Glasgow
and Margaret Irwin.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian register transcription and associated earlier entries], original register PRONI MIC1P/292.</ref>

The known or probable children are:

* [[Glasgow-3897|Robert Glasgow]], baptised in 1827;
* [[Glasgow-3898|James Glasgow]], an artist whose 1853 death notice called him Daniel's third son;
* [[Glasgow-3900|Daniel Glasgow junior]], a probable son identified by the local junior designation and chronology; and
* [[Glasgow-3899|David Glasgow]], directly identified as Daniel's son in Daniel's will.<ref name="JamesDeath">[https://www.cotyrone.com/colondonderry/burial/CoLondonderry-DeathsSentinel-G-1829-1869.html ''Londonderry Sentinel'' death notices], James Glasgow, died Brooklyn, 21 January 1853.</ref><ref name="DanielJuniorDeath">[https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/016800/016836/images/crayon_apr1858_1.pdf ''The Crayon'', April 1858], obituary of Daniel Glasgow junior.</ref>

Daniel's will, proved in 1871, names his son David, his late brother Thomas
Glasgow and his nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow.<ref name="Will1871">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Will Calendars], registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871.</ref> Daniel Neely's 1888 marriage names his father as [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]], farmer, and places him at Lisnagaver.<ref name="DanielNeelyMarriage">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1888/10763/5925382.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Daniel Neely Glasgow and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888.</ref> Together the records prove that Daniel and Thomas were brothers.

=== Parents ===

A descendant family account identifies [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-761034|Rosanna, surname unknown]] as the parents of Thomas Glasgow of Lisnagaver.<ref name="GenesReunitedGlasgow">Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', Find Ancestors message board, posted 25 January 2007, with replies dated 9 April 2020, https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Daniel's original will explicitly calls Thomas his brother.<ref name="DanielWill1871">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], original registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref> If the descendant account correctly identifies Thomas's parents, Alexander and Rosanna are therefore plausible parents of Daniel as well.

No contemporary record inspected directly names Daniel's parents. Alexander and Rosanna should remain attached as '''uncertain parents'''. The evidence does not exclude a half-sibling relationship, an error in the descendant account or another reconstruction of the family.

Rosanna's surname has not been identified. No inspected source supports the surname Shaw.

=== Margaret Irwin ===

The Kilrea First Presbyterian baptism register names '''Daniel Glasgow and Margaret Irwin of Kilrea''' as the parents of their son Robert. Robert was born on 1 September 1827 and baptised on 30 September.<ref name="KilreaBaptism1827">Richard John Torrens, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1827.html "Kilrea First Presbyterian Church Records: Baptisms in 1827"], entry 146, transcribed by Barbara Braswell: Robert, son of Daniel Glasgow and Margaret Irwin of Kilrea, born 1 September and baptised 30 September 1827 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The transcription does not expressly call Margaret Daniel's wife, but they were probably married. Daniel was described as a widower when he died in 1871.<ref name="DanielDeath1871">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cide-7256058 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil death registration of Daniel Glasgow, Kilrea, 16 October 1871: aged 75, widower, watchmaker; Peter Glasgow of Kilrea present at death (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Margaret may be attached as Daniel's '''uncertain spouse'''. Their marriage date and place are unknown.

=== Children ===

Known or probable children of Daniel included:

* '''[[Glasgow-3899|David Glasgow]]''', born at Coleraine in 1824 and later a prominent watchmaker in London. Daniel's will explicitly described David Glasgow of the City of London as '''“my son”''' and left him the residue of the estate.<ref name="DanielWill1871" /><ref name="DavidGlasgow">British Museum, [https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/term/BIOG70412 "David Glasgow"], biographical record stating that David was born at Coleraine in 1824, became a watchmaker and died on 7 December 1911 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref> David's mother has not been identified.
* '''[[Glasgow-3897|Robert Glasgow]]''', born on 1 September 1827 and baptised at Kilrea on 30 September, son of Daniel Glasgow and Margaret Irwin.<ref name="KilreaBaptism1827" />
* '''[[Glasgow-3898|James Glasgow]]''', an artist who died at Brooklyn, New York, on 21 January 1853, in the twenty-fifth year of his age. His death notice described him as the '''third son''' of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea.<ref name="JamesDeath1853">[https://www.cotyrone.com/colondonderry/burial/CoLondonderry-DeathsSentinel-G-1829-1869.html ''Londonderry Sentinel'' death notices], notice published 18 February 1853: James Glasgow, artist, died at Brooklyn, New York, on 21 January 1853 and was described as the third son of Mr Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref> James's mother has not been identified.
* '''[[Glasgow-3900|Daniel Glasgow, Jr.]]''', a water-colour artist who died at Kilrea on 29 January 1858 from consumption, in the twenty-fourth year of his age. The use of “Jr.” and the shared residence make him a probable son of Daniel, but no inspected record explicitly names his father.<ref name="DanielJrDeath1858">[https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc3500/sc3520/016800/016836/images/crayon_apr1858_1.pdf ''The Crayon''], April 1858, p. 118, report of the death of Daniel Glasgow, Jr., at Kilrea on 29 January 1858 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

David, Robert and James account for three sons born before the younger Daniel. The previously proposed unidentified elder son is therefore not required.

Margaret Irwin is proved as Robert's mother. She may also have been the mother of Daniel's other children, but no inspected source establishes that relationship.

=== Occupation and property ===

Daniel was recorded as a watch and clock maker at Kilrea in 1846.<ref name="Slater1846">J. Slater, [https://www.failteromhat.com/slater/0192.pdf ''Slater's National Commercial Directory of Ireland''] (1846), Kilrea, p. 473, “Watch & Clock Makers”, listing “Glasco Daniel” (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Griffith's Valuation records Daniel Glasgow at Church Street, Kilrea, and at Claragh in Kilrea civil parish.<ref name="GriffithKilrea">Fáilte Romhat, [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/derry/kilrea.php "Griffith's Valuation of Ireland — Kilrea, County Derry"], entries for Daniel Glasgow at Church Street, Kilrea, and Claragh (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

The probate calendar later described Daniel as a farmer, while his death registration called him a watchmaker.<ref name="DanielDeath1871" /><ref name="Probate1871">National Archives of Ireland, ''Calendar of Wills and Administrations'', former online reel 005014889, image 00435 ([https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/types-of-research/how-to-find-a-will/ current National Archives guide to wills]), entry for Daniel Glasgow, late of Kilrea, County Londonderry, farmer, who died at Kilrea on 16 October 1871; will proved by Samuel Neely, sole executor; effects under £300 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

He may have combined watchmaking with farming or held agricultural land later in life.

Griffith's Valuation also lists men named Daniel Glasgow and Robert Glasgow at Gortereghy in Rasharkin parish. The Daniel entry probably refers to the Kilrea watchmaker and farmer, but the name-only valuation entry does not directly establish his identity.<ref name="GriffithRasharkin">Fáilte Romhat, [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/rasharkin.htm "Griffith's Valuation of Ireland — Rasharkin, County Antrim"], entries for Daniel and Robert Glasgow at Gortereghy (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

PRONI valuation revision books place Robert Glasgow at Gortereghy house 18c in about 1864–1865. The adjoining house 18b was occupied by Daniel McCochrane, not Daniel Glasgow.<ref name="GortereghyRevision">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Valuation Revision Books'', VAL/12/B/4/17A and VAL/12/B/4/17B, Gortereghy, Rasharkin parish.</ref>

The Robert at Gortereghy was probably [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]], proved son of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], rather than Daniel's son Robert. If Alexander was Daniel's brother, Robert would have been Daniel's nephew. Neither the proposed sibling relationship nor the interpretation of the Gortereghy entries has been proved.

The records do not establish that Daniel and Robert occupied adjoining houses or that they were father and son.

=== Brother Thomas and the Lisnagaver family ===

Daniel's original will refers to '''“my late brother Thomas Glasgow”''' and leaves a legacy to his nephew '''Daniel Neely Glasgow'''.<ref name="DanielWill1871" />

Daniel Neely Glasgow married Mary Jane Boyd at Boveedy First Presbyterian Church on 28 June 1888. He was described as a farmer of Lisnagaver and named his father as '''Thomas Glasgow, farmer'''.<ref name="DanielNeelyMarriage1888">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/ IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of Daniel Neely Glasgow and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church; groom's father recorded as Thomas Glasgow, farmer (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Together these records establish that:

* Daniel had a brother named Thomas;
* Daniel Neely Glasgow was Daniel's nephew;
* Daniel Neely's father was Thomas Glasgow; and
* the family was connected with Lisnagaver.

The two-record evidence chain identifies Daniel's brother as [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow of Lisnagaver]]. Thomas may be attached as Daniel's '''certain brother'''.

A Thomas Glasgow aged 55 was registered in the Ballymoney district during the second quarter of 1870. The age and district fit Thomas of Lisnagaver, who was described as Daniel's late brother in 1871, but the original civil register image is unavailable. The index entry alone does not conclusively identify him or name his parents.<ref name="ThomasDeath1870">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cidenc-772683 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil death index entry for Thomas Glasgow, aged 55, Ballymoney registration district, second quarter of 1870 (accessed 19 July 2026).</ref>

=== Possible brother Alexander ===

[[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] of the Lisnagaver and Rasharkin area may also have been Daniel's brother.

The proposed relationship is supported by locality, connections with Thomas's family and the probable Gortereghy link, but no inspected record explicitly calls Alexander and Daniel brothers. Alexander should therefore remain attached, if at all, as an '''uncertain brother'''.

Daniel, Thomas and Alexander form a probable Bann Valley–Killoquin or Kilrea–Rasharkin family cluster. Only Daniel's relationship to Thomas is directly proved.

=== Death and will ===

Daniel died at Kilrea on '''16 October 1871''', aged 75. His death registration described him as a widower and watchmaker.<ref name="DanielDeath1871" />

His recorded age gives an estimated birth in about 1795 or 1796. It does not provide an exact birth date.

A derivative index was previously read as naming Peter Glasgow at Daniel's death. The original civil image instead clearly names '''Kate Glasgow''', present at death, Kilrea. It states no relationship, so Kate should not be attached as a daughter or other relative without further evidence.<ref name="Death1871" />

Daniel's will was proved at Londonderry by Samuel Neely of Kilrea, assistant land agent and sole executor. His effects were valued at under £300.<ref name="Probate1871" />

The original will named:

* David Glasgow of the City of London, '''his son''';
* Thomas Glasgow, '''his late brother'''; and
* Daniel Neely Glasgow, '''his nephew'''.<ref name="DanielWill1871" />

The will does not name Adam Glasgow, Rose Glasgow, James Glasgow of Inishrush or any property at Inishrush. This omission does not prove that Daniel had no connection with that family, but the will provides no support for attaching him as a son of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush.

Daniel's burial place has not been identified.

The original death image identifies Kate Glasgow as the informant.<ref name="Death1871" />

The only Kate active in Ireland at this time was [[Glasgow-1571|Catherine Glasgow]]

=== Brother Thomas and the Prescott siblings ===

Daniel's will calls [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] his late brother and Daniel Neely Glasgow his nephew.<ref name="DanielWill1871" /> Daniel Neely's 1888 marriage calls his father Thomas Glasgow, farmer, of Lisnagaver, which identifies the brother as Thomas of Lisnagaver.<ref name="DanielNeelyMarriage1888">Ireland civil marriage return, Daniel Neely Glasgow and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1888/10763/5925382.pdf original image] (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Original Grenville deeds under the will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott independently identify Daniel's connection. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, names Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas as Robert's brothers; Mary and the children of brother James complete the six shares, but the will does not call James deceased.<ref name="RobertWill1849">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image].</ref> Memorial 13 records the 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, involving Robert's widow Jane and Samuel Glasgow, merchant, in Samuel's one undivided sixth share.<ref name="RobertWill1856">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image].</ref> Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, transferring two undivided sixth interests to Samuel under Robert's will.<ref name="RobertWill1861">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image].</ref> These deeds establish Daniel, Thomas, Samuel and Robert as brothers by their stated places, trades and wives. They do not identify their parents.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] and Rosanna Unknown are retained as uncertain
parents. A descendant account identifies them as Thomas's parents; because
Daniel's will proves Thomas was Daniel's brother, they are plausible parents of
Daniel as well.<ref name="DescendantAccount">[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited''], descendant account posted 25 January 2007.</ref> No contemporary record inspected names Daniel's parents. Rosanna's reported Shaw surname has not been proved.

Daniel's death age corrects his estimated birth from about 1807 to about
1795/96. That change also requires the proposed parents to be born earlier than
previous estimates. [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and Rose should not be placed
above this family; Rose's age excludes her as the older Alexander's mother.

[[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] is a probable brother of Daniel
and Thomas, not a proved one. The local cluster and Y-DNA support common paternal
kinship, but no found record states the relationship.

==== Additional sources consulted ====
The review retained the [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1827.html 1827 Kilrea baptism transcription], [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/derry/kilrea.php Griffith's Valuation for Kilrea], [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/rasharkin.htm Griffith's Valuation for Rasharkin], [https://www.failteromhat.com/slater/0192.pdf Slater's directory] and the [https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/term/BIOG70412 British Museum biographical entry]. Civil and probate searches included [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/ IrishGenealogy.ie], the retained [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cide-7256058 death result] and [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cidenc-772683 Thomas death result], together with the former online probate-calendar image (reel 005014889, image 00435) and the [https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/types-of-research/how-to-find-a-will/ current National Archives guide to wills]. They do not identify Daniel's parents.

=== Recommended relationships ===

* '''[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]]''' — uncertain father, based on a descendant account concerning Thomas and the proved Daniel–Thomas brotherhood;
* '''[[Unknown-761034|Rosanna, surname unknown]]''' — uncertain mother on the same derivative evidence;
* '''Margaret Irwin''' — uncertain spouse;
* '''[[Glasgow-3899|David Glasgow]]''' — certain son of Daniel; mother unknown;
* '''[[Glasgow-3897|Robert Glasgow]]''' — certain son of Daniel and Margaret;
* '''[[Glasgow-3898|James Glasgow]]''' — certain son of Daniel; mother unknown;
* '''[[Glasgow-3900|Daniel Glasgow, Jr.]]''' — probable or uncertain son;
* '''[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]''' — certain brother;
* '''[[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]''' — probable or uncertain brother;
* '''Daniel Neely Glasgow''' — certain nephew through Thomas;
* '''Kate Glasgow''' — death informant; relationship unknown.

=== Register coverage ===

The surviving First Kilrea Presbyterian baptism register begins on 17 April 1825, about thirty years after Daniel's estimated birth. It therefore cannot contain Daniel's own baptism.

A search of the available 1825–1859 baptism transcription found only the known 1827 baptism of Robert, son of Daniel and Margaret. The transcribed 1825–1845 marriage pages contain no marriage for Daniel Glasgow.

These are bounded transcription negatives. They do not exclude:

* a spelling or transcription error;
* a marriage or baptism in another congregation;
* an event before the surviving register begins; or
* an event that was not recorded.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* Daniel and Margaret Irwin's marriage;
* earlier Kilrea, Killoquin and neighbouring Presbyterian records;
* the original 1827 baptism entry for Robert;
* records identifying the mothers of David, James and Daniel Jr.;
* further contemporary records for Daniel Glasgow Jr.;
* the original Griffith's Valuation pages and complete revision-book sequence;
* confirmation of the map reference for Daniel's Gortereghy holding;
* a burial or gravestone record for Daniel;
* records identifying Kate Glasgow and her relationship to Daniel;
* earlier records for Thomas and Alexander Glasgow; and
* contemporary evidence identifying the parents of Daniel and Thomas.

The death of Daniel Glasgow was registered on 16 October 1871 in Coleraine, aged 75.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Daniel Glasgow, 16 October 1871, aged 75, Coleraine registration district, D/1871/96/1008/2/362.</ref>

26355545.Name: Glasgow-987
26355545.bio:
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}} == Biography == '''Thomas Glasgow''' was a farmer of Lisnagaver in Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. His exact birthplace and parents have not been proved. Thomas was born about 1815. His age of 35 in the 1851 census and his reported age of 55 at death in 1870 independently place his birth in approximately 1814–1816.1851 Ireland Census, residents of house 37, Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim, National Archives of Ireland, [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ household return] (accessed 12 May 2025).“Ireland, Deaths, 1864–1870,” digital film/folder 004024453; FHL microfilm 101716; record 2; packet G; {{FamilySearch Record|FGFD-PYC}}; Thomas Glasgow, died 21 June 1870, aged 55, Lisnagaver (accessed 12 May 2025). This is an indexed record; the original civil return remains to be obtained. Thomas married '''[[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]]'''. Their marriage date and congregation have not been identified. No located record names another wife. === Early family === A derivative transcription of the Rasharkin Presbyterian register records three early children: * Eliza Glascaw, born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin; * Eliza Glascow, born 17 October 1843 and baptised 5 November 1843, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver; * Jane Glascaw, born 29 April 1846, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver.Barbara Braswell, transcript of Rasharkin Presbyterian Church baptisms, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html ''Baptisms, 1834–1846''], entries 162, 199 and 269 (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcription; the controlling original register is PRONI MIC1P/292. The two Eliza entries appear to concern separate children. The younger Eliza was still living in 1851. The older child probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but no death or burial record has been found. Her previously assigned death about 1845 is unproved. === 1851 census === Thomas and Mary Ann were recorded at Lisnagaver in the surviving 1851 Irish census. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Lisnagaver household, 1851''' ! Person ! Age ! Recorded status |- | Thomas Glasgow | 35 | Farmer |- | [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann Glasgow]] | 29 | Wife |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | 10 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | 7 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | 5 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | 3 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | 1 | Daughter |- | Catherine McLaughlin | 15 | Servant |} === Children === The evidence does not give every reported child the same status. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Known and reported children''' ! Child ! Evidence ! Assessment |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | Aged ten and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. Her reported later identification with the wife of John Alexander Redpath in New Zealand depends on later family and New Zealand evidence.Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', Find Ancestors message board, posted 25 January 2007, with replies dated 9 April 2020, [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a later family account, not contemporary proof. |- | [[Glasgow-1360|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck to Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin. | Documented by the derivative baptism transcription. She probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but her death date is unknown. |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 October 1843 at Lisnagaver, baptised 5 November and aged seven in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported later identification as Eliza Haigh in New Zealand has not been fully proved. |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | Born 29 April 1846 at Lisnagaver and aged five in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported marriage to Robert Jamieson and migration to New Zealand remain dependent on later evidence. |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | Aged three and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | Aged one and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter. She was probably the daughter called Peggy in the later family account. |- | [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]] | Aged 24 when she gave notice of marriage at Christchurch in October 1877. A derivative Victorian death-index entry reportedly names her mother as Mary Ann McCracken.New Zealand Notices of Intention to Marry, derivative transcription, Christchurch district, 3 October 1877, Catherine Glasgow, age 24, spinster and milliner, three years' residence at Christchurch, intending to marry Benjamin Pherson Ekberg, [https://itm.howison.co.nz/year/1877/district/christchurch transcription] (accessed 9 August 2026).Victoria death index, Catherine Ekberg, 1946, registration 12550, derivative details reproduced in the later Glasgow family discussion; father recorded under the surname Glasgow and mother as Mary Ann McCracken. | Probable daughter. Her original baptism and Victorian death certificate are required. She is also a plausible, but unproved, identification for the Kate Glasgow present at [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]'s death in 1871. |- | [[Glasgow-3975|Sarah Glasgow]] | Four original civil birth returns identify Sarah Taylor, formerly Glasgow, as the wife of Charles Taylor, farmer, at Lisnagaver.Ireland civil birth returns: Ellen Taylor, born 20 January 1897, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1897/02142/1813179.pdf original image]; Catherine Taylor, born 8 April 1899, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1899/02043/1782340.pdf original image]; Charles Taylor, born 21 December 1902, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1902/01892/1735215.pdf original image]; Alexander Taylor, born 28 January 1905, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1905/01798/1705043.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Probable daughter. The records strongly corroborate the reported marriage and Lisnagaver residence but do not name Sarah's father. |- | Alexander Glasgow | Reported to have emigrated to South Africa or the United States. | Possible child only. No contemporary record identifying him as Thomas's son has been found. |- | [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] | His 1888 marriage records him as a farmer of Lisnagaver and son of Thomas Glasgow, farmer.Ireland civil marriage return, no. 79, [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church, County Londonderry, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1888/10763/5925382.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Documented son of Thomas. The marriage does not name his mother. He was recorded as “Full,” meaning over 21, and was therefore born before 28 June 1867.General Register Office for Northern Ireland, [https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/gronis-online-search-results “GRONI's online search results”], explanation that “Full” means over 21 (accessed 9 August 2026). |} Daniel Neely's previously assigned birth about 1870 is incorrect. His age category at marriage proves that he was born before 28 June 1867. === Brother Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea === Thomas was a brother of '''[[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]''', the watch and clock maker of Kilrea. Daniel's registered will refers to:
“my late brother Thomas Glasgow” ... “my nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow”
The will was proved in 1871.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea, proved 1871; refers to his late brother Thomas and nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel Neely's marriage independently names his father as Thomas Glasgow, farmer, and gives his residence as Lisnagaver. Together, the will and marriage identify Daniel of Kilrea as Thomas's brother and Daniel Neely as Thomas's son. Daniel died at Kilrea on 16 October 1871, aged 75. The original civil return names '''Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea''' as the informant.Ireland civil death return, no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871 at Kilrea, aged 75, widower and watchmaker; informant Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The return does not state Kate's relationship to Daniel. === Landholding === A transcript of Griffith's Valuation lists Thomas Glasgow, John Glasgow and Alexander Glasgow as occupiers at Lisnagaver.Griffith's Valuation transcript for Rasharkin parish, [https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-rasharkin.php entries for Lisnagaver] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcript; the original valuation page, map and plot references remain to be checked. Their presence in the same townland makes a relationship plausible but does not establish whether John and Alexander were Thomas's brothers, uncles, cousins or unrelated members of the same surname cluster. The original valuation page and subsequent revision books are required before plot succession can be used as relationship evidence. === Death === Thomas died at Lisnagaver on '''21 June 1870''', aged 55. His reported age is consistent with the age recorded in 1851 and gives an estimated birth in about 1814 or 1815. His burial place has not been identified. === Brother Daniel and the Prescott connection === Thomas was a brother of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], watchmaker of Kilrea. Daniel's will calls Thomas his late brother and Daniel Neely Glasgow his nephew; Daniel Neely's marriage independently identifies Thomas as his father.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871 (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel's death return names Kate Glasgow as informant but gives no relationship.Ireland civil death return no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The original deeds under the will of their brother Robert Glasgow of Prescott independently identify the same Thomas and Daniel. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives shares to his brothers Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas, sister Mary, and collectively the children of brother James; it does not call James deceased.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image]. Memorial 13 records the 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, between Robert's widow Jane and Samuel Glasgow, merchant, concerning Samuel's one undivided sixth share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image]. Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, as transferors to Samuel of two undivided sixth interests under Robert's will.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image]. The deeds establish Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert as brothers; they do not identify their parents. == Research Notes == === Former merge and the Coltrim census === A formerly separate WikiTree profile, '''Glasgow-2994''', was merged into this profile. Its estimated birth about 1823 has no identified contemporary source and conflicts with the approximately 1815 birth indicated by Thomas's 1851 and 1870 ages. The legacy link attached to the merged material referred to a 1901 household at Coltrim, Moneymore DED, County Londonderry. The surviving Form B1 confirms that another Thomas Glasgow was the householder at house 7 in Coltrim and refers to Form A schedule 6. It appears to record four occupants, but it does not give Thomas's age, family relationships, birthplace or occupation.1901 Ireland Census, Form B1, Coltrim townland, Moneymore DED, South Derry, County Londonderry, house 7, householder Thomas Glasgow, Form A schedule 6, National Archives of Ireland, [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=nai000629314 original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). Since the Lisnagaver Thomas died in 1870, the Coltrim return belongs to another man. It does not establish that the Coltrim man was born about 1823. Glasgow-2994 should not be recreated as a separate person unless Form A schedule 6 or another original record establishes his age and family. === Kate Glasgow at Daniel's death === Daniel's civil death return names Kate Glasgow as the informant and says that she was present at his death. It does not call her his sister and does not state any relationship. [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]], probable daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann, is a plausible candidate. She was aged 24 in October 1877 and reported three years' residence at Christchurch. That chronology is consistent with her still being in Ireland in 1871, but does not prove that she was the informant. If the informant was Catherine, Daniel was her uncle, not her brother. An older sister, daughter, daughter-in-law, other niece or cousin remains possible. === Marriage, Daniel's mother and a possible second wife === No record has been found for the marriage of Thomas and Mary Ann. No positive evidence has been found for another wife. Thomas and Mary Ann are named together in the 1842, 1843 and 1846 baptism entries and in the 1851 household. Daniel Neely's marriage names his father but not his mother. Mary Ann is therefore his probable mother, based on the established family and chronology, but the relationship remains unproved. Daniel was born before June 1867 rather than about 1870. Mary Ann, born about 1821, would have been no more than about 45 or 46. The chronology does not require a second marriage. === Parents === A later family account identifies Thomas as a son of '''[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Unknown-761034|Rosanna]]''' and states that Rosanna died about 23 October 1822. No contemporary record naming Thomas's parents has been found. Both relationships should remain uncertain. Rosanna's maiden surname has sometimes been given as Shaw, but no source proving that surname has been identified. === Priority Research === * '''Priority 1 — identify the Coltrim Thomas:''' obtain Form A schedule 6 for house 7, Coltrim, Moneymore DED, 1901. Record every occupant, age, relationship, occupation and birthplace. This will determine whether the discarded circa-1823 estimate had any basis. * '''Priority 1 — later baptisms:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/292, Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, 1847–1867, for Nancy, Margaret, Catherine or Kate, Sarah, Alexander and Daniel Glasgow. Search Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glasco and Glassgow, with McCracken, McCrackin, McCraken and McCochrane variants. A Daniel entry naming Mary Ann would substantially resolve the second-marriage question; another mother would provide the first positive evidence for a second wife.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records ''Guide to Church Records''], entries for Rasharkin Presbyterian MIC1P/292, Second Portglenone MIC1P/357, Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20 (accessed 9 August 2026). * '''Priority 1 — marriage:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/357, Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages, approximately 1838–1842, for Thomas Glasgow and Mary Ann McCracken variants. Also inspect its baptisms for Rose Ann about 1840–1841. If unsuccessful, continue with Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20. * '''Priority 2 — Catherine:''' obtain Catherine Ekberg's original 1946 Victorian death certificate, registration 12550. Record both parents' full names, birthplace, duration in each colony or state and the informant. Compare these details with the 1877 New Zealand marriage notice and the 1871 Kate Glasgow informant. * '''Priority 2 — Sarah:''' locate the marriage of Sarah Glasgow and Charles Taylor, probably before the birth of Ellen Taylor in January 1897. The marriage should state Sarah's age, residence and father. * '''Priority 2 — land succession:''' obtain the original Griffith's Valuation page and map for Lisnagaver and follow Thomas's plot through the valuation-revision books to at least 1888. Determine whether it passed to Mary Ann, Daniel Neely or another relative, and compare the adjoining holdings of John and Alexander Glasgow. * '''Priority 3 — deaths:''' obtain Thomas's original 1870 civil death return and the candidate 1914 death registration for Mary Ann. Record the informants, exact residences and stated relationships rather than relying only on indexes. Robert's sister Mary is independently identified in a 15 September 1869 deed, registered 1 July 1870, as Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow. Her children, including John Black, Rose Ann Black, Jane Miller, Agnes Black and Thomasina Montgomery, conveyed interests under Robert's will to Mary Eno Glasgow; the deed also records their inheritance of their unmarried intestate sister Elizabeth Black's share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200420, image 277, C298, dated 15 September 1869 and registered 1 July 1870, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K original image]. The death of Thomas Glasgow was registered on 21 June 1870 in Ballymoney, aged 55.[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Thomas Glasgow, 21 June 1870, aged 55, Ballymoney registration district, D/1870/31/1005/2/197. == Sources ==

Spouses.Name: Unknown-761034
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==
Rosanna's maiden surname, birth and death are not established by a contemporary record. A 2007 descendant account names an older [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] and Rosanna as parents of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] of Lisnagaver and reports Rosanna's death about 23 October 1822.<ref name=DescendantAccount>[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 2007 Genes Reunited descendant account], naming Alexander and Rosanna as Thomas Glasgow's parents and reporting Rosanna's death.</ref> This is late descendant testimony rather than contemporary proof.

Rosanna's structured birth is retained as '''before 1778''', an uncertain working boundary rather than a known birth year. The former 1790 estimate was impossible if [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], born about 1795/96, was her son. Daniel's civil death and will support his age and identify Thomas as his brother, but do not prove Rosanna as their mother.

== Research Notes ==
The attached Alexander is retained as an uncertain spouse. Daniel and Thomas are retained as uncertain sons. [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] has also been proposed as a son in the working reconstruction, but no contemporary record presently proves Rosanna's maternity for any of the three.

Rosanna's last name at birth remains '''Unknown'''. The shared clockmaking occupation of Daniel Glasgow and James Shaw does not prove that Rosanna was a Shaw or that James was her brother.

A [https://gw.geneanet.org/bobspree?lang=en&n=glasgow&p=alexander geneanet tree] gives her surname as Alexander

== Biography ==

Jane was born in 1802. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] and [[Arthur-2480|Mary Arthur]].

  - The 1831 census records John Gray at Boveedy with exactly one male and one female, both Presbyterian. Jane was 28 and her known husband John Gray was 32. 1831 transcription (https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census.tsv)
  - Jno. Gray remained a Boveedy landholder in the 1833 tithe, confirming household continuity. 1833 tithe (https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/derry/tithe-applotments/tamlaght-o-crilly-parish.php)
  - Descendant evidence specifically states that Jane married John Gray in Ireland before emigrating to Kentucky. Their later burial grouping confirms the couple’s identities, though not their marriage date. Jane Glasgow
    (https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I374&tree=tree1)

20816530.Name: Glasgow-822
20816530.DeathLocation: Guernsey County, Ohio, United States of America
20816530.bio:
== Biography ==

John Glasgow was born in Ireland on 10 April 1767.<ref name="JohnRegister">[https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I368&tree=tree1 John Glasgow family register and descendant page] (accessed 20 July 2026).</ref><ref name="JohnLetter">[https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/documents/John%20Glasgow%20letter%20to%20Jane%20Glasgow%20Gray%203-20-1847.pdf John Glasgow to Jane Glasgow Gray, 20 March 1847], scan and transcript (accessed 20 July 2026).</ref> He married [[Arthur-2480|Mary Arthur]] on 21 May 1798, and their nine children were born in Ireland between 1799 and 1815.<ref name="JohnRegister" />

The family lived at '''Inishrush, County Londonderry'''. In 1847, John recalled that they had kept more bees there than they ever kept at one time after leaving Ireland.<ref name="JohnLetter" />

The first secure evidence of John in Ohio is his 1833 purchase of land in Guernsey County.<ref name="Deed1833">[http://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89WY-TFPB Guernsey County deeds, volume H, page 457].</ref> He was recorded there in 1840.<ref name="Census1840">“'''United States Census, 1840''',” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHRF-1B6 : 8 September 2017), John Glascow, Guernsey, Ohio, United States; citing p. 355, NARA microfilm publication M704, roll 396; FHL microfilm 20,165.</ref> By 1847, John and Mary were being cared for by their son Arthur, who left “nothing undone” to make them comfortable.<ref name="JohnLetter" /> They were living in Arthur's household in Londonderry Township in 1850.<ref name="Census1850">“'''United States Census, 1850''',” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MX3M-HP3 : 12 April 2016), John Glasgow in household of Arthur Glasgow, Londonderry, Guernsey, Ohio, United States; citing family 1538, NARA microfilm publication M432.</ref>

The Glasgows were a strict Covenanter family; family tradition states that even whistling on the Sabbath was forbidden.<ref name="JohnRegister" /> John's surviving letter reflects this outlook through repeated references to prayer, salvation and holding to Christ “for righteousness and life.”<ref name="JohnLetter" />

John died on 23 December 1851 and was buried in the Scotch Covenanter Cemetery in Guernsey County.<ref name="Grave">“Find A Grave Index,” database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QVKX-FB2D : 13 December 2015), John Glasgow, died 1851; burial in Scotch Covenanter Cemetery, Guernsey County, Ohio; citing {{FindAGrave|43524841}}.</ref>

== Children ==

The Glasgow family register records nine children:<ref name="JohnRegister" />

* [[Glasgow-821|Rose or “Rosanna”]], born 4 March 1799; married Alexander McKeown in Ireland and settled in Harrison County, Ohio.
* '''[[Glasgow-3928|Maria ]]''', born 22 September 1800.
* '''[[Glasgow-3929|Jane]]''', born 5 October 1802; married John Gray in Ireland and settled in Kentucky. John's 1847 letter was apparently addressed to her.<ref name="JohnLetter" />
* [[Glasgow-3373|Adam]], born 7 July 1804.
* '''[[Glasgow-3930|Lavinia]]''', born 21 June 1806.
* [[Glasgow-1165|James]], born 9 November 1808; died 20 April 1823.
* [[Glasgow-43|Margaret]], born 17 October 1810; married John H. Walkinshaw.
* [[Glasgow-1617|John]], born 4 March 1813; died 17 August 1836 in Ohio.
* [[Glasgow-1608|Arthur]], born 1 July 1815; married Jane Neil.

== Research Notes ==

* [[Glasgow-3927|John Glasgow (bef.1813-)]] represents the John Glasco who headed house 2 at Inishrush in the 1831 census. His household contained four males and four females, all Presbyterian.<ref name="Census1831">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census_3.html “Tamlaght O'Crilly Census – 1831”], entry 1019, John Glasco, Innisrush house 2; transcription by Richard John Torrens (accessed 20 July 2026).</ref> The location, religion and household composition are compatible with this family, but the census gives no ages, names or relationships. If they were the same man, John emigrated between the 1831 census and his 1833 Ohio land purchase.<ref name="Census1831" /><ref name="Deed1833" />
* The John Glasgow recorded in Richland Township, Belmont County, in 1830 was aged forty to forty-nine and was almost certainly a different man. John, born in 1767, would have been about sixty-three. The citation is retained to document the rejected identification, but should not be used as evidence that he was in Ohio by 1830.<ref name="Ohio1830">[https://archive.org/details/populationsc18300127unit/page/n484/mode/1up 1830 United States census, Richland Township, Ohio], original census image (accessed 20 July 2026).</ref>
* John may have descended from [[Glasgow-1475|Adam Glasgow (bef.1706-)]], associated with Kilbirnie and the Presbytery of Irvine. This remains unproved.

{{Ireland Native}}

== Biography ==
'''Mary Arthur''' was born in Ireland on 25 March 1774. Her exact date is written in the family register, while the 1850 census records her birthplace as Ireland.<ref name="MaryBible">Glasgow family Bible, family register of [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] and Mary Arthur, [https://hiltner.com/mckeown/histories/8479.jpeg original register image]; [https://hiltner.com/mckeown/showmedia.php?mediaID=532&medialinkID=726 media description], ''McKeown and Shields Families''; the collection is indexed at [https://hiltner.com/mckeown/index.php hiltner.com/mckeown], accessed 29 August 2026.</ref><ref name="Census1850">“United States Census, 1850,” database with images, FamilySearch ([https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MX3M-HPQ MX3M-HPQ], accessed 29 August 2026), Mary Glasgow in the household of Arthur Glasgow, Londonderry, Guernsey County, Ohio, United States; citing family 1538, NARA microfilm publication M432.</ref>

Mary married [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] on 21 May 1798. Their register names nine children and records their birth dates.<ref name="MaryBible" />

== Research Notes ==
The compiled descendant page for Mary reports that her burial place is unknown and only suggests the Scotch Covenanter Cemetery as likely; no burial place should be asserted without a burial record.<ref name="CompiledMary">[https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I369&tree=tree1 “Mary Arthur (1774–1859),” ''McKeown and Shields Families''], accessed 29 August 2026.</ref>

Glasgow-3986.Name: Glasgow-3986
Glasgow-3986.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James was reportedly born about 1773 and died in 1831. His parentage has not been proved. He is currently attached to [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], but the approximately sixty-five-year gap makes a later generation more likely; the relationship should remain uncertain until a baptism, will or property succession identifies his father.

=== Possible early records ===

A release dated 16 April 1795 concerning garden ground in Newtown of Larne was witnessed by '''James Glasgow of Larne, merchant''', and Charles McGarel, gentleman.<ref name="Merchant1795">Registry of Deeds transcript, release dated 16 April 1795, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-Q9B8-H FamilySearch image].</ref>

An assignment recorded in 1797 concerning a Larne tenement near Charles Dawson Stewart's tanyard includes a witness signature for '''James Glasgow junior'''.<ref name="Junior1797">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment recorded in 1797, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-Q96R-C FamilySearch image].</ref>

The date, place, merchant designation and use of “junior” fit this James better than the older Larne men. Neither deed names his parents. “Junior” distinguishes him from an older James but does not by itself prove a father-son relationship.

== Research Notes ==
[[Glasgow-4024|James Glasgow of Cookstown (abt.1791-bef.1831)]] was buried at St Luran's on 13 March 1831 aged 40. He is not this Larne man: the reported ages, locality and burial context differ. The profiles should remain separate.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

The younger James of Larne remains a provisional identity assembled from the 1795 merchant and 1797 “junior” occurrences. Those records need not identify the same man, and neither names him as the father of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]. He is nevertheless an age-compatible possible son of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] and a possible route to Alexander's generation: an estimated birth about 1773 would allow ordinary fatherhood ages in the early nineteenth century. This is an alternative to the older-Alexander route, not a replacement for the Thomas-family testimony, and Thomas and Daniel must not be assigned to this James merely to make a pedigree. The ropemaker, this possible merchant/junior identity, and the Larne tanner are distinct record groups unless a document joins them. Preserve the existing record citations and state the identity and kinship as provisional.<ref name="YoungerJamesCurrent">The merchant and junior references cited above establish leads, not a father statement for Alexander.</ref>

=== Additional source context ===

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.
* Related profile: [[Glasgow-3986]].

29028259.Name: Glasgow-1509
29028259.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was reportedly born in '''1737'''. A Larne or Kilwaughter congregational record is said to contain an entry for a James, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], at '''New Town, Larne''', in that year.

The original congregational entry, or a reliable full transcription, has not yet been cited on this profile. The exact birth date, place and identification of Hugh as James’s father should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively established.

James was a '''ropemaker''' at Larne, County Antrim. A lease dated 10 September 1760, registered on 24 November 1763, describes him as a ropemaker of Belfast and leases him a marked-out ropewalk at Gardenmore in Larne for thirty-one years from 1 November 1760. He agreed to build a house at the south end of the ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1760">Registry of Deeds transcript, lease dated 10 September 1760 and registered 24 November 1763, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 FamilySearch image].</ref>

On 28 March 1768 James, described as a ropemaker of the Old Town of Larne, assigned the plot, workhouse and remainder of the same lease to John Hill for £50. The matching commencement date and rent identify it as the 1760 ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1768">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment dated 28 March 1768, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW FamilySearch image].</ref>


A memorial at '''St Cedma’s Church, Larne''', is reported to record James Glasgow with the dates '''1737–1802''' and to name his wife as '''Janet Shutter'''. A photograph or complete reliable transcription of the monument should be cited before the exact dates and marriage are treated as fully verified.

James is reported to have died in '''1802'''.

An Irish probate-index transcription records a '''James Glasgow of Larne''' in the Diocese of Belfast in '''1803'''.<ref>Irish probate index transcription supplied July 2026, entry for James Glasgow, Diocese of Belfast, residence Larne, 1803.</ref>

The agreement in name and residence, together with probate in the year after the reported death, makes this a strong match to the man commemorated at St Cedma’s.

The 1803 entry should be understood as a probate or estate event. It does not replace the reported 1802 death year. Probate occurring in the year following death would be ordinary.

The probate entry establishes Larne as James’s recorded residence during the estate proceedings. It does not by itself prove that Larne was his place of death.

=== Wife and family ===

James’s wife is reported on the St Cedma’s memorial as '''Janet Shutter'''.

The complete inscription should be obtained and cited because the memorial may also contain:

* Janet’s dates;
* the date or duration of the marriage;
* children buried in the same plot;
* other Glasgow relatives; or
* wording clarifying whether the monument was erected by descendants.

No inspected baptismal, marriage, will or probate record currently cited on this profile names James’s children.

The 1803 probate record may be important. An original will, administration bond or surviving abstract could identify:

* Janet as his widow;
* sons or daughters;
* married daughters or sons-in-law;
* executors or administrators;
* business partners;
* property at Larne or Blackcave; or
* other relatives.

== Research Notes ==
=== Identification and evidence ===

The following records probably concern the same man:

* the James, son of Hugh Glasgow, reportedly recorded at New Town or Larne in 1737;
* James Glasgow, ropemaker, documented in the 1760 ropewalk lease and 1768 assignment;
* James Glasgow commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802 and wife Janet Shutter; and
* James Glasgow of Larne whose estate entered Belfast probate in 1803.

The chronology and repeated Larne association make this identification plausible and probably correct.

The strongest direct contemporary evidence presently cited is the 1760 ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment. The baptism and memorial evidence still require complete source citations, and the probate index does not name James’s father or wife.

The profile should therefore distinguish between:

* directly documented facts, including James’s ropemaking and Larne residence in the 1760–1773 records;
* strong identity matches, including the 1803 probate entry; and
* reported but not yet fully exposed evidence, including the 1737 congregational entry and St Cedma’s memorial.

=== Ropemaker evidence and identity distinction ===

A Registry of Deeds memorial dated 14 May 1766 also names James Glasgow, ropemaker of Larne, as a witness.<ref>[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=204122 Registry of Deeds Index Project, memorial 204122], deed dated 14 May 1766.</ref> In 1773 Mr James Glasgow of Larne, gentleman, swore that he was aged upwards of thirty, placing his birth before 27 October 1743.<ref name="Larne1773">Registry of Deeds memorial and affidavit, sworn 27 October 1773, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M FamilySearch image].</ref> Alexander Holmes's 1799 will later identifies a Larne occupant as James Glasgow, roper. The repeated occupation and place form a coherent sequence.

The 1768 assignment was witnessed by a '''different''' James Glasgow who was expressly described as a tanner. A 1778 mortgage and the 1786 Blackcave lease continue that tanner sequence and fit [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow (about 1747–1812)]]. The two tradesmen should not be conflated.

The reported 1737 congregational occurrence and the present uncertain placement under [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remain competing parentage hypotheses until the original entry or another relationship record is inspected.

=== Research priorities ===

Further research should obtain:

* the original or fullest available congregational entry for the 1737 James, son of Hugh Glasgow;
* the name of the congregation and exact wording of that entry;
* a photograph or complete transcription of the St Cedma’s memorial;
* evidence supporting Janet Shutter’s identity and marriage to James;
* the exact nature of the 1803 Belfast probate entry;
* the original will, administration record or bond, if it survives;
* a Betham or other pre-destruction abstract of the estate;
* names of beneficiaries, executors, witnesses or sureties; and
* records identifying any children of James and Janet.

=== Research conclusion ===

James Glasgow was directly recorded as a ropemaker in the 1760 Larne ropewalk lease, the 1766 memorial and the 1768 assignment.

The 1803 Belfast probate entry for James Glasgow of Larne is a strong match to the man reportedly commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802. It supports Larne as his probate residence while remaining consistent with death in 1802.

The reported identification of his wife as Janet Shutter and his father as Hugh Glasgow is plausible, but the complete memorial and congregational record should be cited before those relationships and the exact dates are treated as certain.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

James is securely the Belfast/Larne ropemaker in the 1760 Gardenmore ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment, and the 1773 affidavit places that adult James at Larne and over thirty. The 1768 document separately calls its witness James Glasgow a tanner; that is a different occupational record group, probably [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]], and does not change this James's occupation. The original 1784 lease registered in 1790 has now been inspected: its witness is explicitly a tanner and belongs to the separate occupational sequence probably represented by [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]]. James is a plausible earlier-generation candidate in the Larne reconstruction, including as a possible father of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and possible kin of [[Glasgow-3904|older Alexander Glasgow]], but no record yet makes either relationship. His 1762 marriage to Janet Shutter postdates Adam's estimated 1758 birth, so Janet cannot be called Adam's mother. A William Glasgow, merchant, witnessed the 1760 lease, but is not yet definitely [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]].<ref name="LarneCurrent">Registry of Deeds memorials for the 1760 lease, 1768 assignment and 1773 affidavit, cited above.</ref>

=== Additional source context ===

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.
* Related profile: [[Glasgow-1509]].
<ref name="Retained2">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF Registry of Deeds, 1784 transaction registered in 1790: James Glasgow, tanner; sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790].</ref>


A lease dated 14 January 1784 was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, '''tanner''', with Samuel Drummond, merchant, and James Farries, writing clerk. James’s affidavit was sworn 17 August 1790; the memorial was registered on 23 August. The original reads “Tanner”, resolving an earlier automated “Turner” reading. This strengthens the occupational sequence, without independently naming his family.<ref name="Tanner1784">Registry of Deeds, memorial 278037, lease 14 January 1784, sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF FamilySearch image 437], original inspected 21 September 2026. The online collection label 1734–1736 does not describe this image’s date.</ref>

=== Newtown title succession: identities unresolved ===

An 1874 deed recites a lease to James Glasgow dated 2 October 1779 and its renewal to Anne Glasgow and Jane Glasgow on 25 February 1832. The north-side Newtown property, formerly John English’s, adjoined a tenement formerly Hugh Glasgow’s. This documents succession to a lease, but does not call the women James’s daughters or identify which James held it. The monument wife Jane of [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]] died in 1820 and cannot automatically be the 1832 Jane. [[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]], whose monument gives a May 1832 death, is only a candidate for Anne; the original renewal is needed.<ref name="Newtown1874">Registry of Deeds, Antrim to John Mulvenna, indenture 25 March 1874, registered 24 August 1874, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H FamilySearch image 475], recital inspected in the original; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77QC-T continuation image 476].</ref>

== Sources ==
<references />

Glasgow-3991.Name: Glasgow-3991
Glasgow-3991.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was born about 1748, the son of '''[[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]''' and his wife '''[[Unknown-763010|Ann Glasgow]]'''. His approximate year of birth is calculated from his age at death.<ref name="Armorial">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], Glasgow monument inscription.</ref>

The family monument explicitly identifies James as the son of Hugh and Ann Glasgow. Hugh died on 8 July 1767, aged 62, and Ann died on 8 June 1786, aged 75.<ref name="Armorial" />

James married '''[[Unknown-763421|Jane]]''', whose maiden name is not given in the monument inscription. Jane was born about 1741, based on her recorded age at death.<ref name="Armorial" />

James and Jane had at least one known child:

* '''[[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]]''', born about 1768; died 25 May 1832, aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" />

James died on '''14 April 1812''', aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" /> His stated age places his birth approximately between 15 April 1747 and 14 April 1748.

His wife Jane survived him. She died on '''21 July 1820''', aged 79.<ref name="Armorial" />

=== Tanner at Larne ===

James is probably the Larne tanner documented between 1768 and 1790. A 1768 assignment by a different James Glasgow, a ropemaker, was witnessed by James Glasgow, tanner. The tanner later swore to the deed's execution at Larne.<ref name="Tanner1768">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment dated 28 March 1768, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW FamilySearch image].</ref>

A mortgage dated 22 June 1778 concerning premises in Newtown of Larne was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, tanner, and John Weir, notary. James swore the supporting affidavit at Larne on 29 June 1778.<ref name="Tanner1778">Registry of Deeds transcript, mortgage dated 22 June 1778, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-64YW FamilySearch image].</ref>

The occupation, place and chronology also agree with the 1786 Blackcave lease to James Glasgow, tanner of Larne. The sequence is a strong identity match, although the deeds do not name his wife or relatives. He should not be confused with the older Larne ropemaker [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]].

A lease dated 14 January 1784 was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, '''tanner''', with Samuel Drummond, merchant, and James Farries, writing clerk. James’s affidavit was sworn 17 August 1790; the memorial was registered on 23 August. The original reads “Tanner”, resolving an earlier automated “Turner” reading. This strengthens the occupational sequence, without independently naming his family.<ref name="Tanner1784">Registry of Deeds, memorial 278037, lease 14 January 1784, sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF FamilySearch image 437], original inspected 21 September 2026. The online collection label 1734–1736 does not describe this image’s date.</ref>

=== Family Monument ===

The Glasgow armorial monument records Hugh Glasgow and Ann Glasgow, followed by:

:''James Glasgow their Son who died the 14th of April 1812 aged 64 years. Also his wife Jane Glasgow died 21st July 1820 aged 79 years. And of Ann Glasgow, Daughter to the last named who died the 25th May 1832 aged 64 years.''<ref name="Armorial" />

The same monument also commemorates eleven children of Hugh and Ann, naming a daughter Jane as "the first" and a son Hugh as "the last". James is recorded separately and explicitly described as "their Son".<ref name="Armorial" />

=== Research Notes ===

James's exact date and place of birth have not yet been established. His birth year of about 1748 is derived from his stated age of 64 at his death on 14 April 1812.

The wording concerning the eleven children of Hugh and Ann should not be interpreted as proving that the younger Hugh was their youngest child. The monument appears to refer to a particular group of children buried or commemorated there, while James is subsequently identified separately as their son.

Jane's maiden surname is currently unknown. The inscription calls her "his wife Jane Glasgow", which records her married surname rather than establishing Glasgow as her birth surname.

=== Newtown title succession: identities unresolved ===

An 1874 deed recites a lease to James Glasgow dated 2 October 1779 and its renewal to Anne Glasgow and Jane Glasgow on 25 February 1832. The north-side Newtown property, formerly John English’s, adjoined a tenement formerly Hugh Glasgow’s. This documents succession to a lease, but does not call the women James’s daughters or identify which James held it. The monument wife Jane died in 1820 and cannot automatically be the 1832 Jane. [[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]], whose monument gives a May 1832 death, is only a candidate for Anne; the original renewal is needed.<ref name="Newtown1874">Registry of Deeds, Antrim to John Mulvenna, indenture 25 March 1874, registered 24 August 1874, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H FamilySearch image 475], recital inspected in the original; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77QC-T continuation image 476].</ref>

=== Uncertain son: the 1843 settlement testator ===

[[Glasgow-4180|Hugh Glasgow]], whose executors or trustees were to pay £250 in the 1843 marriage settlement of [[Glasgow-4181|Mary Glasgow]] and John McGavock, is attached here as an '''uncertain son'''. Neither this father-son relationship nor Hugh's proposed fatherhood of Mary is stated in the settlement.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Ireland, marriage settlement, John McGavock and Mary Glasgow, 10 February 1843, affidavit 14 February and registration 18 February; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-FQ3Q opening image 499] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-F3BZ continuation image 500], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref> James's documented generation and father Hugh make this a compatible working placement, not proof. Hugh's estimated birth about 1770 was chosen for this model and cannot independently support it. [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3931|Hugh Glasgow]] remain alternative fathers. Jane has not been assigned as the testator's mother. Hugh's will and Mary's earlier property title are needed to test the proposed chain.

== Sources ==

<references />

* ''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'', p. 47, Glasgow armorial monument.

29027807.Name: Glasgow-1499
29027807.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}
== Biography ==

Hugh Glasgow was probably born about 1705. This estimate is reportedly based on an inscription on a Glasgow family gravestone in St Cedma's churchyard, Larne.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

=== Residence and property in Larne ===

On 10 March 1736, Hugh Glasgow and [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], both of Larne, County Antrim, received a lease from Alexander, Earl of Antrim. Memorial 63221 was registered on 10 April 1738 at eleven in the morning.<ref name="lease">Registry of Deeds, Dublin, memorial 63221, lease dated 10 March 1736; registered 10 April 1738. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image 542], image group 008088380, volumes 87–88; original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The lease covered two tenements already in their possession on the north side of the street in Newtown, Larne. One had a frontage of 23 feet, bounded east by Mr Agnew's tenement and west by Robert Robinson's. The other had a frontage of 32 feet, bounded east by John Boyd's tenement and west by John White's. Both extended backwards 150 feet.<ref name="lease" />

The annual rent was £1 16 shillings sterling, with receiver's fees of two pence per pound. The term began on the preceding 1 November and was measured by the lives of George II, Frederick Prince of Wales and Prince William Augustus Duke of Cumberland, with provision for replacement lives. The named lives were royal family members, not Glasgow children.<ref name="lease" />

The lease witnesses were James Stenhouse of Larne and William Harrison, clerk to Alexander Stewart of Ballylough. Stenhouse and Robert Wilson of Larne, merchant, witnessed the memorial. Stenhouse proved execution at Carrickfergus on 28 March 1738, stating that Alexander Stewart had executed the lease in the Earl's name and that William and Hugh had executed the lease and memorial.<ref name="lease" />

The memorial names no parent, spouse or child of either lessee and states no relationship between them. The later renewal endorsements remain separate research targets.

=== Joint lessors named in a 1757 assignment ===

A deed poll dated 4 June 1757, Matthew Stewart of Carncastle, farmer, to Robert Rainey of Larne, weaver, concerned a conditional assignment for £20 of Stewart's interest in a lease granted by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne. The original memorial does not date their head lease or describe the holding sufficiently to identify it with the 1736 Newtown tenements.<ref name="JointLessors1757">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159181, manuscript pp. 473–474, deed dated 4 June 1757, registered 26 May 1761; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4 FamilySearch image 257, opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJP6 image 258, continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The joint names and Larne locality strongly support association with these lessees, but the record names no Glasgow relative or relationship between William and Hugh. Neither Glasgow executed this assignment; its registration in 1761 does not prove that either was then living. The separate 1751 and 1767 endorsements to the 1736 lease remain unexamined and may identify replacement lives.<ref>PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A, 1736 William and Hugh Glasgow lease with 1751 and 1767 endorsements; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI eCatalogue], catalogue description only.</ref>

=== Church ===

A family chronology states that Hugh Glasgow became an elder of the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation in 1741.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

A nineteenth-century account quoting the Larne Session Book includes Hugh Glasgow among the members of the Session and records that he died on 8 July 1767.<ref name="death">[https://archive.org/stream/christianunitari0003unse/christianunitari0003unse_djvu.txt “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,”] ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), p. 197. The account quotes the Larne Session Book entry: “Hugh Glasgow … dead July 8, 1767.”</ref>

Hugh therefore died on 8 July 1767, provided that the elder named in the Session Book was the same Hugh Glasgow who held the 1736 Larne lease.<ref name="death" />

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible son John of Larne ===

[[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]], who married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] at Larne in 1769, is a possible son, with low confidence. His estimated birth about 1747 fits Hugh's age and Larne household, but the marriage chronology does not name John's father.<ref>Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Kilwaughter and Larne Glasgow chronology], entry for John Glasgow and Rose Allan's 1769 marriage. The birth estimate of 1745–48 is the compiler's estimate.</ref> The relationship is a working hypothesis and is marked uncertain. [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remains an alternative father. No evidence establishes that Hugh's wife Ann was John's mother.

The Larne memorial gives Hugh's death as 8 July 1767 aged 62 and commemorates members of his family, but does not name John. It has not been established as a complete enumeration of surviving children, so the omission neither proves nor excludes the proposed relationship.<ref>''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'', ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Glasgow stone at Larne], pp. 47–48.</ref> Further tests include the original registers (PRONI MIC/1B/6) and the renewal endorsements to the 1736 lease (PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A).


=== Possible duplicate ===

This profile may represent the same person as [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1706-abt.1760)]]. A merger should not be completed until the conflicting death information and the other relationships attached to the two profiles have been examined. The Larne Session Book supports a death date of 8 July 1767 rather than about 1760.<ref name="death" />

=== Possible Dublin baptism ===

A Hugh Glascoe was baptised in Dublin in 1704, the son of William Glascoe and Jone.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FR3H-8L7 FamilySearch record for Hugh Glascoe].</ref>

No evidence currently establishes that the child baptised in Dublin was the later Hugh Glasgow of Larne. The similar name and approximate date are not enough by themselves to identify them as the same person.

=== 1740 Protestant householder ===

A Hugh Glasgow appears in the 1740 list of Protestant householders for Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish.<ref>[https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PRONI-T808-15258 Virtual Treasury of Ireland, PRONI T808/15258, Names of Protestant Householders, 1740].</ref>

The identification is uncertain. The 1736 lease places Hugh Glasgow in Larne, and the church evidence also associates a man of that name with Larne. The Tamlaght O'Crilly entry should therefore remain a possible identification, not a confirmed event in his life.

=== Duneane surname ambiguity ===
The 1740 Duneane return includes Henry Glads. The reading may represent another surname and is not securely Glasgow. It is retained only as east-Antrim surname context and is not evidence that Henry was this Hugh or a relative.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Underlying record source: henry glads duneane 1740].</ref>

=== Mortgage with Hugh Shutter, 1749 ===

A mortgage dated 6 November 1749 records William Eakine of Larne conveying Old Town premises as security to Hugh Shutter and Hugh Glasgow. Hugh Glasgow is described as a merchant of Larne and executed the memorial. The underlying lease was dated 11 August 1748.<ref name="HughMortgage1749">Registry of Deeds, memorial 97407, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG FamilySearch image 449], original manuscript inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

Place, date and occupation strongly favour this Hugh. The deed establishes a Glasgow–Shutter business association before the reported 1762 marriage of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] to Janet Shutter, but names no relationship and proves neither that marriage nor Hugh’s parentage of James or [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]].
