| Mary's own certificate says she was born in England and names her father as Jackson Baird, born in Ireland.
| The conflict with the daughter's certificate cautions against treating all reported parental birthplaces as exact.
|-
| [https://vitalstats.michigan.gov/osr/gendisx/scripts/individual.asp?UniqueID=1896007182 Michigan historical death index]
| A James Glasgow died on 30 July 1896 and was born in Ireland.
| The index supplies no age, parents or county and does not itself prove that this was the Tecumseh man or the Lisnagaver child.
|-
| [https://lenawee.migenweb.org/MichMessengerVol3_1896-1897.pdf ''Michigan Messenger'', 1 August 1896, p. 1] (compilation p. 98)
| The contemporary report says the long-serving Lake Shore depot baggage master disappeared on Wednesday and was found in the Raisin River near Blood's bridge on Thursday, 30 July. It describes him as about five feet eight inches tall, with a scar across his previously broken nose and one or two missing fingers on his right hand.
| The report gives no parents or Irish locality. Its age estimate of about 55 points to about 1841 and is less exact than the cemetery and 1884 census evidence. Its claims concerning suicide and alcohol misuse are newspaper reporting rather than an inspected coroner's finding.
|}

The existing [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/127743880/james-glasgow Find a Grave memorial 127743880] proposes death on 29 August 1896. Both the Michigan historical index and the contemporary newspaper report establish 30 July 1896 for the Tecumseh candidate, so the memorial date should not be used.

The [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MQ57-BVR current FamilySearch tree profile MQ57-BVR] attaches the Lisnagaver 1851 census to these Michigan records. An [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MDBX-Y1G earlier FamilySearch identifier, MDBX-Y1G] was also recorded as a lead. FamilySearch tree links are derivative conclusions, not independent evidence that the child and adult were the same man. Several of the current profile's 20 source attachments are duplicate extractions of the same underlying event.

=== Dromore identification ===

A James Glasgow did occupy a house and small garden at plot 18b in Dromore, Rasharkin parish. The original PRONI valuation-revision books carry that name on the same holding from `VAL/12/B/3/13A` (1863-79) through `VAL/12/B/3/13C` (1891-1901). This continuing local valuation identity is unlikely to be the Tecumseh man, who was documented in Michigan by 1869 and reported residence there from about 1866. Revision-book names can lag an occupier's departure, however, and the Dromore man's identity has not been proved. The earlier [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/rasharkin.htm Rasharkin valuation transcription] did not expose this entry; the original PRONI revision books supersede that negative search while the transcription remains a useful finding aid.

=== The unnamed 1838 sibling ===

[[Glasgow-3940|The unnamed child baptised in 1838]] should not be renamed Samuel or identified with Samuel Glasgow of Franklin and Blissfield, Michigan. Alexander's 1851 return lists no such child as resident, absent or dead since 1841, and no American record inspected names Samuel's parents or County Antrim.

=== Dromore occupier candidate ===
A James Glasgow occupied property at Dromore in the Rasharkin valuation revisions between 1863 and 1879. The locality and age make this James a plausible candidate, but the valuation gives no parentage and the identification remains unproved.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx Underlying record source: james glasgow unidentified dromore occupier].</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Ann or Anne Glasgow''' was born about 1847 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]].

In 1851 she was recorded as their four-year-old daughter in the family household at Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ National Archives of Ireland, 1851 census], Alexander Glasgow household, Lisnagaver, house 35.</ref>

On 13 October 1876 Ann married '''Robert McCracken''' at Ballymoney. The register describes Robert as a full-age bachelor and farmer of Lisnagaver, son of William McCracken, labourer. Ann was a full-age spinster of Lisnagaver and named her father as Alexander Glasgow, labourer. Samuel Taylor and Mary Ann Henry witnessed the marriage.<ref name="Marriage1876">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Robert McCracken and Ann Glasgow, 13 October 1876; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1876/11181/8097170.pdf digital image].</ref>

Their known child, [[McCracken-5690|William James McCracken]], was born at Lisnagaver on 21 September 1877. His birth registration names Robert McCracken, labourer, and Ann formerly Glasgow as his parents.<ref name="WilliamBirth1877">General Register Office of Ireland, civil birth register, William James McCracken, 21 September 1877, Lisnagaver; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1877/03001/2099809.pdf digital image].</ref> William died there the following day, aged one day, from debility from birth; Ann registered both events.<ref name="WilliamDeath1877">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, William James McCracken, 22 September 1877, Lisnagaver; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1877/020541/7208135.pdf digital image].</ref>

Ann died in 1898 in the Calton registration district of Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland, aged 49, recorded as '''Ann McCracken''' with maiden surname Glasgow and mother's maiden surname McCaughern.<ref name="AnnDeath1898">National Records of Scotland, statutory registers of deaths, 1898, Calton (Glasgow), 644/4 70: Ann McCracken, female, 49, other surname Glasgow, mother's maiden surname McCaughern. [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople] index, searched 23 September 2026; register image not yet viewed.</ref> The maiden name, her mother's maiden name and her age, consistent with the four-year-old Ann of 1851, identify her with Alexander and Mary's daughter. Calton was also where her brother [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] had settled. The register entry, not yet viewed, should give her exact date and place of death, her husband's name and status, and an informant. No later record of Robert McCracken has yet been securely identified.

=== Probate ===

A marriage for Ann Glasgow and McCracken was registered on 13 October 1876 in the Ballymoney district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 13 October 1876, Ballymoney district, M/1876/I1/281/6/191.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

No compatible WikiTree profile has yet been identified for Ann's husband Robert McCracken. A same-name Ballymena mechanic who died in 1880 was the husband of Rose Ann Black and son of John McCracken, and was a different man.

This profile was originally created in 2015 to be Anna, born 1847 in Plains, Lanarkshire, Scotland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-424|John Glasgow]] and [[Forsyth-878|Christina Forsyth]].

This profile was vandalized in 2016 removing relationships and then this profile was merged with a different profile with different parents, so a new profile [[Glasgow-2083|Anna Glasgow (1847-)]] has been created since this profile has now been merged and changed to different parents.  History for that original profile information is in this profile.


The '''Nancy Glasgow''' who registered [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s death at Gortahar in 1888 should not presently be identified as Ann. The death entry calls Nancy the deceased's daughter, but Ann had married Robert McCracken in 1876 and no record yet shows that Nancy was her alternative name or that Ann later used Glasgow rather than McCracken. Nancy may have been a separate daughter.<ref name="AlexanderDeath1888">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Alexander Glasgow, 16 May 1888, Gortahar; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1888/06179/4766466.pdf digital image].</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Mary "Molly" McCaughan''' was born about 1810 or 1811 in County Antrim, Ireland. She married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], a farmer associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim.

Her parentage has not been established.

Mary's surname appears in surviving and transcribed records in several forms, including '''McCaughan''', '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern'''. Her given name appears as both '''Mary''' and '''Molly'''. These variants appear to refer to the same woman rather than separate wives of Alexander Glasgow.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">Richard John Torrens, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian Church Baptisms, 1834–1846], transcription by Barbara Braswell, particularly entries 75, 106 and 203 (accessed 16 July 2026). The page warns that faded or difficult entries may contain transcription errors. Original register: PRONI MIC.1P/292.</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Mary married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] about '''1836''', probably in County Antrim.

The detailed transcription of the surviving 1851 census records 1836 as the first-marriage year for both Alexander and Mary.<ref name="CensusTranscript">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], Lisnagaver households 34–37, p. 183 (accessed 16 July 2026). This is a transcription of the same census return, not independent evidence.</ref>

No original marriage entry has yet been identified.

The surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian marriage register begins only in 1845 and is therefore too late to contain their marriage.<ref name="ChurchCoverage">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/church.php?civilparish=Rasharkin&civilparishid=347&search_type=full Church records for Rasharkin], Presbyterian entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/292: baptisms from 1834 and marriages from 1845 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Second Portglenone Presbyterian Church remains a candidate for further research because its surviving marriage register begins in 1822 under PRONI reference MIC.1P/357.<ref name="SecondPortglenone">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/county_church_full.php?county=Antrim&denomination=Presbyterian&location=Public+Record+Office+of+Northern+Ireland&search_type=full Historic Presbyterian church records for County Antrim], Second Portglenone entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/357, marriages from 1822 (accessed 2026).</ref>

It should not, however, be described as their known marriage congregation unless an entry is found.

=== Children ===

Known and possible children of Alexander Glasgow and Mary McCaughan include:

The published Rasharkin baptism transcription contains no baptism entries for 1840 or 1841. Robert's missing baptism is therefore more likely to reflect incomplete record coverage or transcription than evidence that he belonged to another family.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== 1851 Census ===

In the surviving 1851 census, Mary was living at Lisnagaver with her husband Alexander and their children Robert, James and Ann.

Alexander was aged 40 and Mary was also aged '''40'''. Both were born in County Antrim, and the detailed census transcription records 1836 as their first-marriage year.<ref name="CensusHousehold">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, County Antrim, household 35, Alexander Glasgow household; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ household images] (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref><ref name="CensusTranscript" />

Mary's age therefore supports a birth about '''1810 or 1811'''. Earlier estimates placing her birth around 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with this contemporary census evidence.

=== Residences ===

The surviving records place Alexander and Mary within a small area of Rasharkin parish over a period of years:

Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck are separate adjoining townlands in Rasharkin civil parish, barony of Kilconway, County Antrim.<ref name="Townlands">[https://www.townlands.ie/antrim/kilconway/rasharkin/killoquin/lisnagaver/ Lisnagaver Townland, County Antrim], administrative divisions and adjoining-townland map (accessed 2026).</ref>

The changing descriptions may reflect residence close to a townland boundary rather than a substantial migration.

=== The Lisnagaver Glasgow–McCaughan Network ===

Mary and Alexander were part of a closely associated Glasgow and McCaughan network centred on Lisnagaver and the surrounding townlands.

Several Glasgow households appear together in the surviving 1851 census fragment.<ref name="CensusTranscript" />

The census explicitly identifies '''John and Samuel as brothers'''. It does not identify Alexander or Thomas as their brothers.

Later valuation evidence provides a separate land-based connection. John, Alexander and Thomas occupied consecutive principal holdings at Lisnagaver under the same immediate lessor, Robert Harvey.

The consecutive lot numbers strongly suggest that the holdings were physically close. The valuation map should still be consulted before stating that every plot directly adjoined or shared a boundary.

The combined census, church and land evidence supports a close Glasgow family-and-neighbour network at Lisnagaver while leaving the precise relationships unresolved.

==== Alexander and Thomas Glasgow ====

There is substantial circumstantial evidence that [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] was a close relative, and possibly a brother, of Mary's husband [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].

Alexander and Thomas were:

* born in County Antrim about five years apart;
* farmers;
* able to read and write;
* associated with the same Presbyterian congregation;
* recorded within the same Lisnagaver–Gortereagh–Moneyleck micro-area;
* heads of closely grouped Lisnagaver households in 1851;
* and later occupiers of consecutive valuation lots under the same lessor.

The contemporary Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism register provides a particularly strong FAN connection.

Alexander and Mary or Molly used the congregation while associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver. Thomas and [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]] used the same congregation while associated with Moneyleck and Lisnagaver.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

Most notably:

* Alexander and Mary's son James was born at Lisnagaver on '''9 October 1843''';
* Thomas and Mary Ann's daughter Eliza was born there on '''17 October 1843'''.

The children were born only eight days apart in the same small townland and appear in the same Presbyterian register.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

This is substantial FAN evidence for a close relationship.

No surviving record presently calls Alexander and Thomas brothers. Thomas should therefore be treated as Alexander's '''probable close relative and possible brother''', not as a proved sibling.

==== Thomas and Daniel Glasgow ====

A reported will record for [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea identifies [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] as his "late brother" and [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] as a nephew.<ref name="DanielWill">Will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871, reported in accumulated family research as identifying Thomas Glasgow as his "late brother". The original probate copy and complete archival citation are still required.</ref>

This supports Daniel and Thomas as brothers.

It does not establish Alexander's relationship to either man.

==== McCaughan Marriage Connection ====

The relationship between the Glasgow and McCaughan families was not limited to Mary's marriage to Alexander.

[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]'s daughter [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].

This provides another direct marriage connection between the Glasgow and McCaughen families within the same local network.

It does not, by itself, establish Robert McCaughen's relationship to Mary.

The original 1834 Rasharkin tithe book records William and James McCaheran at Gortereghy. The spelling is compatible with the McAughin and McAughern forms used for Mary in the baptism transcription, and Alexander and Mary's children were recorded at Gortereghy in 1837–38. This supports investigation of a local McCaughan family network, but the tithe names no relationships and does not establish Mary's parents.<ref name="GortereghyTithe1834">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Tithe Applotment Book for Rasharkin parish'', 1834, PRONI FIN/5/A/236, Gortereghy entries for William and James McCaheran.</ref>

=== The 1875 Mary Anne M‘Caughern Witness ===

On 18 February 1875, at Finvoy Parish Church, [[Glasgow-1371|Ann (Glasgow) Bellingham]] married Francis Bellingham.

Ann was the daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], farmer.

The witnesses were:

* Thomas Bellingham;
* '''Mary Anne M‘Caughern'''.

<ref name="BellinghamGlasgow1875">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Francis Bellingham and [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]], 18 February 1875, Finvoy Parish Church; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf digital image], entry 40.</ref>

The witness is relevant because of the established Glasgow–McCaughan network in and around Lisnagaver.

She should '''not''' presently be identified as [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow.

Reasons for caution include:

* the witness was recorded as '''Mary Anne''', rather than Mary or Molly;
* the surname was recorded as '''M‘Caughern''';
* no reliable evidence currently establishes that Alexander's wife was still living in 1875;
* other McCaughan or McAughern households existed within the wider local network.

The witness should therefore remain an unidentified associate pending further evidence.== Research Notes ==

=== Birth Date ===

Mary's age of 40 in the 1851 census supports birth about '''1810 or 1811'''.

Earlier estimates of about 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with the surviving census evidence and should not be used without an independent source.

=== Parentage ===

Mary's parents are presently '''unknown'''.

No surviving baptism, marriage entry, will, gravestone, death record or other contemporary source located for this profile explicitly names either parent.

The Rasharkin baptism entries establish Mary's maiden surname in variants such as '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern''', but they do not identify her father or mother.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== Possible John McCaughen Connection ===

A John McCaughen of Mount Pleasant Township, Washington County, Pennsylvania, made a will dated 22 February 1815 in which he referred to:

:''my onley daughter which I left in Ireland when I came to America.''

The daughter was named Mary McCaughen, and John reportedly left half of his estate to her.<ref name="PennsylvaniaMcCaughen">[https://dokumen.pub/irish-presbyterians-and-the-shaping-of-western-pennsylvania-17701830-hardcovernbsped-0822945436-9780822945437.html ''Irish Presbyterians and the Shaping of Western Pennsylvania, 1770–1830''], discussion of John McCaughen's 1815 will.</ref>

This is potentially relevant because:

* the daughter's name was Mary McCaughen;
* she remained in Ireland when her father emigrated;
* Mary's revised birth estimate of about 1810 or 1811 means she was alive by 1815.

However, no evidence currently connects the Pennsylvania testator to:

* County Antrim;
* Rasharkin;
* Lisnagaver or Gortereagh;
* Alexander Glasgow;
* or the known local McCaughan/McAughern network.

The identification should therefore be treated only as a '''research hypothesis''', not as Mary's established parentage.

=== Distinction from Mary McCaughan, wife of John McAulay ===

This Mary should not be confused with another Mary McCaughan who married John McAulay.

That woman was reportedly born about 1817 in Dublin, married John McAulay in 1840, emigrated to New York in 1859 and later appeared in the 1861 census of Ontario, Canada.

Records identify that Mary as a daughter of Hugh McCaughan.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:27T9-VWQ "New York Passenger Lists, 1820–1891", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1859.</ref><ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MQWD-6ZH "Canada, Ontario Census, 1861", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1861.</ref>

She was therefore a different woman from [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver.

=== Death ===

Mary died at Gortahar, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim, on 27 February 1892. The register describes her as a widow and housewife, reportedly aged 89. Her daughter [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Elder]] was present at death.<ref name="MaryDeath1892">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Mary Glasgow, 27 February 1892, Gortahar, Ballymoney registration district; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1892/06049/4723532.pdf digital image].</ref>

The reported age implies birth about 1803, while the 1851 census implies about 1810 or 1811. Her birth date remains estimated. The former 1866 death estimate is superseded by this registration.

=== Robert Glasgow's Scottish Death ===

[[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]]'s reported death on 27 November 1902 in Glasgow, Scotland, remains potentially important.

A Scottish death registration would normally have space to record both parents, including the mother's maiden surname, if known to the informant.

The original registration should be obtained before relying on parent details copied from online family trees.

=== Local McCaughan / McAughern Network ===

The Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription records McAughern households in or near the same local area.

This does not prove a relationship to Mary, but it makes reconstruction of the local McCaughan/McAughern population a priority.

Particular attention should be paid to:

* [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]];
* the unidentified Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 Bellingham–Glasgow marriage;
* McCaughan, McAughin and McAughern entries associated with Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck;
* witnesses to Glasgow and McCaughan marriages and baptisms;
* valuation and estate records involving the same surnames.

=== Identity and Record Cautions ===

* Mary's age of 40 in 1851 supports birth about 1810 or 1811, not 1817 or 1818.
* ''Molly'' is a familiar form of Mary and does not indicate a second wife.
* The spellings McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and M‘Caughern should not automatically be treated as different families.
* The baptism transcription is derivative evidence and the original PRONI MIC.1P/292 register should be inspected.
* No parent should be attached to Mary solely from surname similarity.
* The Pennsylvania John McCaughen theory remains unproved.
* Mary Anne M‘Caughern, witness in 1875, should not currently be merged with Mary.
* No unsupported 1866 death should be used for Mary.
* No Scottish or Australian death should be attached without evidence connecting it to the Lisnagaver family.

=== Priority Research ===

==== Priority 1 — Find Alexander and Mary's Marriage ====

* Search Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages under '''PRONI MIC.1P/357''' from about 1834 through 1838.
* Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glascow, Glascaw, McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and similar forms.
* Record residences, witnesses and minister even if no parents are named.
* Do not assume Second Portglenone was the congregation unless an entry is found.

==== Priority 1 — Inspect the Original Rasharkin Register ====

* Inspect the original Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries under '''PRONI MIC.1P/292'''.
* Check the entries for James in 1837, the unnamed child in 1838 and James in 1843–1844.
* Record the exact original spelling of Mary's surname.
* Examine adjacent entries, marginal notes and witnesses or sponsors.
* Collect every McCaughan/McAughern entry rather than only those already associated with Alexander.

==== Priority 1 — Reconstruct the McCaughan Network ====

* Investigate [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]].
* Identify Robert's father, mother, siblings, residence and landholding.
* Search for links between Robert and Mary through witnesses, naming patterns, church records, leases, probate or valuation records.
* Reconstruct McCaughan/McAughern households in Lisnagaver, Gortereagh, Moneyleck and adjoining townlands.
* Treat repeated surnames and proximity as FAN evidence only until a direct relationship is found.

==== Priority 1 — Obtain Robert Glasgow's Death Record ====

* Confirm the reported death of [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] in Scotland on 27 November 1902.
* Obtain the original Scottish statutory death registration.
* Record the names of both parents exactly as given.
* Record the mother's maiden surname and the identity of the informant.
* Assess the reliability of the parent information according to the informant's relationship to Robert.

==== Priority 2 — Identify Mary Anne M‘Caughern ====

* Trace the Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 marriage of [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]] and Francis Bellingham.
* Search Finvoy, Rasharkin and Ballymoney-area civil and Presbyterian records.
* Compare age, residence, marital status and family connections.
* Do not attach her to this profile without evidence establishing identity.

==== Priority 2 — Investigate the Pennsylvania Hypothesis ====

* Obtain the original or full abstract of John McCaughen's 1815 Washington County, Pennsylvania will.
* Establish when John emigrated from Ireland.
* Identify his place of origin in Ireland if possible.
* Determine Mary's age or circumstances from probate, guardianship, land or correspondence records.
* Search for associates linking John to County Antrim or the Bann Valley.
* Do not attach John as Mary's father unless a documentary bridge is found.

==== Priority 2 — Land and Estate Records ====

* Trace Glasgow and McCaughan/McAughern occupiers through the Lisnagaver valuation-revision books.
* Examine Harvey estate rentals, leases, assignments, arrears ledgers, tenant correspondence and surrender records.
* Pay particular attention to lots 24, 25 and 26 and nearby holdings.
* Look for explicit relationships such as daughter, son-in-law, brother, widow or representatives.
* Follow parcel numbers and tenancy succession rather than surnames alone.
* Candidate death entry: Mary Glasgow, 17 February 1892, aged 89, Ballymoney district, D/1892/31/1005/8/234. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Biography ==
Elder bible: Notes by Joan Elder McNamara

Father was Robert Elder.  He was born on Finvoy Road, Ballymoney, Antrim which runs from Ballymoney south to Rasherkin.

1851 Census I can not find any Elders (except Matilda Elder as Head) in parishes of Rasharkin nor Ballymoney
in 1855  lived in Gortereghy, Kilrea, Londonderry, Northern Ireland.  His wife's death certificate says he was a farmer.
1862 land records show James, Joseph, Robert, Ellen all leased land from Robert Harvey in "Kilconway, Gortereghy, Rasharkin, Antrim, Ireland"  Robert was flax farmer, the other leased house, offices and land. 

Married in Tamlaght Ocrilly, Derry, Ireland according to ancestry.com.  This is just SW of Rasharin and today in Derry (Londonderry)  County with a population of 121.  At its peak it had 10,460 residents in 1841  with a Presbyterian church and two Roman Catholic chapels.  I am not sure where I got the marriage having taken place in Rasharkin, County Antrim- although this is just a stones throw away.  

Somewhere I had James's death in 1880-just not sure where I got that.  This is a death certificate with death 19 April 1902, dying from dementia, a farmer, with his wife Mary at his side in Gortereghy. Death certrifgicate says he was born around 1820, which is what we think.  Mary also died in Gortereghy two years later, so it fits. 

Possible sister is Elizabeth Elder [ Elder-6372] born 1819 Rasharkin, County Antrim and married Robert Biggart ( Biggart-77   born 1819)  on April 26, 1850.

OVERALL, WHAT I HAVE IS CORRECT.  THERE ARE THREE JOHN ELDER THAT ARE SIMILAR.  ON 1900 Fed census he says he was born in MARCH, 1868.  This is only three year off from Mar 1865 where I found birth record in Dirraw, Antrim, Ireland to parents James and Mary Mcagherin Elder. THIS IS MY STRONGEST TIE THAT THIS IS OUR JOHN ELDER.

I believe born in Antrim,  Ireland @ only immigration of John Elder. In census he says 1888, but searched all records and only John Elder arrived May 16, 1887 o ship Devonia [ Note; some web sites mispell it as Deronidi -I looked at Devonia ship manifest and he is there].  He was age 19 which put DOB about 1867 or 1868 but they frequently did not remember their year of birth.  
Ship sailed from Glascow, Scotland. On ship manifest it says he was from Antrim.

I found a John Elder born 15 Mar 1865 in Dirraw, Antrim, Ireland to James Elder and Mary Mcagherin Elder.  I have a note from Joan Elder McNamara, hand written on a piece of paper, saying John Elder was born 21 March 1865.  {This could have been his baptismal date- only 3 days after birth on March 15]  Also found another son born to same couple there, William Elder Nov. 9, 1869 in Dirraw, Antrim but this is different DOB than Elder bible and father's name is James, not John.  could not find a Martha, Robert or Elizabeth.  

Found Elizabeth Elder 26 Jan 1864 born Dirraw, Antrim to John Elder and Mary Jane Mccaheron.  This is different DOB than Elder bible, and fathers name John not James, but Dirraw is very small townsland.

Found death of A.  Mary M'Caghern  in Ballymoney,  Antrim in 1871. at age 30 DOB: 1841

Mary jo says she found some info bout during irish potato famine, Elders migrated from island off the coast of Ireland to Antrim.  This could explain why I am not finding other data.

NOT SURE HOW THIS ALL FITS TOGETHER.
Middle name may or may not be Edward:

I CAN NOT FIND ANYTHING DEFINITELY SAYING WHO IS MOTHER IS, although I think Mary Jane McAughin is most likely based upon above finding.  
Menands Albany Rural cemetery listing does not list John Elder parents, nor does his marriage certificate.  

Middle name of "Edward" is uncertain. This could be a different John Elder.

Had a farm in Watervliet, NY. They definitely raised chickens for eggs- egg farm and raised dairy cows. .  This gave them  protein during the depression.  They were "White Lace Irish" meaning were well off.  They brought nice things from Ireland, such as lace tablecloths and bought the farm.

Father was Robert Elder.  He was born on Finvoy Road, Ballymoney, Antrim which runs from Ballymoney south to Rasherkin.

== Biography == Matthew was thought to have been born about 1767, probably near Garvagh, in County Antrim. He was ordained in Kilraughts in 1789 and had a new meeting house built in 1817. There was difficulty getting contributions so a special cess was placed on each member. Matthew personally contributed £50. Matthew, son of Mr. Elder, married Miss Graham in December 1804. '''Marriage''': "Ireland, Marriages in Walker's Hibernian Magazine, 1771-1812"

[https://search.findmypast.ie/record?id=IRE%2FDIOC%2F007246591%2F00087&parentid=IRE%2FDIOC%2FWILL%2F00275097 FindMyPast Image] - [https://www.findmypast.ie/transcript?id=IRE%2FDIOC%2FWILL%2F00275097&tab=this FindMyPast Transcription] (accessed 11 February 2026)

26355545.Name: Glasgow-987
26355545.bio:
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}} == Biography == '''Thomas Glasgow''' was a farmer of Lisnagaver in Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. His exact birthplace and parents have not been proved. Thomas was born about 1815. His age of 35 in the 1851 census and his reported age of 55 at death in 1870 independently place his birth in approximately 1814–1816.1851 Ireland Census, residents of house 37, Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim, National Archives of Ireland, [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ household return] (accessed 12 May 2025).“Ireland, Deaths, 1864–1870,” digital film/folder 004024453; FHL microfilm 101716; record 2; packet G; {{FamilySearch Record|FGFD-PYC}}; Thomas Glasgow, died 21 June 1870, aged 55, Lisnagaver (accessed 12 May 2025). This is an indexed record; the original civil return remains to be obtained. Thomas married '''[[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]]'''. Their marriage date and congregation have not been identified. No located record names another wife. === Early family === A derivative transcription of the Rasharkin Presbyterian register records three early children: * Eliza Glascaw, born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin; * Eliza Glascow, born 17 October 1843 and baptised 5 November 1843, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver; * Jane Glascaw, born 29 April 1846, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver.Barbara Braswell, transcript of Rasharkin Presbyterian Church baptisms, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html ''Baptisms, 1834–1846''], entries 162, 199 and 269 (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcription; the controlling original register is PRONI MIC1P/292. The two Eliza entries appear to concern separate children. The younger Eliza was still living in 1851. The older child probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but no death or burial record has been found. Her previously assigned death about 1845 is unproved. === 1851 census === Thomas and Mary Ann were recorded at Lisnagaver in the surviving 1851 Irish census. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Lisnagaver household, 1851''' ! Person ! Age ! Recorded status |- | Thomas Glasgow | 35 | Farmer |- | [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann Glasgow]] | 29 | Wife |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | 10 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | 7 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | 5 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | 3 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | 1 | Daughter |- | Catherine McLaughlin | 15 | Servant |} === Children === The evidence does not give every reported child the same status. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Known and reported children''' ! Child ! Evidence ! Assessment |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | Aged ten and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. Her reported later identification with the wife of John Alexander Redpath in New Zealand depends on later family and New Zealand evidence.Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', Find Ancestors message board, posted 25 January 2007, with replies dated 9 April 2020, [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a later family account, not contemporary proof. |- | [[Glasgow-1360|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck to Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin. | Documented by the derivative baptism transcription. She probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but her death date is unknown. |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 October 1843 at Lisnagaver, baptised 5 November and aged seven in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported later identification as Eliza Haigh in New Zealand has not been fully proved. |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | Born 29 April 1846 at Lisnagaver and aged five in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported marriage to Robert Jamieson and migration to New Zealand remain dependent on later evidence. |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | Aged three and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | Aged one and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter. She was probably the daughter called Peggy in the later family account. |- | [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]] | Aged 24 when she gave notice of marriage at Christchurch in October 1877. A derivative Victorian death-index entry reportedly names her mother as Mary Ann McCracken.New Zealand Notices of Intention to Marry, derivative transcription, Christchurch district, 3 October 1877, Catherine Glasgow, age 24, spinster and milliner, three years' residence at Christchurch, intending to marry Benjamin Pherson Ekberg, [https://itm.howison.co.nz/year/1877/district/christchurch transcription] (accessed 9 August 2026).Victoria death index, Catherine Ekberg, 1946, registration 12550, derivative details reproduced in the later Glasgow family discussion; father recorded under the surname Glasgow and mother as Mary Ann McCracken. | Probable daughter. Her original baptism and Victorian death certificate are required. She is also a plausible, but unproved, identification for the Kate Glasgow present at [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]'s death in 1871. |- | [[Glasgow-3975|Sarah Glasgow]] | Four original civil birth returns identify Sarah Taylor, formerly Glasgow, as the wife of Charles Taylor, farmer, at Lisnagaver.Ireland civil birth returns: Ellen Taylor, born 20 January 1897, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1897/02142/1813179.pdf original image]; Catherine Taylor, born 8 April 1899, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1899/02043/1782340.pdf original image]; Charles Taylor, born 21 December 1902, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1902/01892/1735215.pdf original image]; Alexander Taylor, born 28 January 1905, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1905/01798/1705043.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Probable daughter. The records strongly corroborate the reported marriage and Lisnagaver residence but do not name Sarah's father. |- | Alexander Glasgow | Reported to have emigrated to South Africa or the United States. | Possible child only. No contemporary record identifying him as Thomas's son has been found. |- | [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] | His 1888 marriage records him as a farmer of Lisnagaver and son of Thomas Glasgow, farmer.Ireland civil marriage return, no. 79, [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church, County Londonderry, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1888/10763/5925382.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Documented son of Thomas. The marriage does not name his mother. He was recorded as “Full,” meaning over 21, and was therefore born before 28 June 1867.General Register Office for Northern Ireland, [https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/gronis-online-search-results “GRONI's online search results”], explanation that “Full” means over 21 (accessed 9 August 2026). |} Daniel Neely's previously assigned birth about 1870 is incorrect. His age category at marriage proves that he was born before 28 June 1867. === Brother Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea === Thomas was a brother of '''[[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]''', the watch and clock maker of Kilrea. Daniel's registered will refers to:
“my late brother Thomas Glasgow” ... “my nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow”
The will was proved in 1871.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea, proved 1871; refers to his late brother Thomas and nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel Neely's marriage independently names his father as Thomas Glasgow, farmer, and gives his residence as Lisnagaver. Together, the will and marriage identify Daniel of Kilrea as Thomas's brother and Daniel Neely as Thomas's son. Daniel died at Kilrea on 16 October 1871, aged 75. The original civil return names '''Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea''' as the informant.Ireland civil death return, no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871 at Kilrea, aged 75, widower and watchmaker; informant Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The return does not state Kate's relationship to Daniel. === Landholding === A transcript of Griffith's Valuation lists Thomas Glasgow, John Glasgow and Alexander Glasgow as occupiers at Lisnagaver.Griffith's Valuation transcript for Rasharkin parish, [https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-rasharkin.php entries for Lisnagaver] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcript; the original valuation page, map and plot references remain to be checked. Their presence in the same townland makes a relationship plausible but does not establish whether John and Alexander were Thomas's brothers, uncles, cousins or unrelated members of the same surname cluster. The original valuation page and subsequent revision books are required before plot succession can be used as relationship evidence. === Death === Thomas died at Lisnagaver on '''21 June 1870''', aged 55. His reported age is consistent with the age recorded in 1851 and gives an estimated birth in about 1814 or 1815. His burial place has not been identified. === Brother Daniel and the Prescott connection === Thomas was a brother of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], watchmaker of Kilrea. Daniel's will calls Thomas his late brother and Daniel Neely Glasgow his nephew; Daniel Neely's marriage independently identifies Thomas as his father.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871 (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel's death return names Kate Glasgow as informant but gives no relationship.Ireland civil death return no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The original deeds under the will of their brother Robert Glasgow of Prescott independently identify the same Thomas and Daniel. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives shares to his brothers Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas, sister Mary, and collectively the children of brother James; it does not call James deceased.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image]. Memorial 13 records the 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, between Robert's widow Jane and Samuel Glasgow, merchant, concerning Samuel's one undivided sixth share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image]. Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, as transferors to Samuel of two undivided sixth interests under Robert's will.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image]. The deeds establish Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert as brothers; they do not identify their parents. == Research Notes == === Former merge and the Coltrim census === A formerly separate WikiTree profile, '''Glasgow-2994''', was merged into this profile. Its estimated birth about 1823 has no identified contemporary source and conflicts with the approximately 1815 birth indicated by Thomas's 1851 and 1870 ages. The legacy link attached to the merged material referred to a 1901 household at Coltrim, Moneymore DED, County Londonderry. The surviving Form B1 confirms that another Thomas Glasgow was the householder at house 7 in Coltrim and refers to Form A schedule 6. It appears to record four occupants, but it does not give Thomas's age, family relationships, birthplace or occupation.1901 Ireland Census, Form B1, Coltrim townland, Moneymore DED, South Derry, County Londonderry, house 7, householder Thomas Glasgow, Form A schedule 6, National Archives of Ireland, [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=nai000629314 original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). Since the Lisnagaver Thomas died in 1870, the Coltrim return belongs to another man. It does not establish that the Coltrim man was born about 1823. Glasgow-2994 should not be recreated as a separate person unless Form A schedule 6 or another original record establishes his age and family. === Kate Glasgow at Daniel's death === Daniel's civil death return names Kate Glasgow as the informant and says that she was present at his death. It does not call her his sister and does not state any relationship. [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]], probable daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann, is a plausible candidate. She was aged 24 in October 1877 and reported three years' residence at Christchurch. That chronology is consistent with her still being in Ireland in 1871, but does not prove that she was the informant. If the informant was Catherine, Daniel was her uncle, not her brother. An older sister, daughter, daughter-in-law, other niece or cousin remains possible. === Marriage, Daniel's mother and a possible second wife === No record has been found for the marriage of Thomas and Mary Ann. No positive evidence has been found for another wife. Thomas and Mary Ann are named together in the 1842, 1843 and 1846 baptism entries and in the 1851 household. Daniel Neely's marriage names his father but not his mother. Mary Ann is therefore his probable mother, based on the established family and chronology, but the relationship remains unproved. Daniel was born before June 1867 rather than about 1870. Mary Ann, born about 1821, would have been no more than about 45 or 46. The chronology does not require a second marriage. === Parents === A later family account identifies Thomas as a son of '''[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Unknown-761034|Rosanna]]''' and states that Rosanna died about 23 October 1822. No contemporary record naming Thomas's parents has been found. Both relationships should remain uncertain. Rosanna's maiden surname has sometimes been given as Shaw, but no source proving that surname has been identified. === Priority Research === * '''Priority 1 — identify the Coltrim Thomas:''' obtain Form A schedule 6 for house 7, Coltrim, Moneymore DED, 1901. Record every occupant, age, relationship, occupation and birthplace. This will determine whether the discarded circa-1823 estimate had any basis. * '''Priority 1 — later baptisms:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/292, Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, 1847–1867, for Nancy, Margaret, Catherine or Kate, Sarah, Alexander and Daniel Glasgow. Search Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glasco and Glassgow, with McCracken, McCrackin, McCraken and McCochrane variants. A Daniel entry naming Mary Ann would substantially resolve the second-marriage question; another mother would provide the first positive evidence for a second wife.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records ''Guide to Church Records''], entries for Rasharkin Presbyterian MIC1P/292, Second Portglenone MIC1P/357, Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20 (accessed 9 August 2026). * '''Priority 1 — marriage:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/357, Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages, approximately 1838–1842, for Thomas Glasgow and Mary Ann McCracken variants. Also inspect its baptisms for Rose Ann about 1840–1841. If unsuccessful, continue with Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20. * '''Priority 2 — Catherine:''' obtain Catherine Ekberg's original 1946 Victorian death certificate, registration 12550. Record both parents' full names, birthplace, duration in each colony or state and the informant. Compare these details with the 1877 New Zealand marriage notice and the 1871 Kate Glasgow informant. * '''Priority 2 — Sarah:''' locate the marriage of Sarah Glasgow and Charles Taylor, probably before the birth of Ellen Taylor in January 1897. The marriage should state Sarah's age, residence and father. * '''Priority 2 — land succession:''' obtain the original Griffith's Valuation page and map for Lisnagaver and follow Thomas's plot through the valuation-revision books to at least 1888. Determine whether it passed to Mary Ann, Daniel Neely or another relative, and compare the adjoining holdings of John and Alexander Glasgow. * '''Priority 3 — deaths:''' obtain Thomas's original 1870 civil death return and the candidate 1914 death registration for Mary Ann. Record the informants, exact residences and stated relationships rather than relying only on indexes. Robert's sister Mary is independently identified in a 15 September 1869 deed, registered 1 July 1870, as Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow. Her children, including John Black, Rose Ann Black, Jane Miller, Agnes Black and Thomasina Montgomery, conveyed interests under Robert's will to Mary Eno Glasgow; the deed also records their inheritance of their unmarried intestate sister Elizabeth Black's share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200420, image 277, C298, dated 15 September 1869 and registered 1 July 1870, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K original image]. The death of Thomas Glasgow was registered on 21 June 1870 in Ballymoney, aged 55.[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Thomas Glasgow, 21 June 1870, aged 55, Ballymoney registration district, D/1870/31/1005/2/197. == Sources ==

Spouses.Name: Redpath-489
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==

John was born in 1846 (his obituaries do not say where he was born) . 

He arrived in Lyttelton aged 18y in 1864 on the ship ''Le Parisien''.

He was a storekeeper on the West Coast (surviving an encounter with the Burgess-Sullivan gang) and then was a sheep-farmer in the Upper Rangitata then coal importing and storekeeping in Christchurch.

He founded the firm of J. A Redpath and Sons in Christchurch, in which he was involved until about 1912. It was advertised as a ''cheap drapery and grocery establishment (1878) <ref> https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/TS18780819.2.22.2?end_date=30-08-1878&items_per_page=10&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=13-08-1878 </ref> and an agent for coal (1890)<ref> https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/TS18901104.2.13.4?end_date=31-12-1890&items_per_page=10&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-01-1887&type=ADVERTISEMENT </ref> and in 1942 for carpets  <ref> Carpets from Redpaths (1957) https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19421212.2.48?end_date=31-12-1942&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-12-1942  </ref>

He married Rose Anne Glasgow of Christchurch in 1868. 

He passed away in 1942. in Christchurch. <ref> https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19421212.2.48?end_date=31-12-1942&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-12-1942  </ref><ref> https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/GEST19421212.2.24?end_date=31-12-1942&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-12-1942 </ref><ref> https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/GEST19421212.2.24?end_date=31-12-1942&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-12-1942</ref><ref>https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/NZH19421216.2.37?end_date=31-12-1942&items_per_page=10&query=Redpath&snippet=true&start_date=01-12-1942 </ref>

== Sources ==
<references />

Glasgow-1362.Name: Glasgow-1362
Glasgow-1362.bio:
== Biography ==

'''Nancy Glasgow''' was born about 1848 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann (McCracken) Glasgow]].

=== Early Life ===

Nancy was recorded with her family at Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim, in the surviving 1851 census.

She was aged '''3''', giving an estimated birth year of about 1847 or 1848.

The household included:

* [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]], aged 35, farmer;
* [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann (McCracken) Glasgow]], aged 29, wife;
* Rose Ann Glasgow, aged 10;
* Eliza Glasgow, aged 7;
* Jane Glasgow, aged 5;
* '''Nancy Glasgow''', aged 3;
* Margaret Glasgow, aged 1;
* Catherine McLaughlin, aged 15, servant.

<ref name="Census1851">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, County Antrim, household 37, Thomas Glasgow household; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ household return].</ref>

Nancy's parents and siblings formed part of a closely associated Glasgow family network at Lisnagaver. Her father Thomas was a farmer and a probable close relative, possibly a brother, of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], who occupied the nearby household 35.

No surviving record presently proves the exact relationship between Thomas and Alexander.

=== Marriage ===

Nancy married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].

A secondary civil-registration index reports the marriage in the '''Ballymoney registration district''' during the first quarter of '''1879'''. Nancy was indexed as '''Nancy Glasgow''' and Robert's surname appears in the variants '''M‘Caughron''' and '''M‘Caughern'''.<ref name="Marriage1879">[https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 "Trying to find Glasgow", Genes Reunited], discussion quoting the civil-registration index: Nancy Glasgow, Ballymoney registration district, January–March 1879, vol. 1, p. 181, spouse Robert M‘Caughron/M‘Caughern (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a secondary transcription; the original civil marriage registration should be obtained.</ref>

This marriage is particularly relevant to the wider Glasgow family network.

Nancy's father [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] was married to [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]], while Thomas's probable close relative [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] was married to [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]].

Nancy's own marriage to Robert McCaughen therefore provides another direct connection between the Glasgow and McCaughen families in the wider County Antrim network.

The relationship, if any, between [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]] and [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]] has not yet been established.

=== New Zealand ===

Nancy is reported to have later lived in New Zealand.

A burial on '''22 September 1937''' at '''Linwood Cemetery, Christchurch, Canterbury, New Zealand''' has been attributed to her.

The original cemetery or death record supporting this identification has not yet been added to this profile. Until it is obtained, the burial should be treated as provisional rather than as a proved life event.
A marriage for Annie Glasgow and McCaughern was registered on 14 May 1879 in the Coleraine district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 14 May 1879, Coleraine district, M/1879/K1/1048/4/75.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Name ===

Nancy is recorded as '''Nancy Glasgow''' in the 1851 census and in the secondary index of her 1879 marriage.

A FamilySearch collaborative-tree entry associated with this family uses the name '''Annie Glasgow'''.<ref name="FamilySearch">FamilySearch Family Tree, database, entry for Annie Glasgow, PID [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MQ57-1NV MQ57-1NV]. FamilySearch Family Tree is user-contributed and should not be treated as an original genealogical source.</ref>

Nancy can historically occur as a familiar form associated with Ann or Anne, but the FamilySearch naming should not by itself be used to change her documented name from Nancy.

=== McCracken and McCaughen ===

Nancy's mother is recorded as [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]].

The surname '''McCracken''' should not presently be treated as a transcription variant of '''McCaughen/McAughern'''.

The Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription repeatedly distinguishes the two surnames within the same register. Thomas Glasgow's wife appears as Mary Ann McCrackin or McCracken, while [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s wife appears as Mary or Molly McAughin/McAughern.

Inspection of the original Rasharkin Presbyterian register, PRONI '''MIC.1P/292''', remains desirable before treating any particular spelling as definitive.

=== Glasgow–McCaughen Network ===

Nancy's marriage is significant because several links connect the two surname groups:

* Nancy was the daughter of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]];
* Nancy married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]];
* Thomas's probable close relative [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] married [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]];
* Alexander and Thomas lived in the same small Lisnagaver community;
* Alexander and Thomas later occupied consecutive valuation lots 25 and 26 under the same landlord.

These facts support a close local FAN network.

They do '''not''' yet establish that Robert McCaughen and Mary McCaughan were siblings or otherwise closely related.

=== Thomas and Alexander Glasgow ===

[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] were both County Antrim farmers associated with the same small Lisnagaver–Gortereagh–Moneyleck area.

They used the same Rasharkin Presbyterian congregation, headed closely grouped households in the surviving 1851 census, and later occupied consecutive valuation lots.

Their children also appear close together in the Rasharkin Presbyterian register. Alexander's son James was born at Lisnagaver on 9 October 1843, while Thomas's daughter Eliza was born there eight days later on 17 October 1843.

This provides substantial circumstantial evidence for a close relationship.

No surviving record presently calls Thomas and Alexander brothers. Thomas should therefore be treated as Alexander's '''probable close relative and possible brother''', not as a proved sibling.

=== Burial and Death ===

The reported burial date of '''22 September 1937''' at Linwood Cemetery requires verification.

Priority evidence would be:

* the Christchurch cemetery interment entry;
* a New Zealand civil death registration;
* probate or administration;
* a newspaper death notice or obituary;
* passenger or immigration evidence connecting Nancy and Robert to New Zealand.

The burial should not be treated as proved solely from a collaborative FamilySearch tree.

=== Priority Research ===

* Obtain the original 1879 civil marriage registration for Nancy Glasgow and [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].
* Record Nancy's residence, age, occupation and father's name and occupation.
* Record Robert's residence, age, occupation, father and father's occupation.
* Record the church, minister and both witnesses.
* Establish Robert McCaughen's parents and siblings.
* Investigate whether Robert was related to [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].
* Verify Nancy and Robert's migration to New Zealand.
* Obtain the original New Zealand death and Linwood Cemetery records.
* Search New Zealand records under McCaughen, McCaughern, McCaughan and related spelling variants.

26355545.bio:
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}} == Biography == '''Thomas Glasgow''' was a farmer of Lisnagaver in Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. His exact birthplace and parents have not been proved. Thomas was born about 1815. His age of 35 in the 1851 census and his reported age of 55 at death in 1870 independently place his birth in approximately 1814–1816.1851 Ireland Census, residents of house 37, Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim, National Archives of Ireland, [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/37/ household return] (accessed 12 May 2025).“Ireland, Deaths, 1864–1870,” digital film/folder 004024453; FHL microfilm 101716; record 2; packet G; {{FamilySearch Record|FGFD-PYC}}; Thomas Glasgow, died 21 June 1870, aged 55, Lisnagaver (accessed 12 May 2025). This is an indexed record; the original civil return remains to be obtained. Thomas married '''[[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]]'''. Their marriage date and congregation have not been identified. No located record names another wife. === Early family === A derivative transcription of the Rasharkin Presbyterian register records three early children: * Eliza Glascaw, born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin; * Eliza Glascow, born 17 October 1843 and baptised 5 November 1843, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver; * Jane Glascaw, born 29 April 1846, daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann McCracken of Lisnagaver.Barbara Braswell, transcript of Rasharkin Presbyterian Church baptisms, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html ''Baptisms, 1834–1846''], entries 162, 199 and 269 (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcription; the controlling original register is PRONI MIC1P/292. The two Eliza entries appear to concern separate children. The younger Eliza was still living in 1851. The older child probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but no death or burial record has been found. Her previously assigned death about 1845 is unproved. === 1851 census === Thomas and Mary Ann were recorded at Lisnagaver in the surviving 1851 Irish census. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Lisnagaver household, 1851''' ! Person ! Age ! Recorded status |- | Thomas Glasgow | 35 | Farmer |- | [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann Glasgow]] | 29 | Wife |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | 10 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | 7 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | 5 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | 3 | Daughter |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | 1 | Daughter |- | Catherine McLaughlin | 15 | Servant |} === Children === The evidence does not give every reported child the same status. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ '''Known and reported children''' ! Child ! Evidence ! Assessment |- | [[Glasgow-1034|Rose Ann Glasgow]] | Aged ten and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. Her reported later identification with the wife of John Alexander Redpath in New Zealand depends on later family and New Zealand evidence.Peter, “Trying to find Glasgow,” ''Genes Reunited'', Find Ancestors message board, posted 25 January 2007, with replies dated 9 April 2020, [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 discussion] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a later family account, not contemporary proof. |- | [[Glasgow-1360|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 August 1842 at Moneyleck to Thomas and Mary Ann McCrackin. | Documented by the derivative baptism transcription. She probably died before the younger Eliza was named, but her death date is unknown. |- | [[Glasgow-782|Eliza Glasgow]] | Born 17 October 1843 at Lisnagaver, baptised 5 November and aged seven in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported later identification as Eliza Haigh in New Zealand has not been fully proved. |- | [[Glasgow-1361|Jane Glasgow]] | Born 29 April 1846 at Lisnagaver and aged five in 1851. | Documented daughter. Her reported marriage to Robert Jamieson and migration to New Zealand remain dependent on later evidence. |- | [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] | Aged three and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann. |- | [[Glasgow-1363|Margaret Glasgow]] | Aged one and recorded as a daughter in 1851. | Documented daughter. She was probably the daughter called Peggy in the later family account. |- | [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]] | Aged 24 when she gave notice of marriage at Christchurch in October 1877. A derivative Victorian death-index entry reportedly names her mother as Mary Ann McCracken.New Zealand Notices of Intention to Marry, derivative transcription, Christchurch district, 3 October 1877, Catherine Glasgow, age 24, spinster and milliner, three years' residence at Christchurch, intending to marry Benjamin Pherson Ekberg, [https://itm.howison.co.nz/year/1877/district/christchurch transcription] (accessed 9 August 2026).Victoria death index, Catherine Ekberg, 1946, registration 12550, derivative details reproduced in the later Glasgow family discussion; father recorded under the surname Glasgow and mother as Mary Ann McCracken. | Probable daughter. Her original baptism and Victorian death certificate are required. She is also a plausible, but unproved, identification for the Kate Glasgow present at [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]'s death in 1871. |- | [[Glasgow-3975|Sarah Glasgow]] | Four original civil birth returns identify Sarah Taylor, formerly Glasgow, as the wife of Charles Taylor, farmer, at Lisnagaver.Ireland civil birth returns: Ellen Taylor, born 20 January 1897, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1897/02142/1813179.pdf original image]; Catherine Taylor, born 8 April 1899, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1899/02043/1782340.pdf original image]; Charles Taylor, born 21 December 1902, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1902/01892/1735215.pdf original image]; Alexander Taylor, born 28 January 1905, Lisnagaver, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1905/01798/1705043.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Probable daughter. The records strongly corroborate the reported marriage and Lisnagaver residence but do not name Sarah's father. |- | Alexander Glasgow | Reported to have emigrated to South Africa or the United States. | Possible child only. No contemporary record identifying him as Thomas's son has been found. |- | [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] | His 1888 marriage records him as a farmer of Lisnagaver and son of Thomas Glasgow, farmer.Ireland civil marriage return, no. 79, [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] and Mary Jane Boyd, 28 June 1888, Boveedy First Presbyterian Church, County Londonderry, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1888/10763/5925382.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). | Documented son of Thomas. The marriage does not name his mother. He was recorded as “Full,” meaning over 21, and was therefore born before 28 June 1867.General Register Office for Northern Ireland, [https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/gronis-online-search-results “GRONI's online search results”], explanation that “Full” means over 21 (accessed 9 August 2026). |} Daniel Neely's previously assigned birth about 1870 is incorrect. His age category at marriage proves that he was born before 28 June 1867. === Brother Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea === Thomas was a brother of '''[[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]]''', the watch and clock maker of Kilrea. Daniel's registered will refers to:
“my late brother Thomas Glasgow” ... “my nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow”
The will was proved in 1871.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea, proved 1871; refers to his late brother Thomas and nephew Daniel Neely Glasgow (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel Neely's marriage independently names his father as Thomas Glasgow, farmer, and gives his residence as Lisnagaver. Together, the will and marriage identify Daniel of Kilrea as Thomas's brother and Daniel Neely as Thomas's son. Daniel died at Kilrea on 16 October 1871, aged 75. The original civil return names '''Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea''' as the informant.Ireland civil death return, no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871 at Kilrea, aged 75, widower and watchmaker; informant Kate Glasgow, present at death, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The return does not state Kate's relationship to Daniel. === Landholding === A transcript of Griffith's Valuation lists Thomas Glasgow, John Glasgow and Alexander Glasgow as occupiers at Lisnagaver.Griffith's Valuation transcript for Rasharkin parish, [https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-rasharkin.php entries for Lisnagaver] (accessed 9 August 2026). This is a derivative transcript; the original valuation page, map and plot references remain to be checked. Their presence in the same townland makes a relationship plausible but does not establish whether John and Alexander were Thomas's brothers, uncles, cousins or unrelated members of the same surname cluster. The original valuation page and subsequent revision books are required before plot succession can be used as relationship evidence. === Death === Thomas died at Lisnagaver on '''21 June 1870''', aged 55. His reported age is consistent with the age recorded in 1851 and gives an estimated birth in about 1814 or 1815. His burial place has not been identified. === Brother Daniel and the Prescott connection === Thomas was a brother of [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], watchmaker of Kilrea. Daniel's will calls Thomas his late brother and Daniel Neely Glasgow his nephew; Daniel Neely's marriage independently identifies Thomas as his father.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/willscalendar_ie/willssearch.aspx Will Calendars], registered will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871 (accessed 17 July 2026). Daniel's death return names Kate Glasgow as informant but gives no relationship.Ireland civil death return no. 362, [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]], died 16 October 1871, Kilrea, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1871/020759/7282767.pdf original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). The original deeds under the will of their brother Robert Glasgow of Prescott independently identify the same Thomas and Daniel. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives shares to his brothers Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas, sister Mary, and collectively the children of brother James; it does not call James deceased.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image]. Memorial 13 records the 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, between Robert's widow Jane and Samuel Glasgow, merchant, concerning Samuel's one undivided sixth share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image]. Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, as transferors to Samuel of two undivided sixth interests under Robert's will.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image]. The deeds establish Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert as brothers; they do not identify their parents. == Research Notes == === Former merge and the Coltrim census === A formerly separate WikiTree profile, '''Glasgow-2994''', was merged into this profile. Its estimated birth about 1823 has no identified contemporary source and conflicts with the approximately 1815 birth indicated by Thomas's 1851 and 1870 ages. The legacy link attached to the merged material referred to a 1901 household at Coltrim, Moneymore DED, County Londonderry. The surviving Form B1 confirms that another Thomas Glasgow was the householder at house 7 in Coltrim and refers to Form A schedule 6. It appears to record four occupants, but it does not give Thomas's age, family relationships, birthplace or occupation.1901 Ireland Census, Form B1, Coltrim townland, Moneymore DED, South Derry, County Londonderry, house 7, householder Thomas Glasgow, Form A schedule 6, National Archives of Ireland, [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=nai000629314 original image] (accessed 9 August 2026). Since the Lisnagaver Thomas died in 1870, the Coltrim return belongs to another man. It does not establish that the Coltrim man was born about 1823. Glasgow-2994 should not be recreated as a separate person unless Form A schedule 6 or another original record establishes his age and family. === Kate Glasgow at Daniel's death === Daniel's civil death return names Kate Glasgow as the informant and says that she was present at his death. It does not call her his sister and does not state any relationship. [[Glasgow-3976|Catherine Glasgow]], probable daughter of Thomas and Mary Ann, is a plausible candidate. She was aged 24 in October 1877 and reported three years' residence at Christchurch. That chronology is consistent with her still being in Ireland in 1871, but does not prove that she was the informant. If the informant was Catherine, Daniel was her uncle, not her brother. An older sister, daughter, daughter-in-law, other niece or cousin remains possible. === Marriage, Daniel's mother and a possible second wife === No record has been found for the marriage of Thomas and Mary Ann. No positive evidence has been found for another wife. Thomas and Mary Ann are named together in the 1842, 1843 and 1846 baptism entries and in the 1851 household. Daniel Neely's marriage names his father but not his mother. Mary Ann is therefore his probable mother, based on the established family and chronology, but the relationship remains unproved. Daniel was born before June 1867 rather than about 1870. Mary Ann, born about 1821, would have been no more than about 45 or 46. The chronology does not require a second marriage. === Parents === A later family account identifies Thomas as a son of '''[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Unknown-761034|Rosanna]]''' and states that Rosanna died about 23 October 1822. No contemporary record naming Thomas's parents has been found. Both relationships should remain uncertain. Rosanna's maiden surname has sometimes been given as Shaw, but no source proving that surname has been identified. === Priority Research === * '''Priority 1 — identify the Coltrim Thomas:''' obtain Form A schedule 6 for house 7, Coltrim, Moneymore DED, 1901. Record every occupant, age, relationship, occupation and birthplace. This will determine whether the discarded circa-1823 estimate had any basis. * '''Priority 1 — later baptisms:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/292, Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, 1847–1867, for Nancy, Margaret, Catherine or Kate, Sarah, Alexander and Daniel Glasgow. Search Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glasco and Glassgow, with McCracken, McCrackin, McCraken and McCochrane variants. A Daniel entry naming Mary Ann would substantially resolve the second-marriage question; another mother would provide the first positive evidence for a second wife.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records ''Guide to Church Records''], entries for Rasharkin Presbyterian MIC1P/292, Second Portglenone MIC1P/357, Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20 (accessed 9 August 2026). * '''Priority 1 — marriage:''' inspect PRONI MIC1P/357, Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages, approximately 1838–1842, for Thomas Glasgow and Mary Ann McCracken variants. Also inspect its baptisms for Rose Ann about 1840–1841. If unsuccessful, continue with Boveedy MIC1P/18, First Kilrea MIC1P/87 and Second Kilrea MIC1P/20. * '''Priority 2 — Catherine:''' obtain Catherine Ekberg's original 1946 Victorian death certificate, registration 12550. Record both parents' full names, birthplace, duration in each colony or state and the informant. Compare these details with the 1877 New Zealand marriage notice and the 1871 Kate Glasgow informant. * '''Priority 2 — Sarah:''' locate the marriage of Sarah Glasgow and Charles Taylor, probably before the birth of Ellen Taylor in January 1897. The marriage should state Sarah's age, residence and father. * '''Priority 2 — land succession:''' obtain the original Griffith's Valuation page and map for Lisnagaver and follow Thomas's plot through the valuation-revision books to at least 1888. Determine whether it passed to Mary Ann, Daniel Neely or another relative, and compare the adjoining holdings of John and Alexander Glasgow. * '''Priority 3 — deaths:''' obtain Thomas's original 1870 civil death return and the candidate 1914 death registration for Mary Ann. Record the informants, exact residences and stated relationships rather than relying only on indexes. Robert's sister Mary is independently identified in a 15 September 1869 deed, registered 1 July 1870, as Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow. Her children, including John Black, Rose Ann Black, Jane Miller, Agnes Black and Thomasina Montgomery, conveyed interests under Robert's will to Mary Eno Glasgow; the deed also records their inheritance of their unmarried intestate sister Elizabeth Black's share.Grenville County land records, DGS 8200420, image 277, C298, dated 15 September 1869 and registered 1 July 1870, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K original image]. The death of Thomas Glasgow was registered on 21 June 1870 in Ballymoney, aged 55.[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Thomas Glasgow, 21 June 1870, aged 55, Ballymoney registration district, D/1870/31/1005/2/197. == Sources ==
