== Biography == '''Ann “Annie” Glasgow''' was born about 1848 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was a daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], a farmer, and [[Unknown-540861|Margaret Unknown]]. In 1851, Ann was living with her family at house 34 in Lisnagaver, in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim. Her father, John Glasgow, was recorded as a 50-year-old farmer born in County Antrim. '''1851 Census of Ireland''':
The National Archives of Ireland; residents of house 34 in Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, Kilconway, County Antrim.
[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf Census image] — [https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/ Transcription] (accessed 17 April 2024). On 18 February 1875, Annie Glasgow married '''Francis Bellingham''' at Finvoy Parish Church, County Antrim, according to the rites of the Church of Ireland. Both were described as being of full age. Francis was a bachelor and farmer residing at Culmore in the parish of Rasharkin. Annie was a spinster residing in the parish of Rasharkin. Their fathers were recorded as Thomas Bellingham and John Glasgow, both farmers. '''Civil marriage registration''': Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875; Ballymoney registration district; Group Registration ID 2857472; image path: marriage_returns\marriages_1875\11190\8100682.tif. The marriage witnesses were Thomas Bellingham and Mary Anne McCaughern. '''Civil marriage registration''': Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875; Ballymoney registration district; Group Registration ID 2857472. Mary Anne McCaughern may have been [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]. If so, her presence as a witness may indicate a connection between Annie’s family and that of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]. The identification is plausible but should not be treated as proven from the marriage record alone. A marriage for Annie Glasgow and Bellingham was registered on 18 February 1875 in the Ballymoney district.[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 18 February 1875, Ballymoney district, M/1875/I1/263/1/46. == Research Notes == Ann’s estimated birth year is uncertain. A birth about 1848 is consistent with her presence in the 1851 census and with her being recorded as “full age” when she married in 1875. The previously stated birth year of 1857 cannot be correct if she was the same Ann recorded in the 1851 household. The names Ann and Annie were commonly used interchangeably in Irish records of this period. == Sources == * [https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/ 1851 Census of Ireland: Glasgow household, Lisnagaver]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was a farmer of Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin,
County Antrim. His date of birth is uncertain. The 1851 census reported his age
as fifty, while the family gravestone says that he died in 1895 aged seventy-
eight, implying birth about 1816 or 1817.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Lisnagaver house 34, Rasharkin, County Antrim; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf original census image].</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html Pauline O'Keeffe and Helen Evans, ''Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones''], transcription made August 2004, Glasgo memorial erected by James Garvin Glasgo.</ref>

John married [[Garvin-1831|Margaret Garvin]] on 16 November 1846. The original
register describes him as a bachelor farmer of Lisnagaver and names his father
as '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Margaret was a spinster.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3156063 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of John Glasgow and Margaret Garvin, 16 November 1846, Ballymena registration district, group registration ID 3156063; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1846/09306/5369439.pdf original register image].</ref>
Her father was '''James Garvin, farmer'''. James Garvin and Ann Kelly witnessed
The marriage.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The 1851 household contained John, Margaret, their three-year-old daughter
[[Glasgow-1371|Ann]], and John's brother [[Glasgow-2908|Samuel Glasgow]]. John
Patterson, a fifteen-year-old linen weaver, was their servant. The return records
1846 as the marriage year and explicitly describes Samuel as John's brother.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

Ann married [[Bellingham-700|Francis Bellingham]] on 18 February 1875. Her
marriage names her father as John Glasgow, farmer.<ref name="AnnMarriage1875">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875, Finvoy parish church, entry 40.</ref>

John and Margaret also had a son, [[Glasgow-2406|James Garvin Glasgow]]. James's
1886 marriage records him as a Lisnagaver farmer and son of John Glasgow,
farmer. The family gravestone identifies Margaret Garvin as his mother.<ref name="JamesMarriage1886">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10840/5957283.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Garvin Glasgow and Eliza Ann Aiken, 1 July 1886, Clough, entry 62.</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

The gravestone records that Margaret died on 10 January 1892 aged seventy-four
and John died on 20 June 1895 aged seventy-eight. Their son James erected the
memorial at Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

=== Marriage ===
John married [[Garvin-1831|Margaret Garvin]] on '''16 November 1846''' at '''Second Garvagh Presbyterian Church''', in Errigal parish, County Londonderry. The marriage was by licence and was registered in '''Coleraine''', not Ballymena.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The contemporary return describes John as a full-age bachelor and farmer of '''Lisnagaver, parish of Rasharkin''', son of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Margaret was a full-age spinster of '''Rockfield, parish of Desertoghill''', daughter of '''James Garvin, farmer'''.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The witnesses were '''James Garvin''' and a man whose name was read as '''Wm Keely''', not the previously reported Ann Kelly. The second surname remains a handwriting reading rather than an established identification. Neither witness's relationship to the couple is stated; the witness James Garvin should not automatically be identified as Margaret's father. The minister's signature was read as James B. Rentoul.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

=== Lisnagaver household, 1851 ===
The surviving census places the family at '''house 34, Lisnagaver'''. It records 1846 as John and Margaret's marriage year, agreeing with their marriage return.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

The return directly establishes that '''Samuel was John's brother'''. It contains '''five household members, not five children''': Ann is the only child of John listed in this household.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

=== Children ===
The following children are supported by the household and family records. This is not necessarily a complete child group.

* '''[[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]]''', aged three in 1851 and born in County Londonderry. The working identification is '''Annie Glasgow''', who married [[Bellingham-700|Francis Bellingham]] on '''18 February 1875''' at Finvoy parish church. Annie was a full-age spinster of the '''parish of Rasharkin''', daughter of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Francis was a full-age bachelor and farmer of Culmore, parish of Rasharkin, son of Thomas Bellingham, farmer. The witnesses were Thomas Bellingham and Mary Ann M'Caughern, as read. The marriage does not name Annie's mother or supply a townland for her, so it is consistent with, but does not alone complete, the identification with the census daughter.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" /><ref name="AnnMarriage1875">General Register Office of Ireland, contemporary civil marriage return, Ballymoney registration district, page 191, entry 40: Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875, Finvoy parish church, County Antrim. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf Register image].</ref>
* '''[[Glasgow-2406|James Garvin Glasgow]]'''. His marriage to '''Eliza Ann Aiken''' on '''1 July 1886''' at Clough describes him as a Lisnagaver farmer and son of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. The family memorial, known through transcription, names John and Margaret Garvin as his parents.<ref name="JamesMarriage1886">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage return, entry 62: James Garvin Glasgow and Eliza Ann Aiken, 1 July 1886, Clough. [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10840/5957283.pdf Register image].</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

James's original death return independently records his full name as '''James Garvin Glasgow'''. He died at Lisnagaver on '''14 February 1918''', a married farmer aged '''64''', from acute pneumonia of six days' duration, certified. The informant was '''Eliza Ann Glasgow, widow, present at death, Lisnagaver'''; registration followed on 8 March 1918.<ref name="JamesDeath1918">General Register Office of Ireland, contemporary civil death return, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, County Antrim, entry 165: James Garvin Glasgow, Lisnagaver, 14 February 1918; registered 8 March 1918. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1918/05197/4435754.pdf Register image].</ref>

The memorial transcription gives James's age as '''67''', not 64. These are conflicting reported ages and should not be silently harmonised. His widow's name is not evidence for a sister called Lizzie.<ref name="JamesDeath1918" /><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

=== Death and family memorial ===
The GLASGO memorial at '''Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church''' was erected by James Garvin Glasgo and names his father John and mother Margaret Garvin. The available source is a modern transcription made by '''Pauline O'Keeffe and Helen Evans in August 2004'''; a photograph of this particular stone has not yet been inspected.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

The 1885 return gives the cause of death as '''cancer in lip, three years''', with no medical attendant. It directly documents a '''John Glasgow and son James at Lisnagaver'''. It does not name John's wife, give James a middle name, or state James's age.<ref name="JohnDeath1885" />

The deceased has a separate profile, [[Glasgow-3474|John Glasgow]]. An earlier version of this biography excluded him solely because the memorial transcription gives 1895. '''That exclusion was not justified.''' The same age, the Lisnagaver connection and the son James make identity with this John a substantial possibility.

'''A transcription error is a plausible explanation, not an established correction.''' Both the day and year differ: '''24 June 1885''' against '''20 June 1895'''. A photograph could show whether the published transcription misreads the stone; if the stone itself says 1895, the conflict would still need investigation. Different men, an error on the memorial, or another record error remain possible. The agreement in age does not by itself settle identity.<ref name="JohnDeath1885" /><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

The memorial transcription also records:
* '''Margaret Garvin''', James's mother, died '''10 January 1892''', aged '''74'''.
* '''John Garvin''', an infant son of James.
* '''James Garvin''', died '''14 February 1918''', aged '''67'''.
* '''Elizabeth Ann''', died '''16 June 1933''', aged '''84'''.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

Margaret's original January 1892 death registration has not yet been obtained. Her married or widowed status, address and informant could help distinguish the competing death scenarios, once the record is securely identified as hers. A matching 1895 civil death has likewise not been verified.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

==== Parentage ====
John's marriage proves that his father was another '''John Glasgow, farmer'''.
The father is currently represented by [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] as an
uncertain working identification. No record yet gives the older man's residence,
wife or age. If the gravestone age is correct, the older John would have been
about sixty-five when this John was born; possible, but not enough to identify
him uniquely.

The conflict between the 1851 age of fifty and the gravestone age of seventy-
eight at death remains unresolved. The marriage, residence, wife and 1846
marriage year securely identify the 1851 household, while the gravestone was
erected by the couple's son and names both parents. The birth year should
therefore remain estimated.

==== Alexander Glasgow of Glenleslie ====
[[Glasgow-2385|Alexander Glasgow]] was previously attached as John's son.
However, Alexander was already a full-age bachelor when he married in April
1847, only five months after John and Margaret's marriage. Alexander's original
marriage also names his father as '''John Glasgow, labourer'''. He was detached
from this household because he belongs to an older, separate father-John branch.<ref name="AlexanderMarriage1847">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1847/09322/5375567.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Alexander Glasgow and Mary Anne Martin, 6 April 1847, Clogh, entry 31; derivative [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGVD-P9CS FamilySearch index entry].</ref>

==== Same-name records ====
The following FamilySearch records describe other men named John Glasgow and
are retained as identity checks: a [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KDXL-YJ1 reported 1849 birth at sea], an [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6HW-FPR 1870 Illinois resident], and a [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M47Q-56D Canadian household]. None contains Margaret Garvin, Lisnagaver or another feature identifying this John.

=== Birth estimate ===
Three different birth estimates arise from the records under comparison:

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Record
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Reported age
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Approximate birth implied
|-
| 1851 census || 50 || 1800 or 1801
|-
| Possible 1885 death || 78 || 1806 or 1807
|-
| Published 1895 memorial date || 78 || 1816 or 1817
|}

These estimates should not be averaged. '''About 1800 or 1801''' may be retained as a census-based working estimate, but it is not a resolved birth date. Even if the 1885 death and this profile describe the same man, that would leave a discrepancy with the census age.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" /><ref name="JohnDeath1885" /><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

Earlier descriptions of John as born before 1798 depended on the former attachment of Alexander Glasgow as his son. That attachment is not a sound basis for dating John's birth.

=== Father and earlier parentage theories ===
The marriage return establishes a father named '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. It does '''not''' identify him uniquely as [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow of Glenleslie]], nor give his residence, wife or age.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

John of Glenleslie remains a possible father and may be retained as an '''uncertain working placement'''. Shared name and occupation do not prove the connection. The earlier identification of John and Samuel as sons of that John and Rose Alexander has no demonstrated contemporary link to the Lisnagaver household.

An alternative reconstruction made the brothers sons of '''Adam Glasgow and Rose''', based on ages, Samuel's County Londonderry birthplace, the Inishrush family's proximity and the wider local Glasgow cluster. That theory conflicts with John's recorded father. A proposed father [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] likewise conflicts with the marriage return. There is no current evidence that the father's name in the return is wrong.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

Samuel's stated brotherhood supports investigating the two men together, but does not identify their parents. A half-brother relationship is possible in principle, not something established by the census.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

The Glenleslie John and the Lisnagaver John should also not be treated as the same man: their reported 1851 ages imply substantially different generations. The suggested connection is father and son, not a same-person identification.

=== Possible connection to Nancy Glasgow of Plattsburgh ===
A probate citation for '''Nancy Glasgow of Plattsburgh, New York''', dated '''14 January 1892''' and published in ''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'' on '''26 February 1892''', names:

: ''"James G. Glasgow, Ann [blank] and Lizzie [blank], the children of John Glasgow, late of Baladonly, county Antrime, Ireland".''<ref name="NancyCitation1892">''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 26 February 1892, page 6, legal notice concerning Nancy Glasgow, deceased; citation dated 14 January 1892, returnable 9 May 1892. Contemporary newspaper clipping inspected in the research; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 newspaper issue locator]. Square-bracketed blanks in the quotation represent printed dashes where surnames were not supplied.</ref>

'''This John is the strongest current working candidate for the citation's John''', because his family includes a son James Garvin and a daughter Ann. The identification remains unproved:

* '''James G.''' is a strong candidate for [[Glasgow-2406|James Garvin Glasgow]]. The 1918 civil return independently establishes Garvin as that man's middle name, but does not identify him as Nancy's cited relative.<ref name="JamesDeath1918" />
* '''Ann''' is a candidate for [[Glasgow-1371|Ann/Annie Glasgow, later Bellingham]]. The 1875 marriage provides a father John, but does not identify Nancy or supply the missing sibling group.<ref name="AnnMarriage1875" />
* '''Lizzie''' remains unidentified. No recovered record yet establishes her as a daughter of John and Margaret.

'''Baladonly''' remains unresolved; '''Baladony''' is retained as a search variant. It should not be silently replaced with Lisnagaver or another townland. The notice leaves the daughters' surnames blank and describes the cited Glasgow children's residences as unknown, so it does not establish that they lived in New York or remained in their fathers' Irish localities.<ref name="NancyCitation1892" />

The phrase '''"late of"''' is not treated as independent proof of John's death. A death in 1885 would precede the citation; a death in 1895 would not. The wording alone cannot choose between those dates.

The same notice names '''Mary Jane and Ann, children of Robert Glasgow''', and a separate child group under Alexander Glasgow. It does '''not''' explicitly state that John, Robert and Alexander were Nancy's brothers. A sibling reconstruction, or an older-Alexander/cousin reconstruction, remains a hypothesis rather than a relationship stated in the notice.<ref name="NancyCitation1892" />

The citation's Robert remains unidentified. Existing candidates [[Glasgow-1367|Robert of Glenleslie]], [[Glasgow-3941|Robert of Coltrim]], [[Glasgow-3449|Robert who died in Ballymoney district in 1868]], [[Glasgow-938|Robert, son of Alexander of Lisnagaver]], and [[Glasgow-1049|Robert of the Doonbought/Illinois branch]] have not supplied the required documented Mary Jane and Ann daughter pair in the research reviewed. Neither the shared surname nor the 1834 Lisnagaver tithe Robert establishes a relationship to this John.

==== Unresolved Elizabeth witness lead ====
A modern transcription of marriages involving Cullybackey people records '''Elizabeth Glasgow''' as a witness, with John Taylor, to the marriage of '''Moore Paul of Carnlea''' and '''Lizzie Rock of Dunminning''' at Killymorris Presbyterian Church on '''3 May 1878'''. The stated fathers are David Paul and John Rock respectively.<ref name="ElizabethWitness1878">Cullybackey and District Historical Society, [https://cullybackeyhistory.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/CULLYBACKEY-PEOPLE-MARRIED-IN-OTHER-CHURCH-1870-1921.pdf ''Cullybackey People Married in Other Churches, 1870-1921''], PDF page 4, Moore Paul and Lizzie Rock, 3 May 1878. Modern transcription table inspected; underlying marriage return not inspected for this lead.</ref>

No father, age or residence is given for witness Elizabeth. '''She is not the bride''', and this does not identify her as the citation's Lizzie or as John's daughter. It is retained only as a record to follow, not an additional child.

=== Former child attachments and same-name checks ===
'''[[Glasgow-2385|Alexander Glasgow]]''' was previously attached as John's son. He was already a full-age bachelor when he married Mary Anne Martin on '''6 April 1847''', only five months after John and Margaret's marriage, and his marriage return names his father as '''John Glasgow, labourer'''. The proposed attachment has been removed; this record does not establish him as a child of John and Margaret. His father belongs to a separate working reconstruction rather than being identified through this household.<ref name="AlexanderMarriage1847">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage return, entry 31: Alexander Glasgow and Mary Anne Martin, 6 April 1847, Clogh. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1847/09322/5375567.pdf Register image]; derivative [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGVD-P9CS FamilySearch index], retained as a finding aid.</ref>

'''[[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1840''', is supported in the existing research as a son of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver]], not a child of this John. Repeated given names are not grounds for restoring the attachment.

Other retained same-name checks concern [[Glasgow-3140|John Glasgow, born about 1820]], [[Glasgow-427|John Glasgow, born about 1789 and associated with Scotland]], a John reportedly born at sea on '''25 August 1849''' and later associated with Macoupin County, Illinois, and a John born about 1810 associated with Jane Glasgow and Ontario. The cited derivative records do not supply Margaret Garvin, Lisnagaver or another identifying link to this household.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KDXL-YJ1 FamilySearch record], John Glasgow, reported birth during a voyage to New York, 25 August 1849; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6HW-FPR FamilySearch record], John Glasgow in Illinois, 1870. Retained derivative identity checks, not evidence for this John's life.</ref><ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M47Q-56D FamilySearch record], John and Jane Glasgow, Ontario. Retained derivative identity check.</ref>

'''The 1885 Lisnagaver John is different from these excluded or unsupported matches: his comparison remains open.''' The son-informant associated with [[Glasgow-4043|James Glasgow]] has no age or birth year in the death return. An estimated date attached to that profile cannot independently exclude his being James Garvin.<ref name="JohnDeath1885" />

The concentration of Glasgow households is useful geographical context, not proof that their heads were brothers or father and son. In particular, no direct evidence currently makes Robert of Danbought John's father or brother. The separate question of Alexander's father must be tested against Alexander's own records rather than answered from neighbouring households.

Earlier naming arguments concerned a Matilda reportedly associated with John's family who died aged 23, a later Matilda said to have been named 22 years afterwards in Robert Glasgow's branch, and another Matilda born in 1901 in the family associated with [[Glasgow-943|Glasgow-943]]. Those notes described the two Roberts as 1840-1902 and 1880-1931; these date ranges and the claimed connections have not been established by the records examined for this update. The earlier notes also mentioned repeated use of Archibald. These are retained as unverified leads, not evidence of parentage or a reason to restore detached children.

=== Further research ===
# '''Obtain a photograph or independent reading of the GLASGO memorial.''' The target is the stone erected by James Garvin, naming John, Margaret Garvin and Elizabeth Ann. Check both the day and year of John's death. The [https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/2561344/rasharkin-presbyterian-church-graveyard Find a Grave cemetery entry] was located, but the individual memorial photographs could not be fully inspected. No photograph of this particular stone was located in the searches completed by 15 September 2026. Ballymoney Museum's inventory lists '''"Rasharkin Presbyterian Church, Graveyard Descriptions"''' under Booklets, on PDF page 13. It may supply an independent reading or grave locator; the inventory does not establish that the booklet contains photographs.<ref name="MuseumInventory">Ballymoney Museum, [https://niarchive.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Ballymoney-History-Resource-Area-Inventory.pdf ''History Resource Area Inventory''], PDF page 13, Booklets: "Rasharkin Presbyterian Church, Graveyard Descriptions". Archival finding aid; the booklet itself has not been inspected.</ref>
# '''Obtain Margaret's death return and test the 1895 alternative.''' Search around 10 January 1892 and establish whether Margaret was recorded married or widowed, where she died and who registered the death. Compare any 1895 John death with the full 1885 return rather than treating a matching name as sufficient.
# '''Reconstruct the complete child group, especially Lizzie.''' Examine baptisms, marriages, deaths, wills and sibling statements. Second Garvagh is relevant because John and Margaret married there and Ann was recorded born in County Londonderry. Its register inventory lists baptisms from 1830, but the relevant images have not been examined. The supplied Rasharkin baptism extract does not cover the complete post-1846 childbearing period; its failure to identify Lizzie is not a completed negative search.<ref>[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/GarvaghP2/ Second Garvagh Presbyterian Church register inventory], finding aid; relevant original baptism entries not yet inspected.</ref><ref>[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription], supplied extract used in the wider research; derivative and incomplete for the later childbearing period.</ref>
# '''Obtain Nancy's original probate petition and heir schedule.''' These may identify married surnames, addresses or exact relationships omitted from the newspaper notice. Continue searching Baladonly and Baladony literally, and use Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glascaw and Glasglow as surname variants.
# '''Establish continuity through land and family records.''' Follow John, Margaret and James in Lisnagaver valuations, leases and probate material, and seek a record naming John's father or connecting Samuel to a parent. A completed negative PRONI wills search has not been established for these targets.

The death of John Glasgow was registered on 24 June 1885 in Ballymoney, aged 78.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], John Glasgow, 24 June 1885, aged 78, Ballymoney registration district, D/1885/31/1005/7/2.</ref>

== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a linen weaver}}

'''Robert Glasgow''' was a linen weaver living at '''Donbought''', also written '''Dunbought''' or '''Doonbought''', in Dunaghy parish, County Antrim. His recorded age of forty in the 1851 census suggests birth about '''1811'''; the return gives County Antrim as his birthplace.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, barony of Kilconway, parish of Dunaghy, Donbought, household 16. [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Donbought/16/ National Archives of Ireland, legacy household locator]. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], printed p. 100, household 16, including the death entry for Jane Glasgow. See also {{Ancestry Record|62025|538377}}.</ref>

He married '''Margaret''' in '''1833''', according to the census return. No separate marriage-register entry has yet been established for the couple. Margaret was thirty-seven in 1851 and was also recorded as born in County Antrim.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /> Her proposed maiden name, Dunseath or Dunseeth, is discussed below.

The profile associates this family with Robert and Margaret Glasgow of '''Plainfield, Illinois'''. That remains a working identification, rather than an independently demonstrated link between the Irish and American households. The proposed father, [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]], also remains uncertain.

=== Household in 1851 ===

The return records '''eight living residents''': Robert and Margaret, four daughters and two sons. A fifth daughter, Jane, appears in the separate death section, not among the people alive in the household.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="DonboughtScott">W. Scott and W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], dated 7 May 2014, printed pp. 77-78, references 7883-7890, Dunbought household 16. Her entry accounts for the earlier description of two sons and five daughters, but the household should not be described as having seven children living there in 1851.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" />

=== American records associated with this profile ===

The retained 1880 United States census citation places a Robert Glasgow at '''Plainfield, Will County, Illinois''': enumeration district 210, page 405D, NARA microfilm T9, roll 260. The original household image was not independently examined for this revision.<ref name="Census1880">1880 United States Federal Census, Plainfield, Will County, Illinois; enumeration district 210; p. 405D; NARA microfilm publication T9, roll 260. {{Ancestry Record|6742|47116957}}. Citation retained from the imported profile.</ref>

A published transcription of '''Plainfield Township Cemetery''' records '''Robert Glasgow, died 10 January 1888, aged 75''', described as “Father”. It also records '''Margaret, wife of Robert Glasgow''', born '''12 May 1813''' and died '''16 June 1886'''. These are cemetery-transcription details, not independently inspected civil death records.<ref name="PlainfieldCemetery">Selina Brown, contributor, [https://www.interment.net/data/us/il/will/plainfield/plain_fg.htm ''Plainfield Township Cemetery, Plainfield, Will County, Illinois: surnames F-G''], Interment.net, contributed 15 November 2007; entries for Robert and Margaret Glasgow.</ref>

The Find a Grave memorial attached to the earlier profile is '''113062074'''. The memorial photograph has not been independently inspected for this revision.<ref name="FindAGrave">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/113062074/robert-glasgow Find a Grave, memorial 113062074, Robert Glasgow]. See also {{Ancestry Record|60525|67006055}}.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Proposed father: Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie ===

'''The father-son relationship with [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]] remains uncertain.''' The older man was seventy-two in 1851, married to Catherine, and therefore of a suitable age to be this Robert's father. His household identifies sons John and Samuel, but does not identify the married Robert at Donbought as another son.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy, Glenleslie, household 23. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf Detailed comma-delimited transcription], printed p. 103, including sons John and Samuel absent in America.</ref>

The older Robert is the leading known chronological candidate for '''Robert Glasco of Doonbought in the 1825 tithe applotment'''. He would have been about forty-six, compared with about fourteen for this Robert. The tithe entry, however, gives no age, wife, children or connection to Glenleslie. It neither establishes the identity of the older occupier nor demonstrates father-son succession to a particular holding.<ref name="Tithe1825">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering the Baronies of Cary, Dunluce and Kilconway in North Antrim plus the Barony of N. E. Liberties, Co. Londonderry''], surname order, dated 17 October 2016, printed p. 41, compiler's index 5804: Robert Glasco, Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2], Dunaghy, 1825. The index number is not an original property-lot number. Original tithe-book image not inspected.</ref>

The earlier research transcription of the Glenleslie man's '''3 February 1851 will''' lists a Robert Glasgow among the witnesses, but does not identify him as this man or as a son. The attestation and signature layout require checking before that name is treated as a separately identified witness. The will's reported provision for daughter Margaret and her Young children does not establish this Robert's parentage.<ref name="GlenleslieWill">Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie, will dated 3 February 1851, proved 13 February 1854; National Archives of Ireland copy, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ8-MQQJ?view=fullText FamilySearch, image 229]. Details retained from the supplied Glenleslie profile's earlier research transcription; the image was not re-examined for this revision.</ref>

The fact that the will summary also omits the independently identified sons John and Samuel means it cannot be treated as an exhaustive list of the older man's children. It neither excludes nor proves this Robert as another son. Catherine's maternity is likewise unproved; an uncertain paternal attachment must not automatically become a confident attachment to both parents.

=== Daniel or Samuel: the disputed census name ===

The two examined transcriptions disagree over the seven-year-old son. The detailed comma-delimited transcription gives '''Daniel Glasgow'''; Scott and Macafee's table gives '''Samuel Glasgow''', reference 7889. These are competing readings of the '''same census entry''', not two sons or two independent records.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="DonboughtScott" />

A saved crop of the handwriting in rows 6-8 shows the corresponding sequence of a nine-year-old daughter, the disputed seven-year-old son and Robert aged two. The crop was examined, but it lacks the full page heading and comparison handwriting, and the disputed forename has not been treated as settled.<ref name="CensusCrop">Cropped image of the handwritten census name-and-age columns, rows 6-8, supplied by the profile manager and retained with the research materials. The ages are 9, 7 and 2; the central forename is disputed. The complete original return should accompany this crop when publishing the image.</ref> The current [[Glasgow-1397|Daniel Glasgow]] profile is retained as the navigation link; no additional Samuel child is created from the alternative transcription.

The nine-year-old daughter's name is given as '''Netta''' in the examined transcriptions and as '''Motta''' in the existing tree. The spellings should not be silently treated as separate people.

=== The Ireland-Illinois identification ===

The Illinois identification needs to be demonstrated separately from the proposed Glenleslie parentage. Similar names, approximate ages and the associated family trees are useful starting points, but a tree attachment is not an independent source.

The census age of forty suggests birth about '''1810-1811''', conventionally recorded here as about 1811. The Illinois cemetery age of seventy-five at death in January 1888 suggests birth about '''1812-1813'''. This is a discrepancy to retain, not a reason to manufacture an exact birth date. Cemetery location also does not establish place of death.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="PlainfieldCemetery" />

No inspected passenger record, naturalisation record or other source establishes an emigration date or shows that the whole household travelled together.

=== Griffith's Valuation ===

The Dunaghy valuation index lists '''Robert Glasgow at Doonbought''', along with '''John Dunseath''' in the same townland. A separate entry lists '''Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie'''.<ref name="GriffithDunaghy">[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/dunaghy.php Fáilte Romhat, Griffith's Valuation index, Dunaghy parish, County Antrim], Robert Glasgow and John Dunseath at Doonbought; Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie. Name-and-townland index, not an inspected original valuation page or map.</ref> A parish transcription gives the valuation coverage as '''1861-1862'''; the date of the individual original Doonbought page has not been independently verified.<ref name="GriffithDate">[https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-dunaghy.php Irish Genealogy Hub, ''Griffith's Valuation: Dunaghy Parish, County Antrim''], heading giving coverage as 1861 and 1862.</ref>

The indexed Robert is a candidate continuation of the 1851 Donbought householder. His identity, exact plot, acreage, immediate lessor and subsequent revision history remain unverified. The entry should not yet be used to assert that this Robert emigrated after 1862.

=== Margaret's proposed maiden name ===

Margaret is attached in the existing tree under the surname '''Dunseeth''', with '''Dunseath''' appearing in another family-tree lead. An Ancestry tree-derived entry for '''Samuel Glasgow''', reportedly born 8 November 1841 and deceased 19 January 1918 at Plainfield, names his parents as Robert Glasgow and Margaret Dunseath. The underlying death record or obituary has not been inspected.<ref name="SamuelTree">[https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/results?firstName=samuel&lastName=glasgow Ancestry, ''Samuel Glasgow Family History Records''], tree-derived entry naming Robert Glasgow and Margaret Dunseath as parents. This is a research lead, not an inspected original parentage record.</ref>

Before this can establish Margaret's maiden name, that Samuel must be connected to this household. The reported 1841 birth differs from the approximate 1843-1844 birth implied by the seven-year-old son in 1851, and the Irish child's forename is itself disputed. Another FamilySearch family summary dates the Illinois Samuel to 1843, illustrating the variation between online trees rather than resolving it.<ref name="SamuelFamilySearch">[https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/LR1F-NC8/catherine-e.-glasgow-1873-1950 FamilySearch Family Tree, Catherine E. Glasgow (1873-1950), LR1F-NC8], parent summary giving Samuel Glasgow as 1843-1918 and Martha Ann Isdal as her mother. User-contributed tree summary.</ref>

The local Dunseath surname is independently represented by John Dunseath's Doonbought valuation entry and a Clough Cemetery plot-owners' register entry for '''John Dunseath of Dunbought''': original registration '''353''', '''five graves''', notes '''1076, 1077 and 1078'''. The individual plot entry is undated; it does not name five interments or identify John's relationship to Margaret. Its registration number is not a current individual grave number.<ref name="CloughDunseath">Nancy Crocetti and Alistair McCartney, transcribers (2012), Jim McKane, compiler, [https://www.cotyroneireland.com/burial/clough2.html ''Clough Cemetery (aka Dunaghy Old Graveyard) Plot Owners, Clough, Dunaghy Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland c1875-1937''], entry 353, John Dunseath, Dunbought.</ref>

=== The 1876 Kendall County directory ===

The original imported profile mentioned an image from the ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois''. The local index to the '''1876''' volume gives these precise page references:<ref name="KendallIndex">[https://kendallkin.org/databases/948/A%2CG/19.html Kendall County, Illinois Genealogy, ''Index to Biographical Directories & Histories''], Glasgow entries, source code GF: George Fisher & Co., ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois'' (Chicago, 1876). Index locators retained from the earlier research; the biographies themselves have not been examined.</ref>

The volume is catalogued in HathiTrust under records '''009833464''' and '''008718397'''. Copy identifiers include '''yale.39002070892337''', '''uiuo.ark:/13960/t4fn12z83''' and '''nnc1.cu01651218'''; the Illinois copy is associated with Internet Archive identifier '''biographicaldire00fish'''.<ref name="KendallCatalogue">HathiTrust catalogue, [https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/009833464 record 009833464] and [https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008718397.marc MARC record 008718397], ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois'' (1876).</ref>

The actual entries on pages 95, 97 and 102 remain unread. The Sr./Jr. labels and the shared page do not establish a father-son relationship or identify the Irish birthplace. No biography text or migration date has been inferred from the index.

=== Possible later identification of the two-year-old Robert ===

A potentially corresponding '''Robert Glasgow (1849-1919)''' appears in the FamilySearch tree as husband of '''Margaret Jane Akin/Aiken''', with a marriage dated '''9 June 1870 in Will County, Illinois'''. Her source list includes an Illinois county-marriage entry transcribed as '''Margret Aron'''. The approximate age and the Aiken name in the 1876 directory make this a useful identification to test, not an established connection.<ref name="RobertJuniorTree">[https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/9KMH-FTW/margaret-jane-akin-1847-1910 FamilySearch Family Tree, Margaret Jane Akin (1847-1910), 9KMH-FTW], spouse Robert Glasgow (1849-1919), 9KMH-FT7; source list includes ''Margret Aron, Illinois, County Marriages, 1810-1940''. Tree summary and source locator, not an inspected original marriage record.</ref>

=== Unassigned probate reference ===

The imported profile mentioned an '''1851 County Antrim probate-index occurrence''' for Robert Glasgow without an individual archive reference, residence, role or transcription. It is not usable evidence for this man. The proposed father's known will was written in 1851 but proved in 1854; that does not establish that the unidentified index occurrence refers to the same document. A deceased testator whose probate was granted in 1851 could not also be the man recorded alive in Illinois in 1880.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search], generic locator retained from the imported profile; the purported individual 1851 entry has not been verified.</ref>

=== 1880 Illinois Census === 

Robert is indexed as “Robert Glasgo,” Plainfield, Will County, Illinois; image 815/906, ED 210, sheet 405D. The record gives age 68, married, head of household, born Ireland, with both parents born Ireland, spouse Margaret Glasgo<ref>https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYYB-3RN?view=index&personArk=%2Fark%3A%2F61903%2F1%3A1%3AMX2S-9NW&action=view&lang=en</ref>

== Biography ==
'''Samuel John Glasgow''' was born before about 1845 in County Antrim, Ireland.

He married Margaret Calagher on 21 August 1866 at Ballymoney. The original
register describes Samuel as a full-age bachelor and labourer and names his
father as '''Andrew Glasgow, labourer'''. Margaret was of full age and unmarried;
her father was James Calagher, labourer.<ref name="Marriage1866">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1866/11540/8244496.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Samuel John Glasgow and Margaret Calagher, 21 August 1866.</ref>
A marriage for Samuel Glasgow and Calaghen was registered on 21 August 1866 in the Ballymoney district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 21 August 1866, Ballymoney district, M/1866/I1/281/6/5.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
[[Glasgow-1050|Andrew Glasgow]] is Samuel's strongest identified father
candidate. Andrew was a Glenleslie linen weaver born about 1818 and died in
1848.<ref name="Census1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: detailed comma-delimited transcription''], Glenleslie household 21.</ref> The chronology and locality fit, but Samuel's marriage does not state Andrew's residence and no baptism has been found. Their relationship therefore remains uncertain.

The previously cited 1870 civil birth is not Samuel's marriage record and should
not be used as proof of his parentage. It is retained among the profile's earlier
research sources as the FamilySearch record [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FG82-Q36 FG82-Q36] and its [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=f66be225e5-6432791 IrishGenealogy.ie result page], while the original marriage above provides the controlling evidence.

Glasgow-1780.Name: Glasgow-1780
Glasgow-1780.bio:
== Biography ==

=== Early life and family ===

James was born in 1805 near Clough, County Antrim. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] and [[McClure-6341|Jane McClure]].

His attached siblings are:

* [[Glasgow-1779|Jane Glasgow]], who married Armstrong;
* [[Glasgow-1778|William Glasgow]];
* [[Glasgow-1656|Robert Glasgow]];
* [[Glasgow-1781|Adam Dickie Glasgow]].

James’s missionary journal provides direct, first-person evidence that Adam Dickie Glasgow and Robert Glasgow were his brothers. He repeatedly wrote of “my brother Adam”, described Adam’s move from Belfast to New Zealand, and recorded receiving an encouraging letter from “my brother Robert in Victoria”.<ref name="MissionaryJournal">[https://revjamesmcclureglasgow.blogspot.com/ James McClure Glasgow missionary journal, 1857–1862], first-person journal in which James repeatedly identifies Adam Dickie Glasgow and Robert Glasgow of Victoria as his brothers (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

=== Education ===

James was educated at Ballymena Grammar School, at the academy of the Rev. John Paul, D.D., in Carrickfergus, and at the Royal Belfast Academical Institution, where he gained medals in mathematics and natural philosophy.

=== Presbyterian ministry ===

James was licensed as a probationer by the Presbytery of Belfast on 14 December 1834. He was called to the Presbyterian congregation of Castledawson on 6 October 1835.

On 10 July 1840 the Synod of Ulster and the Associate Synod united to form the Presbyterian Church in Ireland. The first act of the first General Assembly was the “setting apart of two missionaries, for the first time, to carry the light of God’s truth to heathen lands”.

James accepted the call to missionary service.

=== Marriage and departure for India ===

On 27 June 1840 James married [[Wightman-3457|Mary Wightman]] at Fisherwick Place Presbyterian Church, Belfast.

The ceremony took place at one o’clock. Afterwards, James and Mary proceeded on a visit to the Rev. Alexander Crawford of Randalstown, little knowing that Crawford’s ninth child would subsequently marry the Glasgows’ fourth daughter.

On 29 August 1840 James boarded the ''Athlone'', bound for Liverpool.

On 4 September 1840 James and Mary sailed from Liverpool aboard the ''Wave'', accompanied by the Rev. Alexander Kerr and his new wife. They arrived in Bombay on 26 February 1841.

During the voyage Mary suffered from severe seasickness, possibly because she was pregnant. When the ship was becalmed in the Indian Ocean, James taught his wife calculus to help pass the time.

=== Missionary work in Gujarat ===

The Glasgows and the Kerrs remained in Bombay for almost three months.

James and Mary’s first daughter, [[Glasgow-2898|Margaret Jane Glasgow]], was born there on 16 March 1841.

The two missionary families then sailed to Gogha and travelled onward to Rajkot in Gujarat, arriving on 3 June 1841.

Margaret Jane died on 11 June 1841 and was buried in the Anglican cemetery at Rajkot.

James spent the following eleven years in Rajkot and the surrounding parts of Gujarat, establishing missionary outposts and translating religious tracts into Gujarati.

A second daughter, [[Glasgow-2899|Jane Henrie Glasgow]], was born in India. She died on 14 April 1845, aged only three months, and was also buried in the Anglican cemetery at Rajkot.

A third daughter, [[Glasgow-2900|Mary Elizabeth Glasgow]], was born in 1845. A fourth daughter, [[Glasgow-2901|Annie Coulson Glasgow]], was born in 1848.

In 1851 the Glasgow family returned to Ulster on furlough, where their fifth daughter, [[Glasgow-2894|Harriet Glasgow]], was born.

James returned alone to India in 1854 and continued his missionary work there for a further ten years.

Princeton University awarded him an honorary Doctor of Divinity degree in 1856.

Many references to James remain in Gujarat, where churches, schools and homes have been named after him.

=== Family correspondence ===

James’s journal records that on 30 June 1858 he learned that his mother had died on 21 May 1858.<ref name="MissionaryJournal" />

The entry does not state her name. The date matches the known chronology of the attached Jane McClure, but an independent identity source should be found before adding 21 May 1858 to her profile as a proved death date.

=== Academic career ===

After returning to Belfast in 1864, James was appointed Professor of Living Oriental Languages at both Magee College, Londonderry, and Assembly’s College, Belfast.

His towering intellect and profound scholarship were combined with an almost child-like simplicity and straightforwardness of character.

He also served as a government examiner in Gujarati for the Indian Civil Service.

In 1869 James was elected a member of the Belfast Literary Society. In 1872 he was elected its president.

=== Publications and translations ===

James’s publications included:

* ''The Psalms of David, Translated into Gujarati Verse, for the Use of Native Churches and Families'' (Surat Mission Press, 1856);
* ''The Apocalypse—Translated & Expounded'' (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1873).

He also translated Dr. Robert Stewart’s ''Family Worship'' and the Bible into Gujarati, together with many other writings in both English and Gujarati.

=== Children ===

James and Mary had five daughters, three of whom survived into adulthood:

* [[Glasgow-2898|Margaret Jane Glasgow]], born in Bombay on 16 March 1841; died at Rajkot on 11 June 1841 and was buried in the Anglican cemetery there;
* [[Glasgow-2899|Jane Henrie Glasgow]], who died on 14 April 1845 aged three months and was buried in the Anglican cemetery at Rajkot;
* [[Glasgow-2900|Mary Elizabeth Glasgow]], known as “Minnie”, born in 1845; she never married and died in 1874;
* [[Glasgow-2901|Annie Coulson Glasgow]], born in 1848; she married William Crawford;
* [[Glasgow-2894|Harriet Glasgow]], born in Ulster in 1851; she married John Acheson.

Annie’s husband, William Crawford, was the ninth child of the Rev. Alexander Crawford of Randalstown. He later became managing director of the York Street Flax Spinning Company and chairman of the Board of Governors of the Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast. He was subsequently knighted.

Harriet’s husband, John Acheson, was also a linen manufacturer and was proprietor of the Bannview Weaving Factory at Portadown.

=== Later life ===

In Belfast, James and Mary lived at number 82 University Street, now numbered 86.

In 1878 they moved to Portadown to be near their daughter Harriet and son-in-law John Acheson.

Mary died on 19 February 1885.

James retired from his professorial posts in 1889.

=== Death and burial ===

James died on 30 June 1890 at Dunavon, Portadown.

His civil death registration described him as an 85-year-old widower, Presbyterian minister and Doctor of Divinity. His son-in-law John Acheson was present at the death.<ref name="JamesDeath">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/deaths_returns/deaths_1890/06100/4740942.pdf General Register Office, Ireland, civil death registration], Lurgan registration district, death of James Glasgow at Dunavon, Portadown, 30 June 1890; John Acheson, son-in-law, present at death.</ref>

James and Mary were buried with their daughter Minnie in Balmoral Cemetery.

== Research Notes ==

=== Brothers ===

James’s missionary journal is direct, first-person evidence that [[Glasgow-1781|Adam Dickie Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1656|Robert Glasgow]] of Victoria were his brothers.

Those two sibling relationships may therefore be treated as certain.

The journal evidence reviewed so far does not directly discuss [[Glasgow-1779|Jane Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-1778|William Glasgow]]. Their attached relationships should continue to rely on the sources already held on their respective profiles.

=== Mother’s death ===

The journal entry dated 30 June 1858 states that James had learned that day of his mother’s death on 21 May 1858.

The entry does not identify his mother by name. Although the date matches the chronology of [[McClure-6341|Jane McClure]], an independent source connecting the date specifically to her should be found before treating it as proved on her profile.

=== Further research ===

Useful further sources may include:

* the original baptismal or church record for James;
* records directly identifying all children of [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] and [[McClure-6341|Jane McClure]];
* immigration or death records for [[Glasgow-1781|Adam Dickie Glasgow]] in New Zealand;
* Australian records concerning [[Glasgow-1656|Robert Glasgow]] in Victoria;
* an independent death notice, civil record or burial record for Jane McClure;
* original Presbyterian mission records concerning James’s appointments and service.

The death of James Glasgow was registered on 30 June 1890 in Lurgan, aged 85.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], James Glasgow, 30 June 1890, aged 85, Lurgan registration district, D/1890/176/1021/16/104.</ref>

Glasgow-2406.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
'''James Garvin Glasgow''' was born about 1851 at Lisnagaver, County Antrim,
Ireland. His family gravestone records that he died in 1918 aged sixty-seven,
and the 1901 census reported his age as forty-nine.<ref name="RasharkinStone">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html Pauline O'Keeffe and Helen Evans, ''Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones''], transcription made August 2004, Glasgo memorial erected by James Garvin Glasgo.</ref><ref name="Census1901">[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Antrim/Killoquin_Lower/Lisnagaver/946378/ 1901 Census of Ireland], Lisnagaver house 33, Killoquin Lower, County Antrim.</ref>

James was the son of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], a farmer, and
[[Garvin-1831|Margaret Garvin]]. His 1886 marriage names his father, while the
memorial erected by James names both parents.<ref name="Marriage1886">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10840/5957283.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Garvin Glasgow and Eliza Ann Aiken, 1 July 1886, Clough, entry 62.</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

James married [[Aiken-2081|Eliza Ann Aiken]] on 1 July 1886 at Clough. He was a
full-age bachelor farmer of Lisnagaver; she was a full-age spinster and daughter
of William Aiken, farmer. Robert Aiken and Matilda Bell witnessed the
marriage.<ref name="Marriage1886" />

The family gravestone records their infant son '''John Garvin''', identified as [[Glasgow-4005|John Garvin Glasgow]]; his civil birth return gives the birth at Lisnagaver on 3 October 1887.<ref name="Birth1887">General Register Office of Ireland, civil birth register, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, entry 352: John Garvin Glasgow, born 3 October 1887, Lisnagaver. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1887/02541/1940589.pdf register image].</ref> James and Eliza
were the only people in their household in 1901, so the child had died before
that census.<ref name="RasharkinStone" /><ref name="Census1901" />

James and Eliza Ann were again recorded at Lisnagaver in the 1911 census.<ref
name="Census1911">[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1911/Antrim/Killoquin/Lisnagaver/130063/ 1911 Census of Ireland], Lisnagaver house 22, Killoquin, County Antrim.</ref>

James died at Lisnagaver on 14 February 1918 aged sixty-seven. He was a married
farmer and had suffered acute pneumonia for six days. Eliza Ann Glasgow, widow,
was present at the death.<ref name="Death1918">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1918/05197/4435754.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], James Garvin Glasgow, 14 February 1918, Dervock registrar's district, entry 165.</ref> Letters of administration of his estate were granted at Belfast on 8 May 1918 to Eliza Ann Glasgow, the widow.<ref>PRONI Will Calendars, 1918: letters of administration of James Garvin Glasgow, Lisnagaver, farmer, died 14 February 1918, granted to Eliza Ann Glasgow, widow.</ref>

The gravestone records Eliza Ann's death on 16 June 1933 aged eighty-four.<ref
name="RasharkinStone" /> Her probate (as Eliza Ann Glasgow, of Tullynahinion, widow) was granted at Belfast on 17 July 1933 to Robert Andrew Aicken, farmer, and William Shaw, solicitor.<ref>PRONI Will Calendars, 1933: Glasgow, Eliza Ann, of Tullynahinion, widow, died 16 June 1933, probate to Robert Andrew Aicken and William Shaw.</ref>
A marriage for James Glasgow and Aicken was registered on 1 July 1886 in the Ballymena district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 1 July 1886, Ballymena district, M/1886/H1/231/5/62.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The family memorial uses the spelling '''Glasgo''' and calls James's wife
'''Elizabeth Ann'''. The civil marriage, censuses and death registration use
'''Glasgow''' and the shorter form '''Eliza Ann'''. The matching residence,
husband and dates identify the same couple.

22571674.Name: Glasgow-867
22571674.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}}

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was a farmer of Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin,
County Antrim. His date of birth is uncertain. The 1851 census reported his age
as fifty, while the family gravestone says that he died in 1895 aged seventy-
eight, implying birth about 1816 or 1817.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/34/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Lisnagaver house 34, Rasharkin, County Antrim; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/reels/c19/007246523/007246523_00173.pdf original census image].</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html Pauline O'Keeffe and Helen Evans, ''Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones''], transcription made August 2004, Glasgo memorial erected by James Garvin Glasgo.</ref>

John married [[Garvin-1831|Margaret Garvin]] on 16 November 1846. The original
register describes him as a bachelor farmer of Lisnagaver and names his father
as '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Margaret was a spinster.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3156063 IrishGenealogy.ie], civil marriage registration of John Glasgow and Margaret Garvin, 16 November 1846, Ballymena registration district, group registration ID 3156063; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1846/09306/5369439.pdf original register image].</ref>
Her father was '''James Garvin, farmer'''. James Garvin and Ann Kelly witnessed
The marriage.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The 1851 household contained John, Margaret, their three-year-old daughter
[[Glasgow-1371|Ann]], and John's brother [[Glasgow-2908|Samuel Glasgow]]. John
Patterson, a fifteen-year-old linen weaver, was their servant. The return records
1846 as the marriage year and explicitly describes Samuel as John's brother.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

Ann married [[Bellingham-700|Francis Bellingham]] on 18 February 1875. Her
marriage names her father as John Glasgow, farmer.<ref name="AnnMarriage1875">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875, Finvoy parish church, entry 40.</ref>

John and Margaret also had a son, [[Glasgow-2406|James Garvin Glasgow]]. James's
1886 marriage records him as a Lisnagaver farmer and son of John Glasgow,
farmer. The family gravestone identifies Margaret Garvin as his mother.<ref name="JamesMarriage1886">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10840/5957283.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Garvin Glasgow and Eliza Ann Aiken, 1 July 1886, Clough, entry 62.</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

The gravestone records that Margaret died on 10 January 1892 aged seventy-four
and John died on 20 June 1895 aged seventy-eight. Their son James erected the
memorial at Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

=== Marriage ===
John married [[Garvin-1831|Margaret Garvin]] on '''16 November 1846''' at '''Second Garvagh Presbyterian Church''', in Errigal parish, County Londonderry. The marriage was by licence and was registered in '''Coleraine''', not Ballymena.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The contemporary return describes John as a full-age bachelor and farmer of '''Lisnagaver, parish of Rasharkin''', son of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Margaret was a full-age spinster of '''Rockfield, parish of Desertoghill''', daughter of '''James Garvin, farmer'''.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

The witnesses were '''James Garvin''' and a man whose name was read as '''Wm Keely''', not the previously reported Ann Kelly. The second surname remains a handwriting reading rather than an established identification. Neither witness's relationship to the couple is stated; the witness James Garvin should not automatically be identified as Margaret's father. The minister's signature was read as James B. Rentoul.<ref name="JohnMarriage1846" />

=== Lisnagaver household, 1851 ===
The surviving census places the family at '''house 34, Lisnagaver'''. It records 1846 as John and Margaret's marriage year, agreeing with their marriage return.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

The return directly establishes that '''Samuel was John's brother'''. It contains '''five household members, not five children''': Ann is the only child of John listed in this household.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

=== Children ===
The following children are supported by the household and family records. This is not necessarily a complete child group.

* '''[[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]]''', aged three in 1851 and born in County Londonderry. The working identification is '''Annie Glasgow''', who married [[Bellingham-700|Francis Bellingham]] on '''18 February 1875''' at Finvoy parish church. Annie was a full-age spinster of the '''parish of Rasharkin''', daughter of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. Francis was a full-age bachelor and farmer of Culmore, parish of Rasharkin, son of Thomas Bellingham, farmer. The witnesses were Thomas Bellingham and Mary Ann M'Caughern, as read. The marriage does not name Annie's mother or supply a townland for her, so it is consistent with, but does not alone complete, the identification with the census daughter.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851" /><ref name="AnnMarriage1875">General Register Office of Ireland, contemporary civil marriage return, Ballymoney registration district, page 191, entry 40: Francis Bellingham and Annie Glasgow, 18 February 1875, Finvoy parish church, County Antrim. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf Register image].</ref>
* '''[[Glasgow-2406|James Garvin Glasgow]]'''. His marriage to '''Eliza Ann Aiken''' on '''1 July 1886''' at Clough describes him as a Lisnagaver farmer and son of '''John Glasgow, farmer'''. The family memorial, known through transcription, names John and Margaret Garvin as his parents.<ref name="JamesMarriage1886">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage return, entry 62: James Garvin Glasgow and Eliza Ann Aiken, 1 July 1886, Clough. [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10840/5957283.pdf Register image].</ref><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

James's original death return independently records his full name as '''James Garvin Glasgow'''. He died at Lisnagaver on '''14 February 1918''', a married farmer aged '''64''', from acute pneumonia of six days' duration, certified. The informant was '''Eliza Ann Glasgow, widow, present at death, Lisnagaver'''; registration followed on 8 March 1918.<ref name="JamesDeath1918">General Register Office of Ireland, contemporary civil death return, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, County Antrim, entry 165: James Garvin Glasgow, Lisnagaver, 14 February 1918; registered 8 March 1918. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1918/05197/4435754.pdf Register image].</ref>

The memorial transcription gives James's age as '''67''', not 64. These are conflicting reported ages and should not be silently harmonised. His widow's name is not evidence for a sister called Lizzie.<ref name="JamesDeath1918" /><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

=== Death and family memorial ===
The GLASGO memorial at '''Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church''' was erected by James Garvin Glasgo and names his father John and mother Margaret Garvin. The available source is a modern transcription made by '''Pauline O'Keeffe and Helen Evans in August 2004'''; a photograph of this particular stone has not yet been inspected.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;"
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Source
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | John's reported death
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Age
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Identifying details
|-
| Contemporary civil death return || '''24 June 1885''', Lisnagaver || '''78''' || Married farmer; informant '''James Glasgow, son, present at death, Lisnagaver'''.<ref name="JohnDeath1885">General Register Office of Ireland, contemporary civil death return, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, County Antrim, page 1, entry 2: John Glasgow, Lisnagaver, 24 June 1885; registered 3 July 1885. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1885/06280/4799372.pdf Register image].</ref>
|-
| Published memorial transcription || '''20 June 1895''' || '''78''' || John named as the father of James Garvin Glasgo, alongside Margaret Garvin.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />
|}

The 1885 return gives the cause of death as '''cancer in lip, three years''', with no medical attendant. It directly documents a '''John Glasgow and son James at Lisnagaver'''. It does not name John's wife, give James a middle name, or state James's age.<ref name="JohnDeath1885" />

The deceased has a separate profile, [[Glasgow-3474|John Glasgow]]. An earlier version of this biography excluded him solely because the memorial transcription gives 1895. '''That exclusion was not justified.''' The same age, the Lisnagaver connection and the son James make identity with this John a substantial possibility.

'''A transcription error is a plausible explanation, not an established correction.''' Both the day and year differ: '''24 June 1885''' against '''20 June 1895'''. A photograph could show whether the published transcription misreads the stone; if the stone itself says 1895, the conflict would still need investigation. Different men, an error on the memorial, or another record error remain possible. The agreement in age does not by itself settle identity.<ref name="JohnDeath1885" /><ref name="RasharkinStone" />

The memorial transcription also records:
* '''Margaret Garvin''', James's mother, died '''10 January 1892''', aged '''74'''.
* '''John Garvin''', an infant son of James.
* '''James Garvin''', died '''14 February 1918''', aged '''67'''.
* '''Elizabeth Ann''', died '''16 June 1933''', aged '''84'''.<ref name="RasharkinStone" />

Margaret's original January 1892 death registration has not yet been obtained. Her married or widowed status, address and informant could help distinguish the competing death scenarios, once the record is securely identified as hers. A matching 1895 civil death has likewise not been verified.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

==== Parentage ====
John's marriage proves that his father was another '''John Glasgow, farmer'''.
The father is currently represented by [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] as an
uncertain working identification. No record yet gives the older man's residence,
wife or age. If the gravestone age is correct, the older John would have been
about sixty-five when this John was born; possible, but not enough to identify
him uniquely.

The conflict between the 1851 age of fifty and the gravestone age of seventy-
eight at death remains unresolved. The marriage, residence, wife and 1846
marriage year securely identify the 1851 household, while the gravestone was
erected by the couple's son and names both parents. The birth year should
therefore remain estimated.

==== Alexander Glasgow of Glenleslie ====
[[Glasgow-2385|Alexander Glasgow]] was previously attached as John's son.
However, Alexander was already a full-age bachelor when he married in April
1847, only five months after John and Margaret's marriage. Alexander's original
marriage also names his father as '''John Glasgow, labourer'''. He was detached
from this household because he belongs to an older, separate father-John branch.<ref name="AlexanderMarriage1847">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1847/09322/5375567.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Alexander Glasgow and Mary Anne Martin, 6 April 1847, Clogh, entry 31; derivative [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGVD-P9CS FamilySearch index entry].</ref>

==== Same-name records ====
The following FamilySearch records describe other men named John Glasgow and
are retained as identity checks: a [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KDXL-YJ1 reported 1849 birth at sea], an [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6HW-FPR 1870 Illinois resident], and a [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M47Q-56D Canadian household]. None contains Margaret Garvin, Lisnagaver or another feature identifying this John.

=== Birth estimate ===
Three different birth estimates arise from the records under comparison:

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;"
