The published reconstruction does not include a daughter Mary of the correct age and remains partly inferential. It is therefore a comparison/exclusion branch, not evidence that John and Margaret were Mary's parents.

=== 1740–1796 Tamlaght O'Crilly / Drumcannon McCaughan continuity lead ===

The 1740 Protestant Householders' Returns identify '''John McCahan''' and '''James McCahan''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''', in the Loughinsholin barony. This is an unusually early, exact-parish occurrence of two McCaughan-variant householders, decades before the Rasharkin baptismal material. The return gives no ages, household composition or relationship between the two men.<ref name="Evidence1740TamlaghtMcCahan">[https://adamsfamilydna.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/1740-Protestant-Returns-Londonderry-County-Ireland.pdf 1740 Protestant Householders' Returns], records 1171–1172.</ref>

A later circa-1800 rent-roll transcription records four McCaughan tenants in '''Drumcannon''' in '''1791''': '''Samuel''', '''Matthew''', '''William''' and '''John'''. The source explains that the undated entries are part of farm rental lists dating roughly 1796–1814, so the dated 1791 entries should be treated as a landlord record, not a census. The 1796 Flaxgrowers' List then records '''William M'Caughin''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''' with three wheels/looms.<ref name="Evidence1791Rent1796Flax">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/misc/rentrolls.html circa-1800 Bann Valley rent-roll transcription], Drumcannon entries 182, 185, 197–198; [https://www.billmacafee.com/1796flaxgrowerslist/1796flaxgrowersderry.pdf 1796 Flaxgrowers' List], record 4754.</ref>

This is new pre-1811 evidence in the same broader parish region and strengthens the case for investigating Tamlaght O'Crilly, Drumcannon and Gortereghy together. It does not prove the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]: the named tenants have no demonstrated relationship to her, and the 1791 William has not been shown to be the 1796 William. The next test is to trace these names through surviving estate papers, Presbyterian records and valuation revisions for a daughter Mary born about 1811 or a transfer into Lisnagaver/Gortereghy.

=== 1817 First Ballymoney McCaughan household: a new Mary-parent candidate ===

Rev. Robert Park's 1817 register of the First Ballymoney Presbyterian Church records '''John McCaughan [McCahon]''', wife '''Mary McCaughan [McCahon]''', and son '''James McCaughan [McCahon]''' at '''Drumard [Drumart]''', house 8. The same register records '''Grissel McCaughan [McCahan]''' and '''Hugh McCaughan [McCahan]''' in a Bendooragh household, showing the variant forms in the Ballymoney-area Presbyterian network at the period when Mary Glasgow would have been a child.<ref name="Evidence1817BallymoneyMcCaughan">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf 1817 First Ballymoney Presbyterian register], records 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

A separate compiled Ballyverdagh account lists a Drumant church-member household as John and Mary McCahon, with son James and daughters Mary and Elizabeth. Since that detail is not present in the searchable Park register entry and the underlying membership source has not been inspected, it remains a secondary lead. If the two records refer to the same couple, their daughter Mary would be chronologically compatible with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s estimated birth about 1811; no marriage, migration, residence or Glasgow connection has been found.

This is currently the strongest new chronological candidate for a Mary-parent household outside the immediate Rasharkin cluster, but it is not proof. The decisive test is to identify the original Drumard/Drumant membership sheet and trace John and Mary McCaughan through Ballymoney Presbyterian baptisms, marriages and valuation records.<ref name="EvidenceDrumantMcCahon">[https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm compiled Ballyverdagh account].</ref>

=== Complete 1817 Ballymoney-area McCaughan audit ===

The full searchable 1817 register contains at least five distinct McCaughan/McCahon placements: '''Charles and Elizabeth McCaughan''' at Balnamore, with children James, Samuel, John, Ann, Daniel and Elizabeth and an older Mary whose relationship is uncertain; '''Samuel and Martha McCaughan''' at Taghey, with sons John and James; '''John and Mary McCaughan''' at Drumard, with son James; '''Grissel McCaughan''' and '''Hugh McCaughan''' in a Bendooragh household headed by William McMaster; and '''Elizabeth McCaughan''' in a Currysiskan household headed by Widow Knox.<ref name="Evidence1817CompleteMcCaughanAudit">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf complete searchable 1817 register], records 1239–1248, 1383, 1436–1439, 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

This is important negative evidence: the primary searchable register does '''not''' list a daughter Mary in the Drumard John-and-Mary household. The separate compiled account's Drumant list of daughters Mary and Elizabeth may represent a different membership list, a different townland, or an expanded/parallel record, but it cannot currently prove that the Drumard couple had a daughter Mary. The Drumard family remains a possible chronological comparison branch, but its evidential weight is lower than the initial reading suggested.

The audit also identifies a Balnamore Mary McCaughan candidate, but the register marks her relationship as uncertain and suggests only that she may be Charles's mother. None of the five placements supplies a marriage, parent statement, migration record or Glasgow link. [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parents therefore remain unproved.

=== Dreen probate cluster: Agnes and Peter McCaughern, 1916 ===

The [https://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/reels/cwa/005014919/005014919_00647.pdf National Archives of Ireland will-calendar] records two adjacent Dreen, Rasharkin estates: '''Agnes McCaughern''', spinster, died 26 March 1916, administration granted to '''William McCaughern'''; and '''Peter McCaughern''', farmer, died 27 February 1916, also granted to William. Later unadministered grants for both estates were made to '''Catherine McCaughern''', spinster.

These entries show a substantial late local McCaughern cluster and a repeated William–Catherine administrative connection, but the calendar does not identify their exact kinship. The underlying probate packets should be obtained because they may name beneficiaries, relatives and property. This is a useful local-network lead, not evidence for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parents.

=== New parent-bearing Armoy/Cromaghs branch: William McCaughan ===

The National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index gives a new parent-bearing local record: '''William McCaughan''', whose present address was Fairhill Street, Ballycastle, supplied an 1851 census extract naming his father '''Archibald McCaughan''' and mother '''Mary'''. The indexed residence was '''Cromaghs, parish of Armoy, barony of Cary''', placing this branch in the wider Ballycastle–Armoy area rather than directly at Lisnagaver or Gortereghy.

This proves an additional Archibald–Mary McCaughan parental pair in the wider North Antrim research region, but it does not identify William with any existing WikiTree profile or connect him to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The record is a census-search-form abstraction rather than the underlying 1851 return, and the next step is to obtain the extract/image and trace William, Archibald and Mary through Cromaghs valuation and church records. No safe WikiTree ID has been assigned to this branch.

Source: [https://censussearchforms.nationalarchives.ie/search/cs/results.jsp?applicantAddress=&applicantFirstname=&applicantSurname=&barony=&censusExtractYear=&city=&county=&fatherFirstname=&fatherSurname=&motherFirstname=&motherSurname=&pageSize=&pager.offset=14290&parish=&search=Search&sort=residence_baronySort&townland= National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index], accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Cromaghs valuation corroboration: Archibald and Margaret McCahan ===

Two independent online transcriptions of Griffith's Valuation for Armoy, dated to the 1861/62 county survey, list '''Archibald Mc Cahan''' as an occupier in '''Cromaghs'''. The same entries also list '''Margaret Mc Cahan''' in Cromaghs. This corroborates the parent-bearing 1851 census-search-form branch: the Archibald named there was an Archibald of the same surname variant and townland in the next decade.

The entries do not state whether Margaret was Archibald's wife, sister, daughter or another household occupier. The valuation is an occupier/property record, not a family register. The spelling is '''McCahan''', while the 1851 search-form entry uses '''McCaughan'''; this is compatible with local spelling variation but cannot identify either person with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s family. No safe WikiTree ID has been found for Archibald or Margaret.

Sources: [https://irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-armoy.php Irish Genealogy Hub transcription of Armoy Griffith's Valuation]; [https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/armoy.php Fáilte Romhat transcription]; [https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/research-guides/valuation-office-records/ National Archives guide to valuation records]. Accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Pre-1790 Ballintoy record: Archd. McKaughin at Lisbellanagroagh More ===

The 1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish records '''Archd. McKaughin''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', identified as Protestant. This is a new pre-1790 occurrence of the McCaughan spelling family in the barony of Cary, the same wider North Antrim barony containing later Ballintoy, Armoy and Ballycastle McCaughan/McCahan households.

The census supplies no age, household composition or relationship to Mary Glasgow. It cannot identify this Archibald as her father, and Lisbellanagroagh More is not the same place as Lisnagaver/Gortereghy. It is nevertheless a valuable locality and spelling lead for testing whether the later Armoy/Cromaghs and Rasharkin branches descend from an older Cary family.

Source: [https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf 1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish], entry 318, accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Lisbellanagroagh continuity: Catherine M'Caghan and Daniel McCaw ===

The 1803 Ballintoy census records '''Kath. M'Caghan''', standardised as Catherine McCaughan, at '''Lisbellanagroagh Beg'''. She was listed as the wife of John McIlfatrick and as Church of Ireland; the row gives her age as 29, implying an estimated birth about 1774. The 1824 Ballintoy tithe book then records '''Danl. McCaw''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', the neighbouring “More” townland where the 1766 census had recorded Archd. McKaughin.

These records create a continuous locality trail from an Archibald in 1766, to a McCaughan woman in the adjoining townland in 1803, to a McCaw occupier in More in 1824. They do not prove that Catherine was Archibald's daughter, that Daniel was related to either person, or that this Cary cluster was the family of [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan Glasgow]]. They are nevertheless stronger than isolated surname occurrences and justify targeted searches of Ballintoy Church of Ireland marriages, baptisms and vestry records.

Sources: [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf 1803 Trail census, Ballintoy], entries 2852–2853; [https://www.billmacafee.com/ballintoy/earlydatabases/titheballintoy.pdf 1824 Ballintoy tithe applotment], entry for Daniel McCaw at Lisbellanagroagh More; accessed 15 September 2026.

=== FamilySearch record-hint collision: James McCaughan and Alexander McCaughan ===

The logged-in FamilySearch record search returned an indexed Ireland marriage result describing '''James Mc Caughan''' as father of '''Alexander Mc Caughan'''. The attached Family Tree match was '''MCGP-3S2''', but that profile is James McCaughan born about '''1827''', with spouse Catharine McConachie and children Alexander McCaughan ('''1847–1921''', 96QG-NVJ) and Robert Mc Caughan ('''1853–1934''', K4GP-RD8). The tree profile has no sources and the relationship was added in 2020.

This is a new and important exclusion. The attached tree person cannot be the older James proposed as Mary's father: he is too young, and his son Alexander was born decades after Mary's marriage and the 1837–1844 Glasgow baptisms. The indexed father statement may belong to a different McCaughan family or be an aggregation error; it must not be cited as evidence for Mary's parentage. Source: [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCGP-3S2 FamilySearch tree profile MCGP-3S2], and [https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&q.givenName=James&q.surname=McCaughan&q.birthLikeDate.from=1760&q.birthLikeDate.to=1800&q.birthLikePlace=Antrim%2C%20Ireland FamilySearch James McCaughan search results], accessed 15 September 2026.

The same search also surfaced '''James McCaughan''' in the Irish Valuation Office Books for '''Shankill in 1838''' and '''Billy, Ballycastle in 1861'''. These are new locality leads, but the index does not expose enough detail to identify the tenant with [[McCaughan-68|McCaughan-68]], the Gortereghy tithe tenant, or Mary's father. The underlying valuation images should be checked for townland continuity, occupier changes and adjoining McCaughan households.

The death of Alexander Glasgow was registered on 16 May 1888 in Ballymoney, aged 84.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], Alexander Glasgow, 16 May 1888, aged 84, Ballymoney registration district, D/1888/31/1005/7/348.</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Mary "Molly" McCaughan''' was born about 1810 or 1811 in County Antrim, Ireland. She married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], a farmer associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver in the civil parish of Rasharkin, County Antrim.

Her parentage has not been established.

Mary's surname appears in surviving and transcribed records in several forms, including '''McCaughan''', '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern'''. Her given name appears as both '''Mary''' and '''Molly'''. These variants appear to refer to the same woman rather than separate wives of Alexander Glasgow.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">Richard John Torrens, [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian Church Baptisms, 1834–1846], transcription by Barbara Braswell, particularly entries 75, 106 and 203 (accessed 16 July 2026). The page warns that faded or difficult entries may contain transcription errors. Original register: PRONI MIC.1P/292.</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Mary married [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] about '''1836''', probably in County Antrim.

The detailed transcription of the surviving 1851 census records 1836 as the first-marriage year for both Alexander and Mary.<ref name="CensusTranscript">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], Lisnagaver households 34–37, p. 183 (accessed 16 July 2026). This is a transcription of the same census return, not independent evidence.</ref>

No original marriage entry has yet been identified.

The surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian marriage register begins only in 1845 and is therefore too late to contain their marriage.<ref name="ChurchCoverage">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/church.php?civilparish=Rasharkin&civilparishid=347&search_type=full Church records for Rasharkin], Presbyterian entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/292: baptisms from 1834 and marriages from 1845 (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref>

Second Portglenone Presbyterian Church remains a candidate for further research because its surviving marriage register begins in 1822 under PRONI reference MIC.1P/357.<ref name="SecondPortglenone">John Grenham, [https://www.johngrenham.com/records/county_church_full.php?county=Antrim&denomination=Presbyterian&location=Public+Record+Office+of+Northern+Ireland&search_type=full Historic Presbyterian church records for County Antrim], Second Portglenone entry citing PRONI MIC.1P/357, marriages from 1822 (accessed 2026).</ref>

It should not, however, be described as their known marriage congregation unless an entry is found.

=== Children ===

Known and possible children of Alexander Glasgow and Mary McCaughan include:

The published transcription names '''Alex Glascaw''' and '''Mary McAughin''' as his parents.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" /> The later reuse of the name James suggests that he died before October 1843, but no burial has been identified and the original register should be checked before treating this as proved.

Alexander remained named through the 1865–1878 volume and was later replaced by Robert Elder.</ref> Her identification as a daughter of Mary McCaughan is plausible but her mother is not independently named in the marriage record.

The published Rasharkin baptism transcription contains no baptism entries for 1840 or 1841. Robert's missing baptism is therefore more likely to reflect incomplete record coverage or transcription than evidence that he belonged to another family.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== 1851 Census ===

In the surviving 1851 census, Mary was living at Lisnagaver with her husband Alexander and their children Robert, James and Ann.

Alexander was aged 40 and Mary was also aged '''40'''. Both were born in County Antrim, and the detailed census transcription records 1836 as their first-marriage year.<ref name="CensusHousehold">National Archives of Ireland, ''Census of Ireland, 1851'', Lisnagaver, Rasharkin, County Antrim, household 35, Alexander Glasgow household; [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ household images] (accessed 16 July 2026).</ref><ref name="CensusTranscript" />

Mary's age therefore supports a birth about '''1810 or 1811'''. Earlier estimates placing her birth around 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with this contemporary census evidence.

=== Residences ===

The surviving records place Alexander and Mary within a small area of Rasharkin parish over a period of years:

Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck are separate adjoining townlands in Rasharkin civil parish, barony of Kilconway, County Antrim.<ref name="Townlands">[https://www.townlands.ie/antrim/kilconway/rasharkin/killoquin/lisnagaver/ Lisnagaver Townland, County Antrim], administrative divisions and adjoining-townland map (accessed 2026).</ref>

The changing descriptions may reflect residence close to a townland boundary rather than a substantial migration.

=== The Lisnagaver Glasgow–McCaughan Network ===

Mary and Alexander were part of a closely associated Glasgow and McCaughan network centred on Lisnagaver and the surrounding townlands.

Several Glasgow households appear together in the surviving 1851 census fragment.<ref name="CensusTranscript" />

The census explicitly identifies '''John and Samuel as brothers'''. It does not identify Alexander or Thomas as their brothers.

Later valuation evidence provides a separate land-based connection. John, Alexander and Thomas occupied consecutive principal holdings at Lisnagaver under the same immediate lessor, Robert Harvey.

The consecutive lot numbers strongly suggest that the holdings were physically close. The valuation map should still be consulted before stating that every plot directly adjoined or shared a boundary.

The combined census, church and land evidence supports a close Glasgow family-and-neighbour network at Lisnagaver while leaving the precise relationships unresolved.

==== Alexander and Thomas Glasgow ====

There is substantial circumstantial evidence that [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] was a close relative, and possibly a brother, of Mary's husband [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].

Alexander and Thomas were:

* born in County Antrim about five years apart;
* farmers;
* able to read and write;
* associated with the same Presbyterian congregation;
* recorded within the same Lisnagaver–Gortereagh–Moneyleck micro-area;
* heads of closely grouped Lisnagaver households in 1851;
* and later occupiers of consecutive valuation lots under the same lessor.

The contemporary Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism register provides a particularly strong FAN connection.

Alexander and Mary or Molly used the congregation while associated with Gortereagh and Lisnagaver. Thomas and [[McCracken-5681|Mary Ann McCracken]] used the same congregation while associated with Moneyleck and Lisnagaver.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

Most notably:

* Alexander and Mary's son James was born at Lisnagaver on '''9 October 1843''';
* Thomas and Mary Ann's daughter Eliza was born there on '''17 October 1843'''.

The children were born only eight days apart in the same small townland and appear in the same Presbyterian register.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

This is substantial FAN evidence for a close relationship.

No surviving record presently calls Alexander and Thomas brothers. Thomas should therefore be treated as Alexander's '''probable close relative and possible brother''', not as a proved sibling.

==== Thomas and Daniel Glasgow ====

A reported will record for [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel Glasgow]] of Kilrea identifies [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] as his "late brother" and [[Glasgow-2413|Daniel Neely Glasgow]] as a nephew.<ref name="DanielWill">Will of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea, proved 1871, reported in accumulated family research as identifying Thomas Glasgow as his "late brother". The original probate copy and complete archival citation are still required.</ref>

This supports Daniel and Thomas as brothers.

It does not establish Alexander's relationship to either man.

==== McCaughan Marriage Connection ====

The relationship between the Glasgow and McCaughan families was not limited to Mary's marriage to Alexander.

[[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]'s daughter [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] married [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]].

This provides another direct marriage connection between the Glasgow and McCaughen families within the same local network.

It does not, by itself, establish Robert McCaughen's relationship to Mary.

The original 1834 Rasharkin tithe book records William and James McCaheran at Gortereghy. The spelling is compatible with the McAughin and McAughern forms used for Mary in the baptism transcription, and Alexander and Mary's children were recorded at Gortereghy in 1837–38. This supports investigation of a local McCaughan family network, but the tithe names no relationships and does not establish Mary's parents.<ref name="GortereghyTithe1834">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Tithe Applotment Book for Rasharkin parish'', 1834, PRONI FIN/5/A/236, Gortereghy entries for William and James McCaheran.</ref>

=== The 1875 Mary Anne M‘Caughern Witness ===

On 18 February 1875, at Finvoy Parish Church, [[Glasgow-1371|Ann (Glasgow) Bellingham]] married Francis Bellingham.

Ann was the daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], farmer.

The witnesses were:

* Thomas Bellingham;
* '''Mary Anne M‘Caughern'''.

<ref name="BellinghamGlasgow1875">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, marriage of Francis Bellingham and [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]], 18 February 1875, Finvoy Parish Church; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1875/11190/8100682.pdf digital image], entry 40.</ref>

The witness is relevant because of the established Glasgow–McCaughan network in and around Lisnagaver.

She should '''not''' presently be identified as [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow.

Reasons for caution include:

* the witness was recorded as '''Mary Anne''', rather than Mary or Molly;
* the surname was recorded as '''M‘Caughern''';
* no reliable evidence currently establishes that Alexander's wife was still living in 1875;
* other McCaughan or McAughern households existed within the wider local network.

The witness should therefore remain an unidentified associate pending further evidence.== Research Notes ==

=== Birth Date ===

Mary's age of 40 in the 1851 census supports birth about '''1810 or 1811'''.

Earlier estimates of about 1817 or 1818 are inconsistent with the surviving census evidence and should not be used without an independent source.

=== Parentage ===

Mary's parents are presently '''unknown'''.

No surviving baptism, marriage entry, will, gravestone, death record or other contemporary source located for this profile explicitly names either parent.

The Rasharkin baptism entries establish Mary's maiden surname in variants such as '''McAughin''' and '''McAughern''', but they do not identify her father or mother.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms" />

=== Possible John McCaughen Connection ===

A John McCaughen of Mount Pleasant Township, Washington County, Pennsylvania, made a will dated 22 February 1815 in which he referred to:

:''my onley daughter which I left in Ireland when I came to America.''

The daughter was named Mary McCaughen, and John reportedly left half of his estate to her.<ref name="PennsylvaniaMcCaughen">[https://dokumen.pub/irish-presbyterians-and-the-shaping-of-western-pennsylvania-17701830-hardcovernbsped-0822945436-9780822945437.html ''Irish Presbyterians and the Shaping of Western Pennsylvania, 1770–1830''], discussion of John McCaughen's 1815 will.</ref>

This is potentially relevant because:

* the daughter's name was Mary McCaughen;
* she remained in Ireland when her father emigrated;
* Mary's revised birth estimate of about 1810 or 1811 means she was alive by 1815.

However, no evidence currently connects the Pennsylvania testator to:

* County Antrim;
* Rasharkin;
* Lisnagaver or Gortereagh;
* Alexander Glasgow;
* or the known local McCaughan/McAughern network.

The identification should therefore be treated only as a '''research hypothesis''', not as Mary's established parentage.

=== Distinction from Mary McCaughan, wife of John McAulay ===

This Mary should not be confused with another Mary McCaughan who married John McAulay.

That woman was reportedly born about 1817 in Dublin, married John McAulay in 1840, emigrated to New York in 1859 and later appeared in the 1861 census of Ontario, Canada.

Records identify that Mary as a daughter of Hugh McCaughan.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:27T9-VWQ "New York Passenger Lists, 1820–1891", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1859.</ref><ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MQWD-6ZH "Canada, Ontario Census, 1861", FamilySearch], Mary McCaughan, 1861.</ref>

She was therefore a different woman from [[McCaughan-222|Mary "Molly" McCaughan]], wife of Alexander Glasgow of Lisnagaver.

=== Death ===

Mary died at Gortahar, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim, on 27 February 1892. The register describes her as a widow and housewife, reportedly aged 89. Her daughter [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Elder]] was present at death.<ref name="MaryDeath1892">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Mary Glasgow, 27 February 1892, Gortahar, Ballymoney registration district; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1892/06049/4723532.pdf digital image].</ref>

The reported age implies birth about 1803, while the 1851 census implies about 1810 or 1811. Her birth date remains estimated. The former 1866 death estimate is superseded by this registration.

=== Robert Glasgow's Scottish Death ===

[[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]]'s reported death on 27 November 1902 in Glasgow, Scotland, remains potentially important.

A Scottish death registration would normally have space to record both parents, including the mother's maiden surname, if known to the informant.

The original registration should be obtained before relying on parent details copied from online family trees.

=== Local McCaughan / McAughern Network ===

The Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription records McAughern households in or near the same local area.

This does not prove a relationship to Mary, but it makes reconstruction of the local McCaughan/McAughern population a priority.

Particular attention should be paid to:

* [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]];
* the unidentified Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 Bellingham–Glasgow marriage;
* McCaughan, McAughin and McAughern entries associated with Lisnagaver, Gortereagh and Moneyleck;
* witnesses to Glasgow and McCaughan marriages and baptisms;
* valuation and estate records involving the same surnames.

=== Identity and Record Cautions ===

* Mary's age of 40 in 1851 supports birth about 1810 or 1811, not 1817 or 1818.
* ''Molly'' is a familiar form of Mary and does not indicate a second wife.
* The spellings McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and M‘Caughern should not automatically be treated as different families.
* The baptism transcription is derivative evidence and the original PRONI MIC.1P/292 register should be inspected.
* No parent should be attached to Mary solely from surname similarity.
* The Pennsylvania John McCaughen theory remains unproved.
* Mary Anne M‘Caughern, witness in 1875, should not currently be merged with Mary.
* No unsupported 1866 death should be used for Mary.
* No Scottish or Australian death should be attached without evidence connecting it to the Lisnagaver family.

=== Priority Research ===

==== Priority 1 — Find Alexander and Mary's Marriage ====

* Search Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriages under '''PRONI MIC.1P/357''' from about 1834 through 1838.
* Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glascow, Glascaw, McCaughan, McAughin, McAughern and similar forms.
* Record residences, witnesses and minister even if no parents are named.
* Do not assume Second Portglenone was the congregation unless an entry is found.

==== Priority 1 — Inspect the Original Rasharkin Register ====

* Inspect the original Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries under '''PRONI MIC.1P/292'''.
* Check the entries for James in 1837, the unnamed child in 1838 and James in 1843–1844.
* Record the exact original spelling of Mary's surname.
* Examine adjacent entries, marginal notes and witnesses or sponsors.
* Collect every McCaughan/McAughern entry rather than only those already associated with Alexander.

==== Priority 1 — Reconstruct the McCaughan Network ====

* Investigate [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]], husband of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]].
* Identify Robert's father, mother, siblings, residence and landholding.
* Search for links between Robert and Mary through witnesses, naming patterns, church records, leases, probate or valuation records.
* Reconstruct McCaughan/McAughern households in Lisnagaver, Gortereagh, Moneyleck and adjoining townlands.
* Treat repeated surnames and proximity as FAN evidence only until a direct relationship is found.

==== Priority 1 — Obtain Robert Glasgow's Death Record ====

* Confirm the reported death of [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] in Scotland on 27 November 1902.
* Obtain the original Scottish statutory death registration.
* Record the names of both parents exactly as given.
* Record the mother's maiden surname and the identity of the informant.
* Assess the reliability of the parent information according to the informant's relationship to Robert.

==== Priority 2 — Identify Mary Anne M‘Caughern ====

* Trace the Mary Anne M‘Caughern who witnessed the 1875 marriage of [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]] and Francis Bellingham.
* Search Finvoy, Rasharkin and Ballymoney-area civil and Presbyterian records.
* Compare age, residence, marital status and family connections.
* Do not attach her to this profile without evidence establishing identity.

==== Priority 2 — Investigate the Pennsylvania Hypothesis ====

* Obtain the original or full abstract of John McCaughen's 1815 Washington County, Pennsylvania will.
* Establish when John emigrated from Ireland.
* Identify his place of origin in Ireland if possible.
* Determine Mary's age or circumstances from probate, guardianship, land or correspondence records.
* Search for associates linking John to County Antrim or the Bann Valley.
* Do not attach John as Mary's father unless a documentary bridge is found.

==== Priority 2 — Land and Estate Records ====

* Trace Glasgow and McCaughan/McAughern occupiers through the Lisnagaver valuation-revision books.
* Examine Harvey estate rentals, leases, assignments, arrears ledgers, tenant correspondence and surrender records.
* Pay particular attention to lots 24, 25 and 26 and nearby holdings.
* Look for explicit relationships such as daughter, son-in-law, brother, widow or representatives.
* Follow parcel numbers and tenancy succession rather than surnames alone.
* Candidate death entry: Mary Glasgow, 17 February 1892, aged 89, Ballymoney district, D/1892/31/1005/8/234. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Biography == 
Annie was born 21 December 1882 at Kildress townland (not sure whether Lower or Upper). She was the daughter of [[McAlister-2321|Joseph McAlister]] and [[Wallace-26525|Mary Wallace]]. <ref>Cookstown SR District  https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/birth_returns/births_1882/02764/2014915.pdf </ref> <ref>General Record Office Northern Ireland ref: U/1882/99/1009/13/442	Mary	McAlister	21st December 1882	Female	Wallace	Cookstown </ref> 

In 1901 the McAlister family were living in Gortreagh, Joseph 55, his wife Mary Ann 54 and their children Robert 22, Annie 15 and Richard 12. <ref> https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Tyrone/Oaklands/Gortreagh/1729425/ </ref> 

In the family him in 1911 in Gortreagh were Joseph 69, his wife Mary 65 and two of their children Annie 23 and Richard 21. They had been married 40 years with 5 children all still living. <ref> https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1911/Tyrone/Oaklands/Gortreagh/859175/ </ref> 

On 29 Feb 1916 at Clare Church of Ireland, she married Henry Glasgow of Montober, a widowed farmer. Witnessed by Minnie Black and William Glasgow.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/4c34f61720603 Henry Glasgow, Annie McAlister, 1916, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

Mary Ann Glasgow died 28th January 1961. <ref>General Record Office Northern Ireland ref: D/1961/99/1009/32/421	Mary	Glasgow	28th January 1961	77		Female	Cookstown </ref> 

MRS. M. A. GLASGOW, Montober, Cookstown

... WIDESPREAD sorrow was felt in the district on Saturday morning when news of the death of Mrs. Mary Ann Glasgow, Montober, Cookstown, became known. Mrs. Glasgow, a native of Gortreagh, was beloved and respected by all who knew her. She was of a friendly. retiring disposition...  She was buried at Clare Churchyard. The chief mourners were:<ref> 
[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19610204/038/0002 ''Obituary'']], Published: Saturday 04 February 1961. Newspaper: Mid-Ulster Mail </ref> 
* Robert J, George A, David H & [[Glasgow-1768|Ivan H Glasgow]] (sons)
* [[McAlister-2320|Richard McAllister]] (brother)
* Robert Irvine, John Logan, William McConnell (sons-in-law)
* grandson
* David McAllister, Joseph McAllister; Robert, Joseph & Herbert Patterson; Cecil, Samuel, Desmond, Samuel David, Thomas, & Henry G. Glasgow; John Blair, Thomas Henry, Robert Allen, Herbert McFarland, [[Glasgow-1641|Hartley Glasgow]], George Alexander & Andrew Black (nephews)
* [[Black-27577|Andrew Black]] (cousin)

== Research Notes ==
Her mother's 1911 census says "5 children, 5 alive". Considering that we have 4 profiles for her siblings already, this suggests that the 21 Dec 1882 birth registration for "Mary Anne" is probably the "Annie" from the 1901/11 censuses and therefore the wife of Henry Glasgow; even though she is therefore 2 years older than the age recorded on the 1901 census (and 5 years older than the 1911 age).

In the obituary, "son" Ivan H. Glasgow is a stepson.  The nephew is presumably [[Alexander-19840|George Alexander]] although he is a brother-in-law of the cousin Andrew Black; not a nephew.  Have not identified the nephew Andrew Black either. It could perhaps have been reported incorrectly in the newspaper.

[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Dublin/South_City/Wicklow_Street/1305141/ Possible 1901 census] - in a boarding house in Dublin with a bunch of Plymouth Brethren.

== Biography ==

THIS IS THE WEAK LINK IN ELDER FAMILY HISTORY.  IF this is who married our James Elder, then everything is correct.  I need some data point linking her to our James Elder.  There are many James Elders.  I will check their children to see if I can find a link.  I checked death certificate, marriage certificate and neither shows mothers name.  There are many Robert and James and John Elders all around Antrim county.  Other trees on ancestry.com have a mixture of these.  There is no way to be certain unless some other data point is found and I do not know what that could possibly be.  

IF HER LAST NAME WAS SPELLED "MCCAHEREN", THEN I BELIEVE THE PARENTS AND SIBLINGS LISTED ARE CORRECT.  THERE IS ANOTHER Archibald and Elizabeth McCaheren ( married 1816) living in same place with different kids. Mary (but no middle name- THIS IS THE KEY TO DISTINGUISH OUR FAMILY), OTHER SIBLINGS NAMES, ELIZABETH, SERAGH AND MARGARET.  AGAIN, THESE ARE NOT OUR FAMILY. THIS IS ACCORDING TO 1851 CENSUS, ANTRIM.  
Our Archibald was dead by then.  Elizabeth leased land.  Catherine and Robert were linen weavers.
HOWEVER, HER MARRIAGE TO JAMES ELDER IN DERRY, HER LAST NAME IS SPELLED "MCAUGHIN".  HER FATEHRES NAME WAS ALSO ARCHY.  HE HAD TWO CHILDREN I CAN FIND, MARY AND ANNE,  [I suspect, this is our real ancestors and there is just not a lot of info.  I have been unable to find more info. It is quite easy to get lost and get the wrong people. 

Mary Jane was born about 1830.  She passed away in 1904.

The spelling of her last name has been misread or altered through the years.  This spelling is off the original marriage certificate to James Elder.  Also, on the marriage certificate is name of her father, same spelling, and I find him in census under this spelling.[ McAughin]

In 1851, before marriage, she lived in Lisnagavor, Antrim, Ireland.  
In 1901 she lived in Gortereghy, Killoquin, North Antrim, Ireland.   Her husband, James, died  19 Aril 1902 in Gortrighey, Finvoy, Ballymoney, Antrim, Norther Ireland. She died at home in same location with her son by her side.  Death certificate says she died of "senile decay".

== Biography ==
OVERALL, WHAT I HAVE IS CORRECT.  THERE ARE THREE JOHN ELDER THAT ARE SIMILAR.  ON 1900 Fed census he says he was born in MARCH, 1868.  This is only three year off from Mar 1865 where I found birth record in Dirraw, Antrim, Ireland to parents James and Mary Mcagherin Elder. THIS IS MY STRONGEST TIE THAT THIS IS OUR JOHN ELDER.

I believe born in Antrim,  Ireland @ only immigration of John Elder. In census he says 1888, but searched all records and only John Elder arrived May 16, 1887 o ship Devonia [ Note; some web sites mispell it as Deronidi -I looked at Devonia ship manifest and he is there].  He was age 19 which put DOB about 1867 or 1868 but they frequently did not remember their year of birth.  
Ship sailed from Glascow, Scotland. On ship manifest it says he was from Antrim.

I found a John Elder born 15 Mar 1865 in Dirraw, Antrim, Ireland to James Elder and Mary Mcagherin Elder.  I have a note from Joan Elder McNamara, hand written on a piece of paper, saying John Elder was born 21 March 1865.  {This could have been his baptismal date- only 3 days after birth on March 15]  Also found another son born to same couple there, William Elder Nov. 9, 1869 in Dirraw, Antrim but this is different DOB than Elder bible and father's name is James, not John.  could not find a Martha, Robert or Elizabeth.  

Found Elizabeth Elder 26 Jan 1864 born Dirraw, Antrim to John Elder and Mary Jane Mccaheron.  This is different DOB than Elder bible, and fathers name John not James, but Dirraw is very small townsland.

Found death of A.  Mary M'Caghern  in Ballymoney,  Antrim in 1871. at age 30 DOB: 1841

Mary jo says she found some info bout during irish potato famine, Elders migrated from island off the coast of Ireland to Antrim.  This could explain why I am not finding other data.

NOT SURE HOW THIS ALL FITS TOGETHER.
Middle name may or may not be Edward:

I CAN NOT FIND ANYTHING DEFINITELY SAYING WHO IS MOTHER IS, although I think Mary Jane McAughin is most likely based upon above finding.  
Menands Albany Rural cemetery listing does not list John Elder parents, nor does his marriage certificate.  

Middle name of "Edward" is uncertain. This could be a different John Elder.

Joan Elder McNamara says DOB was 3/21/1865*****

1892 Census:  lived in Watervliet age 23  No other data.

1900 Census:  John & Mary Elder at 128 Third St. Watervliet-renting . 
Married 1898  Immigrated 1888.  In USA for 12 years. Day Laborer Naturalized citizens John Born Mar. 1868  Mary born June 1871.  

1905 Census: lived 128 Third St. Watervliet. Worked as Fireman. Immigrated 1887.

1910 Census: lived 128 Second Ave. Watervliet-owned home not mortgage. Worked as Laborer at Valve Works

1920 and 1932 Census: lived 128 Third St, Watervliet-owned home. Laborer at Steel Works.  William, John and Robert lived with them. 

1930 census Immigrated from Northern Ireland 1890. Owned and Lived on 128 Third St. Watervliet, NY in 1930. He worked as foreman in mmill supply.  Son, John age 27 lived with them and   worked as boilermaker for D&H railroad. House value $ 3500.  Rented to a John & Ella Elder with daughter (?? possibly Olive)) ages 32/31/9.  

Had a farm in Watervliet, NY. They definitely raised chickens for eggs- egg farm and raised dairy cows. .  This gave them  protein during the depression.  They were "White Lace Irish" meaning were well off.  They brought nice things from Ireland, such as lace tablecloths and bought the farm.

Married Mary A. Harper 24 June 1898 Jermain Memorial Presbyterian Church, Watervliet, NY Minister: George Bohne???   Witness: Sophia Harper& George Bohne  @ US Presbyterian Church Records 1701-1970.  

Marriage records Presbyterian Church do not list minister but show George and Sophia as witness's. 

Sophia Harper is listed as Sophia Bohne at funeral records of this John Elder which implies Sophia married George who was a minister at Germain Memorial.  Sophia was Mary Harper's sister.   Joan Elder called her Aunt Sophia. Possibly, Sophia Harper and Mary and possibly Adam Harper immigrated together because MR. & Mrs. Adam Harper were at the funeral.

== Biography ==
Elder bible: Notes by Joan Elder McNamara

Father was Robert Elder.  He was born on Finvoy Road, Ballymoney, Antrim which runs from Ballymoney south to Rasherkin.

1851 Census I can not find any Elders (except Matilda Elder as Head) in parishes of Rasharkin nor Ballymoney
in 1855  lived in Gortereghy, Kilrea, Londonderry, Northern Ireland.  His wife's death certificate says he was a farmer.
1862 land records show James, Joseph, Robert, Ellen all leased land from Robert Harvey in "Kilconway, Gortereghy, Rasharkin, Antrim, Ireland"  Robert was flax farmer, the other leased house, offices and land. 

Married in Tamlaght Ocrilly, Derry, Ireland according to ancestry.com.  This is just SW of Rasharin and today in Derry (Londonderry)  County with a population of 121.  At its peak it had 10,460 residents in 1841  with a Presbyterian church and two Roman Catholic chapels.  I am not sure where I got the marriage having taken place in Rasharkin, County Antrim- although this is just a stones throw away.  

Somewhere I had James's death in 1880-just not sure where I got that.  This is a death certificate with death 19 April 1902, dying from dementia, a farmer, with his wife Mary at his side in Gortereghy. Death certrifgicate says he was born around 1820, which is what we think.  Mary also died in Gortereghy two years later, so it fits. 

Possible sister is Elizabeth Elder [ Elder-6372] born 1819 Rasharkin, County Antrim and married Robert Biggart ( Biggart-77   born 1819)  on April 26, 1850.

33132504.Name: McCaughan-128
33132504.DeathLocation: Rochester Township, Beaver, Pennsylvania, United States
33132504.bio:
== Biography ==
Was born in Ireland in 1773. Immigrated to Philadelphia (PA) in 1792, where he was a teacher. He married Hannah Jane Johnson. 20 March, 1802 in Blount County, TN. They moved to Trigg County, Kentucky, where he had been hired to survey, and laid out the town, County Seat, of Cadiz. He parents are Patrick and Rose ( Stuart) McCaughan. All of their children were born in Trigg County, KY. Family history claims that he went to Ireland for a visit, and on the way home, he fell while aboardship, and was injured. He made it back to a hotel, in Rochester, PA, it is thought, where he died, and was buried locally there...though no one has been able to locate his grave..The grave of his wife, HAnnah, is believed to be in Shelby County, Ohio, where they moved after leaving Trigg Co., though noone has been able to locate her final resting place as well. I make this Memorial, until such time as his true grave is found, in order to compile the relationships between him, wife Hannah, their children and decendants.

June 24, 1992 – The Cadiz Record printed a story about the Rock House, formally named “Rocky Ridge”, which is purported to be the oldest house in Trigg County. The house was built for John McCaughan (Ma-con) and is located north of the Montgomery community.
McCaughan came to the United States from Ireland in 1792 and settled in Philadelphia. A few years later he obtained permission to act as a surveyor in Kentucky. McCaughan received a land grant of over 2,500 acres in what would later become Trigg County. He built a log cabin on this land, and named it “Rocky Ridge”.
In 1802, McCaughan married Hannah Johnston from Blount County, Tennessee. They first lived in the log cabin, but built the stone house around 1807. Rocky Ridge has a basement, two stories and an attic, with seven fireplaces, and solid stone walls that are 27 inches thick.
McCaughan was appointed as surveyor of the newly formed Trigg County in 1820, and was responsible for laying out the town of Cadiz. A troubled conscience drove McCaughan to free his slaves in 1831, and give them each a piece of land. John, Hannah, and two of their sons moved to Ohio and settled among people with similar beliefs.
In its early years, the house served as the Rocky Ridge post office and a stagecoach stop, and later as a boarding school. The Rock House is an excellent example of a two-story dry-stone house of the type commonly built by the Scotch-Irish in central Kentucky, and is the only one of this style found in Western Kentucky. According to legend, the builder of Rocky Ridge was paid with a muzzle loading gun. The builder, whose name is unknown, next built an identical house at the Shaker Village near Harrodsburg, Kentucky.

Beechy Mire – Dixon Township
Post Office: 1833 – 1846
Location: unknown
Description: The town was founded by Irish immigrant John McCaughan (1773 – 1850) who was the postmaster and was a surveyor by trade. John arrived in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania about 1792 and worked as a merchant and school teacher. He married Hannah Jane (Johnston) McCaughan (1781 – died c. 1864) from Tennessee in 1802. They subsequently moved to Trigg County, Kentucky, had 8 children, and lived in house built out of a rock in 1815. The area became known as Rocky Ridge. John acquired most of the county’s land, a total of 3,000 acres, and some slaves in payment for completing surveying duties. The family attended a Presbyterian church and didn’t agree with how slaves were normally treated in those days. Their slaves were welcome to attend church with them and learn how to read and write if they chose to. John freed them sometime around 1830 by giving each a dollar, then selling them land for the dollar to make the transactions legal. He also donated land for a church their purchased area. After that, John and Hannah moved to Preble County and founded Beechy Mire. They relocated to Steuben County, Indiana in the mid-1840s and the Beechy Mire post office moved to Union County, Indiana. John made a trip to Ireland to visit family in 1850 and was injured from a falling accident on a ship during his return voyage. He made it to Rochester, Pennsylvania but died in a hotel room before the next morning and was reportedly interred in Rochester. Unfortunately, an extensive search didn’t reveal the burial locations of John and Hannah.

Research notes:  This may be a different person, however, the name, birth date and location of birth match, as well as the questions surrounding  his end of life journey. 33132561.Name: Johnston-24031
33132561.bio:
== Biography ==
Hanna was born about 1781. She passed away in 1864. 

THE IMMIGRANT
JOHN McCAUGHAN
N. IRELAND TO Pennsylvania IN 1795, TO Kentucky.
1- JOHN McCAUGHAN: of whom I have referred to as "John The Surveyor", in my books because there are so many John McCaughan's, born 12 April 1773, County Antrim, Ireland. He cane to Philadelphia around 1792 where he was a merchant and a school teacher. He at least had connections in Blount County, Tennessee for he owned land there before he went to Trigg County, Kentucky as a Government Surveyor. We know that Blount County, Temessee had a very active Covenanter Presbyterian Church, of which he was a member. He married HANNAH JANE JOHNSTON from Blount County, Temessee 20 March 1802. There were several Johnston families in Blount County so we don't know which were her parents.

Their first home in Trigg County, Kentucky was no doubt a log cabin. In Rev. Charles Thompson's autobiography he states that the rock home was built around 1815. It was called "Rocky Ridge". Now, the whole area is called that. It is about two miles east and one mile north of Cadiz, Kentucky on the Hopkinsville, Eddyville roads. It is a beautiful two story rock home with a basement. We heard that a brick mason was traveling through and built the home for a good rifle. Through the years, since the McCaughan's owned it, it has been a stage coach stop, a post office and a private school. In 1946 when they started restoring it, it was so run down, it was full of hay. In 1955, Herbert and Frances Sizemore bought it and have done a beautiful job restoring it back to the original state. He told me he found a rock slab to the side where the kitchen had been and also found the rock floors he thought were the slave quarters.

We spent three days in the court house in Cadiz, Kentucky and all one has to do is look in the early books to see that John McCaughan, at one time or another, owned most of the land in Trigg County. Their copying machine was broken so all we got done was jot down what he sold. Since he was a surveyor, he would be able to know what was being sold cheaply and too, some of the land was given to him for services he rendered. The days we were there , a man kept running in, look up something, and be gone. On the third day, we started talking to him and told him what we were doing. He said, "Tell me something, I run across John McCaughan's name every day. He owned most of Trigg County, why did he settle on the worse land around?" We couldn't answer that. Possible since he owned so much land, they built where rock was available, near the rock quary.

In a letter we have, written by a granddaughter, she tells of John McCaughan planting a peach orchard and he had such a good crop of peaches he gave some to anyone around who wanted some. He later heard that some of the men had made peach brandy out of their peaches. It made him so mad, he cut down his trees.

Schools were so few and far apart in the area and were not teaching up to John McCaughan's standards so when the two older boys became old enough, they were sent to a private school run by one of John's friends. They were gone three or four years and their mother missed them so badly that when the other children got old enough to go, she couldn't part with them so a tutor was hired. Because of this better education, wherever these children settled, they were the leaders in the communities where they settled.

392.

John and Hannah became very unhappy with the south. The closest Covenanter Presbyterian church was 30 miles away so they didn't get to go to church very often, but Rev. Charles mentioned that each Sunday was spent in worship and studying the Bible. The slaves were free to worship and study with them. No slave worked on Sunday. Tom, the overseer, owned his own horse and was free to come and go as he chose. When the tutor was hired, any slave who wanted to learn was taught how to read and write. Rev. Charles mentions also that Haggar, their nanny, was very smart. She soon was able to read and write and she was always at their church services.

Around 1830, twenty years before the Civil War, the Presbyterian church came out that it was not right for a man to own another man. John McCaughan freed each of his slaves. He gave then each a dollar, gave them land around Rocky Ridge but made them give him back the dollar for payment so no one could ever get their land from them. He then gave them land for a church.

John took his wife and the three youngest children to Preble county, Ohio and later they moved to Stueben County. By the time they left Kentucky, the older children had married so stayed in the south. The oldest son, Kain Alexander, stayed at Rocky Ridge and sold off his father's land, which consisted of 3,000 acres, for him. Rocky Ridge was the last to be sold in 1849, recorded 15 December 1850. It is the oldest building in Trigg County, Temessee. John Johnston and Mary Am went to the coast of Mississippi, James to the middle part of Mississippi, so grandsons of John McCaughan fought on both sides of the Civil War.

In 1850, John McCaughan decided to go back and see his kin in Ireland. He asked his daughter, Nancy Jane, and her husband, John Wilson, to come to take care of things while he was gone. On his way home, his last day out, he fell aboard ship and injured himself however was able to get to Rochester, Pemsylvania where he rented a room at the inn. The next morning the owner found that John had died during the night. He is buried in Rochester with a wrought iron fence around his grave.

Hannah Jane Johnston was born 24 March 1781. After her husband's death, Nancy and John Wilson stayed with Hamah, helping her. She died around 1864. Their children:

----2-1 KAIN ALEXANDER McCAUGHAN

----2-2 JOHN JOHNSTON McCAUGHAN

----2-3 JAMES LEE McCAUGHAN

----2-4 MARY ANN McCAUGHAN

----2-5 THOMAS BOSTON McCAUGHAN (1)

----2-6 REV. CHARLES THOMPSON McCAUGHAN, D.D.

----2-7 THOMAS BOSTON McCAUGHAN (2)

----2-8 NANCY JANE McCAUGHAN


We have not found out why the name Thomas Boston was so important that they named two sons that. This was a very interesting line to work. Since the boys were the Leaders, they were Representatives, and they wrote many articles for their local newspaper. They had a charter and plamed to build a railroad from the coast of Mississippi, through thestate to Memphis, Temessee, this is why John settled on the coast and James in the middle of the state, but since James and John died young, this was never completed.

- J. D. McCaughan, for many years a prominent resident of Gonzales County, died at his home near Wrightsboro at 8 o'clock this morning, after a long illness. He was an ex-Confederate soldier, and is survived by his wife and the following children: Mrs. Zach Snell and Mrs. A. Williams, Ballinger; Mrs. M. C. Ellis, Dewet; Mrs. P. W. Jane's husband Henry died of heart failure in 1890.  Jane's brother Robert had been present at the time.  Her son William died in 1893.  His death was registered by Jane's mother Sarah Simpson.

In the 1901 Ireland census, Jane Elliott, a widow, was age 38 living at Tehorny, Rasharkin, County Antrim with her children Henry Elliott (13), Samuel Elliott (11) and Sarah Elliott (9).  Also Isaac Elder (23), farm servant.<ref>National Archives of Ireland. 1901 Ireland census: http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Antrim/Killoquin_North/Tehorney/946758/</ref>

Isaac and Jane Elder had a son, Robert Alexander Elder (b.1903).

Isaac Elder died of tuberculosis in 1910 at Tehorny, Rasharkin, County Antrim. 

In the 1911 Ireland census, Jane Elliott (sic), a widow, was age 48 living at Tehorny, Rasharkin, County Antrim with her children Samuel James Elliott (21), Sarah J M Elliott (19) and Robert Al Elder (7).<ref>National Archives of Ireland. 1911 Ireland census: http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1911/Antrim/Killoquin__Upper/Tehorny/130409/</ref>

Henry's father Henry Elliott died of heart failure in 1890.

In the 1901 Ireland census, Henry Elliott was age 13 living at Tehorny, Rasharkin, County Antrim with his mother Jane Elliott (38), a widow, and sblings Samuel Elliott(11) and Sarah Elliott (9).  Also Isaac Elder (23), farm servant.<ref>National Archives of Ireland. 1901 Ireland census: http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Antrim/Killoquin_North/Tehorney/946758/</ref>

Henry appears to have emigrated to Colonie, Albany, New York, United States in 1909.<ref name="1910 census"/>

In the 1910 US census, Henry Elliott was age 21, a hired man, living at Colonie, Albany, New York, United States in the household of William W Hannell (43), with William's wife Alice Hannell (33) and three children. Also Mary H Wilson (22), servant.<ref name="1910 census">"United States Census, 1910," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M5CQ-43M : accessed 27 October 2019), Henry J Elliott in household of William W Hannell, Colonie, Albany, New York, United States; citing enumeration district (ED) ED 131, sheet 3B, family 44, NARA microfilm publication T624 (Washington D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, 1982), roll 922; FHL microfilm 1,374,935.</ref>

Henry Elliott married Anna M Darragh, originally from County Antrim, Ireland, but also living in Colonie, Albany, New York, some time between 1910 and 1917.  Henry Elliott appeared on the US Draft registration in and is listed as a dairy farmer operating his own farm and as being married<ref>"United States World War I Draft Registration Cards, 1917-1918", database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KXTD-9XG : 24 August 2019), Henry John Elliott, 1917-1918.</ref>

Henry and Annie Elliott do not appear to have had any children.  Henry joined Annie in the home of her uncle Robert Graffin after their marriage.

In the 1920 US census, Henry Elliott was age 31, living at Colonie, Albany, New York, United States with his wife Anna Elliott (30) in the household of his wife's uncle Robert Grafton (sic) (68).<ref>"United States Census, 1920," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MJKZ-DRV : accessed 27 October 2019), Henry Elliott in household of Robert Grafton, Colonie, Albany, New York, United States; citing  ED 147, sheet 1A, line 4, family 2, NARA microfilm publication T625 (Washington D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, 1992), roll 1083; FHL microfilm 1,821,083.</ref>

In the 1930 US census, Henry Elliott was age 40, living at Colonie, Albany, New York, United States with his wife Anna Elliott (35) and his wife's uncle Robert Graffin (75).<ref>"United States Census, 1930," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X7HS-KN6 : accessed 27 October 2019), Henery Elliott, Colonie, Albany, New York, United States; citing enumeration district (ED) ED 130, sheet 13B, line 91, family 282, NARA microfilm publication T626 (Washington D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, 2002), roll 1405; FHL microfilm 2,341,140.</ref>

Henry Elliot died in September 1936 in Colonie, Albany, New York.  He was buried at Albany Rural Cemetery Menands, Albany, New York.<ref>"Find A Grave Index," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q2D2-MS8R : 6 December 2016), Henry John Elliott, 1936; Burial, Menands, Albany, New York, United States of America, Albany Rural Cemetery; {{FindAGrave|172046521|sameas=yes}} </ref>

Elder bible: Notes by Joan Elder McNamara

Father was Robert Elder.  He was born on Finvoy Road, Ballymoney, Antrim which runs from Ballymoney south to Rasherkin.

1851 Census I can not find any Elders (except Matilda Elder as Head) in parishes of Rasharkin nor Ballymoney
in 1855  lived in Gortereghy, Kilrea, Londonderry, Northern Ireland.  His wife's death certificate says he was a farmer.
1862 land records show James, Joseph, Robert, Ellen all leased land from Robert Harvey in "Kilconway, Gortereghy, Rasharkin, Antrim, Ireland"  Robert was flax farmer, the other leased house, offices and land. 

Married in Tamlaght Ocrilly, Derry, Ireland according to ancestry.com.  This is just SW of Rasharin and today in Derry (Londonderry)  County with a population of 121.  At its peak it had 10,460 residents in 1841  with a Presbyterian church and two Roman Catholic chapels.  I am not sure where I got the marriage having taken place in Rasharkin, County Antrim- although this is just a stones throw away.  

Somewhere I had James's death in 1880-just not sure where I got that.  This is a death certificate with death 19 April 1902, dying from dementia, a farmer, with his wife Mary at his side in Gortereghy. Death certrifgicate says he was born around 1820, which is what we think.  Mary also died in Gortereghy two years later, so it fits. 

Possible sister is Elizabeth Elder [ Elder-6372] born 1819 Rasharkin, County Antrim and married Robert Biggart ( Biggart-77   born 1819)  on April 26, 1850.

29316591.Name: Elder-3946
29316591.bio:
== Biography ==
Elder bible: Notes by Joan Elder McNamara

Father was Robert Elder.  He was born on Finvoy Road, Ballymoney, Antrim which runs from Ballymoney south to Rasherkin.

1851 Census I can not find any Elders (except Matilda Elder as Head) in parishes of Rasharkin nor Ballymoney
in 1855  lived in Gortereghy, Kilrea, Londonderry, Northern Ireland.  His wife's death certificate says he was a farmer.
1862 land records show James, Joseph, Robert, Ellen all leased land from Robert Harvey in "Kilconway, Gortereghy, Rasharkin, Antrim, Ireland"  Robert was flax farmer, the other leased house, offices and land. 

Married in Tamlaght Ocrilly, Derry, Ireland according to ancestry.com.  This is just SW of Rasharin and today in Derry (Londonderry)  County with a population of 121.  At its peak it had 10,460 residents in 1841  with a Presbyterian church and two Roman Catholic chapels.  I am not sure where I got the marriage having taken place in Rasharkin, County Antrim- although this is just a stones throw away.  

Somewhere I had James's death in 1880-just not sure where I got that.  This is a death certificate with death 19 April 1902, dying from dementia, a farmer, with his wife Mary at his side in Gortereghy. Death certrifgicate says he was born around 1820, which is what we think.  Mary also died in Gortereghy two years later, so it fits. 

Possible sister is Elizabeth Elder [ Elder-6372] born 1819 Rasharkin, County Antrim and married Robert Biggart ( Biggart-77   born 1819)  on April 26, 1850.
== Sources ==
1851 census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim
NOTE: Ballymoney, Rasharkin, and Fivoy, as well as others, are all Parishes in Kilconway Barony
<references />
* Elder Family Bible

47726743.Name: McAughin-1
47726743.DeathLocation: Gortereghy, Finvoy, Ballymoney, County Antrim, Ireland,
47726743.bio:
== Biography ==

THIS IS THE WEAK LINK IN ELDER FAMILY HISTORY.  IF this is who married our James Elder, then everything is correct.  I need some data point linking her to our James Elder.  There are many James Elders.  I will check their children to see if I can find a link.  I checked death certificate, marriage certificate and neither shows mothers name.  There are many Robert and James and John Elders all around Antrim county.  Other trees on ancestry.com have a mixture of these.  There is no way to be certain unless some other data point is found and I do not know what that could possibly be.  

IF HER LAST NAME WAS SPELLED "MCCAHEREN", THEN I BELIEVE THE PARENTS AND SIBLINGS LISTED ARE CORRECT.  THERE IS ANOTHER Archibald and Elizabeth McCaheren ( married 1816) living in same place with different kids. Mary (but no middle name- THIS IS THE KEY TO DISTINGUISH OUR FAMILY), OTHER SIBLINGS NAMES, ELIZABETH, SERAGH AND MARGARET.  AGAIN, THESE ARE NOT OUR FAMILY. THIS IS ACCORDING TO 1851 CENSUS, ANTRIM.  
Our Archibald was dead by then.  Elizabeth leased land.  Catherine and Robert were linen weavers.
HOWEVER, HER MARRIAGE TO JAMES ELDER IN DERRY, HER LAST NAME IS SPELLED "MCAUGHIN".  HER FATEHRES NAME WAS ALSO ARCHY.  HE HAD TWO CHILDREN I CAN FIND, MARY AND ANNE,  [I suspect, this is our real ancestors and there is just not a lot of info.  I have been unable to find more info. It is quite easy to get lost and get the wrong people. 

Mary Jane was born about 1830.  She passed away in 1904.

The spelling of her last name has been misread or altered through the years.  This spelling is off the original marriage certificate to James Elder.  Also, on the marriage certificate is name of her father, same spelling, and I find him in census under this spelling.[ McAughin]

In 1851, before marriage, she lived in Lisnagavor, Antrim, Ireland.  
In 1901 she lived in Gortereghy, Killoquin, North Antrim, Ireland.   Her husband, James, died  19 Aril 1902 in Gortrighey, Finvoy, Ballymoney, Antrim, Norther Ireland. She died at home in same location with her son by her side.  Death certificate says she died of "senile decay".

6111255.Name: Wallace-3464
6111255.bio:
== Biography == 
Cillimon Wallace was born in 1846 in Ballynure, Larne, County Antrim. He was the son of [[Wallace-3459|William]] and [[Junkin-6|Mary Eliza ]] (''née'' Junkin) Wallace.

Cillimon married [[Dickson-844|Emma Dickson]] on the 19th June 1868 in Carrickfergus, County Antrim. <ref>
'''Marriage''':
Department of Arts, Heritage, Regional, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs, "Civil Records," database with images, IrishGenealogy.ie, marriage of Cillimon Wallace and Emma Dickson, 19 June 1868, Registration District/Office: Carrickfergus; entry 102 of the 'copied register' of the Marriage Register Books, signed and dated 19 June 1868 by James Michaud. (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1868/11458/8210442.pdf : accessed 29 December 2022).
</ref>

Cillimon passed away on the 5th May 1886 in Carrickfergus.

6111422.Name: Dickson-844
6111422.bio:
== Biography == 
Emma was born in 1848 in Carrickfergus, County Antrim. She was the daughter of [[Dickson-971|John Dickson]].

Emma married [[Wallace-3464|Cillimon Wallace]] on the 19th June 1868 in Carrickfergus. <ref>
'''Marriage''':
Department of Arts, Heritage, Regional, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs, "Civil Records," database with images, IrishGenealogy.ie, marriage of Cillimon Wallace and Emma Dickson, 19 June 1868, Registration District/Office: Carrickfergus; entry 102 of the 'copied register' of the Marriage Register Books, signed and dated 19 June 1868 by James Michaud. (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1868/11458/8210442.pdf : accessed 29 December 2022).
</ref>

Emma died on the 1s April 1918 in Belfast, County Antrim.

Anderson-41446.bio:
== Biography ==
Neal was born about 1804

Married Elizabeth Crawford 

 He passed away in 1877 at the age of 73
<ref>
https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie
</ref>
===Will===
A transcription of the digital copy of the will on the PRONI website: “The will and testament of Neal Anderson of Gortreigh in the County of Antrim. I will and bequeath to my three sons the farm of land which I now occupy. I give to my son Neal Twelve acres on the North side of the Farm and the lower part of the dwelling house. To my son Abraham I give twelve acres adjoining the other together with the upper part of the dwelling house. To my son Robert I give twelve acres on the south side together with the Housing situated thereon. To my daughter Elizabeth I give ten pounds stg and to my daughter Mary I give ten pound stg. To my wife Elizabeth I give ten pound stg. To my daughter Anna I give ten pounds stg. To my daughter Leonora I give one pound stg. To my daughter Sarah I give ten pounds stg. To my daughter Isabella I give ten pounds stg if she claims it. All the above sums each of the Boys are to pay an equal share. But in no case do I allow it to be paid for inside five years from the present date. I hereby allow all my legal debts to be paid by my three sons each an equal share. I give to each of my three sons an equal share of my chattle property.
Neal Anderson X His Mark
Witness Robert Adams, John Deullin”

===Probate===
“Letters of Administration (with the Will annexed) of the personal estate of Neal Anderson late of Gortreighy County Antrim Farmer who died 10 April 1877 at same place were granted at Belfast to Neal Anderson of Gortreighy Farmer one of the Residuary Legatees.”

24725689.bio:
== Biography ==
Helena was born in 1842. She was the daughter of [[Anderson-41446|Neal Anderson]] and [[Crawford-11632|Betty Crawford]]. She married Martin McFetridge on 22 Oct 1867   She was mentioned in her father’s will in 1877, along with her mother and siblings. She passed away in 1933. 
===Marriage===
Transcription of the digital image of the marriage certificate on Irishgenealogy website:
“:SCHEDULE G. ] Registrar’s District of Ballymena
:Marriage solemnized At Clough In the Parish of Dunaghy in the Co Antrim
:No: 152; 
:When married: Oct 22 1867
:Name and Surname: Martin McFetridge; Lenora Anderson
:Age: full; full
:Condition: Bachelor; spinster
:Rank or profession: farmer
:Residence at the time of the marriage: Eglish; Portna
:Father’s Name and Surname: Hugh McFetridge; Neill Anderson
:Rank or Profession of father: Farmer; Farmer
:Married in the Clough Pres Church according to the form and discipline of the Presbyterian Church By License by me James Reutoul
:This marriage was solmnized between us Martin McFetridge X His Mark, Lenora Anderson X Her Mark, in the presence of us Mary Ann Crawford; Alexander Montgomery”
===Probate===
“McFetridge Helena of Drumagrove county Antrim widow died 22 December 1933 Probate Belfast 6 March to George Bellis Caruth solicitor. Effects £117 16s.”

== Biography ==

'''Sarah (Dysart) McCaughern''' — recorded as '''Sallie''' — was a daughter of [[Dysart-1684|James Dysart]] and [[Glasglow-11|Jane Catherine (Glasgow) Dysart]] of Crushybracken, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. She was a minor when she married [[McCaughern-23|John McCaughern]] of Gortereghy at Rasharkin Presbyterian Church on 18 March 1851.

Her daughter [[McCaughern-24|Mary Anne McCaughern]] was named residuary legatee in the 1881 will of her grandfather James Dysart. Sarah is the "Sallie, daughter of Jane Dysart, residing at Ballymena" of the 14 January 1892 probate citation of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]].

The civil register describes her as married and "the wife of a farmer", and records the cause of death as heart disease of two years' duration, certified. Her husband [[Dysart-1684|James Dysart]], who signed by his mark as "James Dysert", was present at her death at Crushybracken; the death was registered on 22 September 1868.<ref name="JaneDeathGRONI">General Register Office for Northern Ireland, death register, Ballymena superintendent registrar's district, Clough registrar's district, entry 418, 13 September 1868: Jane Dysert, Crushybracken, Rasharkin parish, female, married, 64, the wife of a farmer; cause disease of the heart, two years, certified; informant James Dysert (his mark), present at death, Crushybracken; registered 22 September 1868. He married [[Dysart-1893|Sarah Dysart]] of Crushybracken, daughter of Jas Dysart, farmer, at Rasharkin Presbyterian Church on 18 March 1851; the witnesses were Thomas Henry and Archibald McCaughern.

== Biography ==
Joseph Jubilee Elder was born in 1871. He was the son of Joseph William Elder and Sarah Jane Manning.

Joseph married [[Hill-59261|Lula Laura Hill]] on 8 December 1892 in Clay County, Alabama.

He passed away in 1958 in New Point, Mathews County, Virginia. He is buried at Rose Hill Cemetery in York, York County, South Carolina.
=== Obituary ===
The ''Daily Press'' (Newport News, Virginia), Tuesday, 29 July 1958, page 14:
:Joseph J. Elder Dies At Age 88 
:MATHEWS -- Joseph Jubilee Elder, 88, died Monday in the Horne Harbor Nursing Home here after a lengthy illness. A former resident of York. S.C., he made his home for several years with a daughter, Mrs. Roy W. Kennedy, of 111 Post St., Newport News. 
:Other survivors include another daughter, Mrs. Coit Lineberger, of Dallas, N.C.; two sons, Robert A. Elder, of Albemare, N.C. and Russell B. Elder, a patient at Veterans Hospital, Mountain Home, Tenn; one brother, Wych Elder, of Rock Hill. SC.; two sisters, Mrs. Lula Strickland and Mrs. Nettie Strickland, of Texas; five grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren. 
:Funerla services will be held at 2 p.m. Wednesday in the York Funeral Home. Burial will be in Rose Hill Cemetery, York.

ELDER.—On May 29, at Gore (the result of a motor accident), Alexander Elder, agent for Storne and Co., Invercargill. [https://icc.govt.nz/cemetery-result/?id=36586 Alexander Elder cemetery record] : Name: ALEXANDER, ELDER : Gender: Male : Date of Burial: Friday, 01 June 1917 : Cemetery: Eastern Cemetery : Classification - Block/Plot: General - 19 / 99 All records for this plot in Eastern Cemetery : ELDER JOHN H 62 Years - Burial: 18 October 1934 : ELDER MARGARET 83 Years - Burial: 28 February 1957 : ELDER ALEXANDER 42 Years - Burial: 1 June 1917 : ELDER HELEN JANE 28 Years - Burial: 12 July 1906 Probate of will: Alexander died 30 May 1917 intestate, a batchelor. NZBDM deaths 23/3/1918 1918/2797 Elder, Alexander, 74Y From his obituary and the probate of his son Alexander's estate, we know that since about 1878 Alexander (senior) was a farmer in Kakanui, which is on the East Coast, south of Oamaru, Otago. Obituary [https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/NOT19180326.2.24 North Otago Times, Volume CVI, Issue 14081, 26 March 1918, Page 3]
ALEXANDER ELDER On Saturday, at Invercargill, the death occurred of one of the early settlers of Otago in the person of Mr Alexander Elder, who had resided at Kakanui for forty years, Mr Elder, who was a farmer, was a staunch supporter of the Presbyterian Church, taking a keen interest in its Sunday School, besides being an elder of some years' standing in the Church itself. Mr Elder indirectly met his death through, catching a chill during a visit to Roxburgh. The deceased gentleman was a widower, Mrs Elder having been dead for several years. He leaves a family of four sons and two daughters (Messrs Donald Elder (Auckland), John and William Elder (Invercargill), and Jas. Elder (of Kakanui), and Mesdames A. McKenzie (Southland) and W. Gillies (Oamaru). The funeral will take place from the Presbyterian Church at Kakanui to-day. He is buried in block 2 plot 73 of the Maheno Cemetery. == Biography == Alexander Montgomery was born about 1784 in County Antrim of Ireland. He was the son of Archibald Montgomery (1747–1823) and Sarah Campbell (1737–??) who were married about 1767 at Boltna-Connell, Antrim, Ireland. He had seven siblings; William 1768, John 1771, Margaret 1773, Elizabeth 1776, Joshua 1778, Alexander 1784, Henry 1788 and Mary ??. Alexander was married to Anne Eliza (Agnes?) Neill in about 1810, probably in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of James Neill. They had ten children; James Neill 1811, Sarah 1812, Mary 1814, Margaret 1817, Eliza Swan 1820, Archibald 1821, Catherine 1825, Henry 1826, Alexander 1829 and Nancy 1829. Alexander was a farmer. He was in a land valuation record in Dundesert, Antrim, Ireland. He had a house, offices, a corn mill, kiln, and stores. On 16 October 1835, Alexander's neighbors were John Thompson, Thomas Robb, John Palmer, Alexander Higgs' son, and Robert McCune. 38023044.bio:
== Biography == Archibald was born about 1737. Archibald's child Rev. Dr. [[Montgomery-17854|Henry Montgomery LLD (1788-1865)]] was written-up in a national biographical directory in 1865. It records that Archibald "held a commission in the Irish volunteers of 1778 and was usually styled lieutenant." Archibald's two oldest sons William and John ("United Irishmen") fought in the battle of Antrim on 7 Jun 1798. Archibald's house was burned down by men looking for William and John two days later. 38023064.bio:
== Biography == Sarah was born about 1737 and had eight children (one son and two daughters died early). Her son-in-law wrote a biography about her son [[Montgomery-17854|Henry Montgomery LLD (1788-1865)]]. He describes Sarah as a fearless woman and a fierce mother in the face of insurgents burning down her house in search of her "United Irishmen" sons after the Battle of Antrim in 1798. '''Book''', "The Life of the Reverend Henry Montgomery, LLD" (pages 10-16); author: the Rev. John A. Crozier, A.B; publisher: London: E.T. Whitfield and Simpkin, Marshall & Co.; and Belfast: W.H.Greer; 1875; made available on the Forgotten Books website. [https://www.forgottenbooks.com/en/readbook/TheLifeoftheRevHenryMontgomeryLLDDunmurryBelfast_10234552#26.] == Research Notes == * There is a difference between two sources in the name of Sarah's father - John or William. However, both sources record that his home was in Killealy, Killead parish. So, they likely point to the same person.
