MIC1P/87; posted to the Bann Valley Genealogy mailing list 2002-10-12, hosted by Richard Torrens, www.4qd.org/bann/ (accessed Dec. 2002); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Marriages/1828.html.</ref>

: He married [[Gordon-17989|Mary Gordon]] about 1795 or so, possibly when the Rev. John Smith was still the minister at Kilrea First Presbyterian church. <ref>Kernohan, J.W. The ''Parishes of Kilrea and Tamlaght O'Crilly: A sketch of their history, with an account of Boveedy congregation''. Coleraine: Coleraine Chronicle office, 1912. Extracts online at [http://genealogy.torrens.org/index.html Bann Valley Genealogy], hosted by Richard Torrens. — See the sub-headiing, "Rev. John Smith" in [http://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/books/Kilrea/Kilrea03.html Part 2].</ref>

: Adam Kilpatrick/Kirkpatrick died sometime before 1826, when the Tithe Applotment records for the parish of Kilrea listed his widow as the named occupier of their several acres in Lislea townland. <ref name="tithe" />

== Research notes ==
* '''Please do not attach this profile to an earlier, supposed parent.'''—There were earlier Kilpatrick/Kirkpatrick men in the parish of Kilrea. While it might be tempting to attach Adam Kilpatrick as the son or brother of one of them, there is no genealogical evidence to support this kind of supposition. This conclusion has been drawn after a very careful study, conducted by [[Kilpatrick-1128]] of the available records held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland in Belfast during several research trips between 2001–2018. Church records survive only from 1825; rent rolls are non-existent; and a search for wills and administrations, newspaper articles, rent rolls, bonds, and other legal documents have yielded null results.  

:: — ''Please contact the profile manager should you discover sound genealogical evidence which might support the addition of a parent or other family member''. (2022-08-02) —
* Estimated year of birth:—based on the –estimated– year of birth of Adam's and Mary's eldest child, Elizabeth. Elizabeth having married Samuel Irwin before 1825‡— and their first child (Mary) born in 1826, <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation.'' Record of Baptism.'' Extract: “No. 69. 1826 Mary daughter of Samuel Irwin of Moyknock and Betty Kilpatrick his wife born 19th April and baptized this 21st day of April 1826.” Extract by Barbara Braswell, 2003-10-22; hosted online by Richard Torrens, “Kilrea First Presbyterian Church Records,” Bann Valley Genealogy genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/ (accessed 2021-06-22).</ref> the estimated year of birth for Elizabeth has been set at 1800. Thus, the estimate for Adam Kilpatrick is strictly an estimate. — ‡ Note:—Records of marriage in Kilrea First Presbyterian survive from mid-1825. ~[[Kilpatrick-1128]]
* Estimated year of marriage:—has been set at five years before the estimated date of birth for Adam's and Mary's eldest child, Elizabeth.
* Estimated year of death:—occurred before 1826 when Adam's widow, Mary Gordon, was listed as the named occupier of their holding in Lislea townland. <ref name="tithe" />

== Biography ==
: Mary Gordon was born about 1775 in Lislea townland in the parish of Kilrea, county Londonderry.

: She married [[Kilpatrick-2115|Adam Kilpatrick]] (''alias'' Kirkpatrick) about 1795 or so, possibly when the Rev. John Smith was still the minister at Kilrea First Presbyterian church. <ref>Kernohan, J.W. The ''Parishes of Kilrea and Tamlaght O'Crilly: A sketch of their history, with an account of Boveedy congregation''. Coleraine: Coleraine Chronicle office, 1912. Extracts online at [http://genealogy.torrens.org/index.html Bann Valley Genealogy], hosted by Richard Torrens. — See the sub-headiing, "Rev. John Smith" in [http://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/books/Kilrea/Kilrea03.html Part 2].</ref>

: In 1826, Mary was recorded as In 1826, “Widow Kirkpatrick,” the head of the household in the Tithe Applotment book for the parish of Kilrea. She held 6 acres 2 roods 10 perches of land, Irish Plantation measure in Lislea townland. <ref>Church of Ireland. ''Commissioner’s Return Under the Tithe Composition Act (Tithe Applotment Book)''. Parish of Kilrea, Diocese of Derry (1826). Henry Ellis, Esq., and James Courtenay, Commissioners. Extract: “No. 44. Tenant’s name: Widow Kirkpatrick. Content: 6A 2R 10P. Acreage Value per Acre: 35[d.] Amout of Tithe: Irish: 13[s.] 4[d.]” — Note: “Irish” denotes Irish plantation measure used for determining acreage. Records held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), archival ref. FIN/5/A/189A. Photocopies obtained from the PRONI, Belfast (2014); digital images online at www.nidirect.gov.uk (accessed 2021-06-20).</ref>

: In 1831, Mary Kilpatrick was recorded again as the head of the household in Lislea. The household consisted of three males, and two females, and the family's religious denomination was Presbyterian. <ref>''Ireland 1831 Census''. County of Londonderry, Parish of Kilrea, Barony of Loughinsholin. Extract: “Name of Owner or Occupier: Mary Kilpatrick. Townland: Lislea. No. of House: 55. No. of families: 1. No. of persons in family: 3 males, 2 females. No. of servants: 0. Total: 5. Religion: Presbyterian.” Photocopies obtained for Lislea townland, parish of Kilrea, county Londonderry from the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Belfast (2014); archival ref. MIC5A/8a & 8B. Digital image hosted online by the National Archives of Ireland (Dublin), censusnationalarchives.ie (accessed 2021-06-22).</ref> — Unfortunately, the 1831 census of Ireland was a nominal one, in that only the name of the head of the household was recorded. At that time, however, Mary had four adult, unmarried children: Adam, William, Sarah, and Samuel, accounting for the three males and two females making up the household.

: Mary Kilpatrick née Gordon died sometime before 6th October 1858. <ref name="griffiths">Griffith, Richard. ''General Valuation of Rateable Property in Ireland…Union of Ballymoney, County of Londonderry, Parish of Kilrea (1858-10-06)''. Dublin: Alex. Thom and Sons, for her Majesty's Stationery Office, 1858. Digital images of valuation books and maps online at AskAboutIreland.ie (accessed  2014-06-14).</ref> 

== Research notes ==
* '''Please do not attach this profile to an earlier, supposed parent.'''—The Gordon surname was numerous in the parish of Kilrea, particularly in Lislea townland.. However, while it might be tempting to attach Mary Gordon as the daughter or sister of one of them, there is no genealogical evidence to support this kind of supposition. This conclusion has been drawn after a very careful study, conducted by [[Kilpatrick-1128]] of the available records held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland in Belfast during several research trips between 2001–2018. Church records survive only from 1825; rent rolls are non-existent; and a search for wills and administrations, newspaper articles, rent rolls, bonds, and other legal documents have yielded null results.  
* On Ancestry™, people have connected Mary Gordon who married Adam Kilpatrick to a ''single'' woman of Ballymena, with parents named Rodger Gordon and Jane Trail of Pennsylvania, USA ''without offering documentary evidence''. Therefore, this suggestion must be rejected. — [[Kilpatrick-1128]] (11 June 2025).

:: — ''Please contact the profile manager [[Kilpatrick-1128]] should you discover sound genealogical evidence which might support the addition of a parent or other family member''. (2nd Aug. 2022)
* Estimated year of birth:—based on the –estimated– year of birth of Mary's and Adam's eldest child, Elizabeth. Elizabeth having married Samuel Irwin before 1825‡— and their first child (Mary) born in 1826, <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation.'' Record of Baptism.'' Extract: “No. 69. 1826 Mary daughter of Samuel Irwin of Moyknock and Betty Kilpatrick his wife born 19th April and baptized this 21st day of April 1826.” Extract by Barbara Braswell, 2003-10-22; hosted online by Richard Torrens, “Kilrea First Presbyterian Church Records,” Bann Valley Genealogy genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/ (accessed 2021-06-22).</ref> the estimated year of birth for Elizabeth has been set at 1800. Thus, the estimate for Mary Gordon is strictly an estimate. — ‡ Note:—Records of marriage in Kilrea First Presbyterian survive only from mid-1825. ~[[Kilpatrick-1128]]
* Estimated year of marriage:—has been set at five years before the estimated date of birth for Mary's and Adam's eldest child, Elizabeth.
* Estimated year of death:—occurred before 6th October 1858, the date on which Griffith's Valuation was completed for the parish of Kilrea. Mary Kilpatrick (née Gordon) was not recorded as the head of a household in Lislea townland. <ref name="griffiths" />

: Mary Jane White was born in Fallahogy townland in the parish of Kilrea, county Derry on 11th November 1829. She was the daughter of [[White-77377|William White, jun.]] and [[Kilpatrick-2163|Mary Anne "Annie" Kilpatrick]]. Mary Jane was baptised in Kilrea First Presbyterian Church on 22nd November in the same year. <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation, Kilrea, County Londonderry. ''Solemnization of a Baptism''. Extract: Mary Jane White, born 11th November 1829, daughter of William White of Fallahogey [parish of Kilrea] and Mary Anne [sic] Kilpatrick, his wife; baptised 22nd November 1829 by the Rev. Hugh Walker Rodgers. Transcript by Barbara Braswell from the microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Belfast), archival ref. MIC1P/87; posted to Bann Valley Genealogy, 1 January 2003, online at www.4qd.org/bann/, hosted by Richard Torrens (accessed 2003); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1829.html.</ref>

: Sometime after their mother's death, Mary Jane and her sister, Sarah Ann, went to live in Moboy townland in the parish of Craigs, county Antrim. In 1852, Mary Jane married [[Steele-12616|John Steele]], a weaver from the parish of Rasharkin, in the Second Presbyterian Church at Ahoghill. <ref>General Register Office, Ireland.'' Civil Registration of a Marriage''. Extract: Marriage solemnized on 22nd January 1852 at Ahoghill in the parish of Ahoghill [Craigs], county Antrim. John Steele (signed with his mark), full age, bachelor, occupation: weaver; residence: Drumack [parish of Rasharkin, county Antrim]; father: Robert Steele, farmer. Mary Jane White (signed with her mark), full age, spinster; residence: Mayboy [Moboy, parish of Ahoghill], county Antrim; father: William White, farmer. Marriage solemnized in 2nd Presbyterian Church, Ahoghill, according to the form and discipline of the Presbyterian Church by licence by G. Buick [or Quick]; witnesses: F[—] Hay, Samuel Caulfield. Archival ref. registrar’s district: Ballymena, nos. 87, 0513099, 2. Digital image online at Irish Genealogy, hosted by the Department of Culture, Heritage, and the Gaeltacht, www.civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie (extract by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-08-23).</ref>

: Mary Jane's first five children were born in Ireland, probably in county Antrim and possibly in her husband's family home in Drumack townland in the parish of Rasharkin. The remaining five were born in Scotland at Greenock.

: By 1871, Mary jane and John lived in the Back Lands off Mackenzie street in Greenock. John was employed as a labourer in a sugar house. <ref name="census-1871" /> Nine children were born of the marriage to this date, but two—a boy named Campbell, of measles in 1864 and a daughter, Sarah, in 1868—had died as toddlers. <ref>National Records of Scotland. Statutory Registers. D''eaths in the East Parish of Greenock in the County of Renfrew''. Extract: No. 143. Campbell Steele (single), died 28th April 1964 at 8h 3m p.m. at East[?] Hamilton Street, Greenock; male; aged 2-1/2 years; father: John Steele, labourer; mother: Mary Jane Steele M.S. [maiden surname:] White; cause of death: measles, no medical attendance; informant: [father], his mark, John Lowe, registrar, witness; registered 30th April 1864 at Greenock, John Lowe, registrar. Archival ref. Greenock East (Renfrewshire) registration district, 564/2 143, pg. 48. Image online at ScotlandsPeople, hosted by National Records of Scotland, scotlandspeople.gov.uk (purchased by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-08-26).</ref> <ref>National Records of Scotland. Statutory Registers. ''Index of Civil Registrations of Deaths''. Index entry: Sarah Steele, age 3, mother’s maiden name: White, died in 1868, registration district: Greenock West, ref. no. 564/2 151. Index online at ScotlandsPeople, hosted by National Records of Scotland, scotlandspeople.gov.uk (accessed 2022-08-26).</ref>

: During the next ten years, the family fell into reduced circumstances. In 1879, Mary Jane's husband was admitted to the lunatic asylum at Smithston in the parish of Inverkip, Renfrewshire. <ref>''Scottish Indexes''. Index entry: John Steel, patient no. 33289, admission/transfer date: 12th April 1879, institution: Smithston Poorhouse and Asylum, county: Renfrewshirre. Original records: National Records of Scotland references: MC7/4, pg. 338, general register; and MC2/241, admission form. Index compiled by Graham Maxwell, 2014–2021; online at scottishindexes.com/mcrtranscript.aspx?mcrid=433818 (accessed 2022-11-04).</ref> Mary Jane and two of her sons had to take refuge in the Greenock Poorhouse. <ref name="census-1881" />

: Mary Jane's husband, John Steele, died at home, in the Back Lands off McKenzie Street in Greenock in 1886. <ref>National Records of Scotland. Statutory Registers. ''Deaths in the East District of Greenock in the County of Renfrew.'' Extract: No. 87. John Steel, labourer, married to Mary Jane Whyte [sic], died 15th March 1886 at 11h 30min p.m. at Back Lands, McKenzie Street, Greenock; male, aged 46 [sic] years; father: James Steel, labourer (deceased); mother: Mary Steel M.S. [maiden surname] Colquhoun (deceased); cause of death: heart disease as certified by John Macdougall, M.D.; informant: Elizabeth Dinnan (her X mark), daughter, Ja’s M’Cunn, registrar, witness; registered 16th March 1886 at Greenock, Ja’s M’Cunn, registrar. Archival ref. Greenock East (Renfrew) registration district, 564/2 87, pg. 29. Image online at ScotlandsPeople, hosted by National Records of Scotland, scotlandspeople.gov.uk (purchased by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-08-24).</ref>

: During the last several years of her life, Mary Jane lived at no. 6 Ingleston street in Greenock. The 1891 census shows that her sons, Stewart, age 24, and Samuel, age 19, were supporting the household from their employment as carters. <ref name="census-1891" />

: On 2nd February 1896, Mary Jane Steele, née White, died at Greenock in her sixty-seventh year. <ref>National Records of Scotland. Statutory Registers. ''Deaths in the East District of Greenock in the County of Renfrew''. Extract: No. 58. Mary Jane Whyte [sic] Steele, widow of John Steele, labourer; died 2nd February 1896 at 10 hours 15 minutes p.m. at 44, Arthur Street, Greenock; female, aged 60 years; father: William Whyte, farmer (deceased); mother: Annie Whyte M.S. [maiden surname] Kilpatrick (deceased); cause of death: acute bronchitis and general debility, as certified by W. Walker, M.B.; informatn: Grace Steele, daughter-in-law, present; registered 3rd February 1896 at Greenock, W. Johnston, registrar. Archival ref. Greenock East (Renfrew) registration district, 564/1 58, pg. 20. Image online at ScotlandsPeople, hosted by National Records of Scotland, scotlandspeople.gov.uk (purchased by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-08-23).</ref>

On 11th March in the same year, she was baptised in Kilrea First Presbyterian Church. <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation, Kilrea, County Londonderry. Hugh Walker Rodgers. Transcript by Barbara Braswell from the microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Belfast), archival ref. MIC1P/87 (Autumn 2002); posted to Bann Valley Genealogy, 3 February 2003, online at www.4qd.org/bann/, hosted by Richard Torrens (accessed 2003); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1840.html.</ref>

== Research notes ==
* An extensive search has been conducted to trace Ellen White, without success. If Ellen died before 1864 (the year in which civil registrations of deaths commenced in Ireland), then a death notice or gravestone would be the only available sources. However, neither of these kinds of records were found. ~[[Kilpatrick-1128]] (2022-11-04)

== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
: William White was born about 1803, possibly in Fallahogy townland in the parish of Kilrea. <ref name="tithe" /> He was the son of William White and Sarah (Sally) Gibson. <ref name="marriage-first" />

: On 12th March 1828, he married [[Kilpatrick-2163|Mary Anne Kilpatrick]] of Lislea townland, in the parish of Kilrea, in the Presbyterian Church at Kilrea. <ref name="marriage-first">Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation, Kilrea, County Derry. ''Solemnization of a Marriage''. Extract: Martha Kirpatrick [sic], daughter of late Adam Kirpatrick and Mary Gordon, of Lislea and Kilrea, to William White, jun. of Fallahogy [parish of Kilrea], son of William White, sen. and Serah [sic] Gibson. Marriage solemnized by the Rev. Hugh walker Rodgers, 12th March 1828; witnesses: Wilson Gordon, John Kirkfatrick, Jno [John] Snipe. Transcript by Barbara Braswell (2002) from microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, archival ref. MIC1P/87; posted to the Bann Valley Genealogy mailing list 2002-10-12, hosted by Richard Torrens, www.4qd.org/bann/ (accessed Dec. 2002); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Marriages/1828.html.</ref>

: In 1826, William held 6 acres 1 rood 32 perches of land (Irish plantation measure) in Fallahogy townland. <ref name="tithe">Church of Ireland. ''Tithe Applotment Books''. Parish of Kilrea, County Londonderry (1826). Extract for Widow or W’m [William] White in Fallahogy townland. Records held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, archival ref. FIN/5/A/189A (pg. 6), completed 27th February 1826. Digital images online at www.nidirect.gov.uk (extracts by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-11-03).</ref>

: When the 1831 census of Ireland was enumerated (for which some fragments remain for county Derry), William's household comprised one male and two females (assumed to be his wife and daughter, Mary Jane). The family continued to live in Fallahogy townland. <ref>''Ireland 1831 Census''. Household of William Whyte [sic] in Fallyhogay  [Fallyhogy townland], parish of Kilrea, barony of Loughinsholin, county Londonderry (house no. 12, pg. 5). Digital image hosted online by the National Archives of Ireland (Dublin), censusnationalarchives.ie (accessed 2021-06-29).</ref>

: Three children were born of William's marriage to Mary Anne:
* [[White-77389|Mary Jane]], born in Fallahogy townland in the parish of Kilrea on 11th November 1829; <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation, Kilrea, County Londonderry. ''Solemnization of a Baptism''. Extract: Mary Jane White, born 11th November 1829, daughter of William White of Fallahogey [parish of Kilrea] and Mary Anne [sic] Kilpatrick, his wife; baptised 22nd November 1829 by the Rev. Hugh Walker Rodgers. Transcript by Barbara Braswell from the microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Belfast), archival ref. MIC1P/87; posted to Bann Valley Genealogy, 1 January 2003, online at www.4qd.org/bann/, hosted by Richard Torrens (accessed 2003); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1829.html.</ref>
* Sarah Ann, born in Fallahogy townland, and baptised 19th February 1832; <ref>Church of Ireland. Parish of Kilrea, County Londonderry. ''Records of baptisms 1829–1861, marriages 1829–1848, and burials 1828–1862''. Extract of record of baptism: “1832 02 Feb.; Sarah Ann; Wm & Mary A. White; Tallynoy? [Fallahogy?]” (pg 4.) Transcribed by Zara K. Mettam from photostat copies held at the Public Record Office, Belfast, 1967. Digital images online at FamilySearch Int’l., familysearch.org; archival ref. FHL film no. 908817, item 3 (accessed 2021-06-29).</ref> and,
* [[White-77388|Ellen]], born in Drumsaragh townland in the parish of Tamlaght O'Crilly, on 27th February 1840. <ref>Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Kilrea First Congregation, Kilrea, County Londonderry. ''Solemnization of a Baptism''. Extract: Ellen White born 27th February 1840, daughter of William White of Fallahogey [parish of Kilrea] and Marianne [sic] Kilpatrick of Dromsara [Drumsaragh, parish of Tamlaght O’Crilly]; baptised 11th March 1840 by the Rev. Hugh Walker Rodgers. Transcript by Barbara Braswell from the microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Belfast), archival ref. MIC1P/87 (Autumn 2002); posted to Bann Valley Genealogy, 3 February 2003, online at www.4qd.org/bann/, hosted by Richard Torrens (accessed 2003); archived online at genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Baptisms/1840.html.</ref>

: William's wife, Mary Anne, died sometime before 1846. On 7th December 1846, he remarried to Marianne McCord, daughter of James of Timaconway townland in the parish of Tamlaght O'Crilly. The marriage was solemnized in Kilrea First Meeting House (Presbyterian church). <ref>General Register Office, Ireland. ''Civil Registration of a Marriage''. Extract: William White, full age, widower, occupation: cottier; residence: Moneydig, parish of Doghill [Desertoghill], county L:Derry; son of William White, farmer. Marianne McCord, full age, spinster; resident of Timmaconway, parish of T: OCrilly [Tamlaght O’Crilly]; daughter of James McCord, farmer. Marriage solemnized on 7th December 1846 at 1st Kilrea Meeting House in the parish of Kilrea, county Londonderry, according to the form and discipline of the Presbyterian Church, by licence, by the Rev. Hu W Rodgers, minister; witnesses: Rich’d M. Henderson, James (his mark) McCord. Archival ref. registrar’s district: Ballymoney, no. 16/05367893/211. Digital image online at Irish Genealogy, hosted by the Department of Culture, Heritage, and the Gaeltacht, civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie (transcribed by Alison Kilpatrick, 2021-06-11).</ref>

: One child was born of this second marriage: Hugh, in Killygullib Glebe, parish of Tamlaght O'Crilly, on 20th February 1860. <ref name="baptism-hugh">Presbyterian Church of Ireland. Churchtown Congregation, parish of Tamlaght O’Crilly, County Derry. ''Solemnization of a Baptism''. Transcript: “No. 349; 1860 Mar 2; Hugh White, age 10 days; father: Wm White; mother: Mary Ann McCord; residence: [Killygullib] Glebe.” (pg 22.) Transcript by William Scott from the microfilm copy held by the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Belfast), ref. PRONI MIC 1P/347A/1; online at “Churchtown Church Baptisms,” hosted by Richard Torrens online at Bann Valley Genealogy, genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/TamlaghtP/Baptisms.html (accessed 2021-06-11).</ref>

: William rented a house without land in Killygullib, from Thomas McKay. <ref>Griffith, Richard. ''General Valuation of Rateable Property in Ireland''. County of Londonderry, Union of Ballymoney (part of). Extract re: house of William White, held from Thomas M’Kay, in Killygullibe Glebe, parish of Tamlaght O’Crilly; OS ref. 48d Dublin: Alex. Thom and Sons, for her Majesty's Stationery Office, 9th October 1858. Digital images of table and map online at AskAboutIreland.ie (extract by Alison Kilpatrick, 2022-11-03).</ref> The house lay on a road, since removed, a few hundred feet southwest of the Harvey Hill Post Office. Rental of a house without land confirms William's employment status as a cottier. ''(See links, below.)'' 

: William White appears to have died sometime between 1860 and 1864. ''(See research note.)''

== Research notes ==
* Estimated year of birth:—assumes an age of about twenty-five years when he married in 1828. <ref name="marriage-first" />
* Estimated date of death—No mention was made of William having died in the baptismal record for his son, Hugh, in 1860; <ref name="baptism-hugh" /> a registration of the death was not found in the civil records from 1864''ff''; and William's name was not found in the Valuation Revision Book for Killygullib Glebe during the period 1867–1884. — [[Kilpatrick-1128) (2022-11-03)
